stories.Headline: Gan Kim Yong unveils three national AI missions for finance at Singapore FinTech Festival
stories.Summary:
Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong announced three national artificial intelligence missions on 18 November at the Singapore FinTech Festival. These missions aim to strengthen financial crime prevention, improve access to financing, and enable AI-driven transactions. The government will bring together researchers, public agencies, technology companies, and financial institutions to develop these solutions. This initiative follows the establishment of the National AI Council, which is chaired by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong. The government intends to test promising solutions against global standards before moving toward wider deployment.

The first mission involves a trial with five banks that securely combine transaction data to identify suspicious patterns. The Monetary Authority of Singapore will start a design study in early 2027 for an industry-wide scam detection system. The second mission uses synthetic data to help AI companies create financing solutions for startups and small and medium-sized enterprises. The third mission tests AI agents in controlled environments to handle automatic payments and purchases for individuals and businesses. These trials will examine accountability, authorization, identity verification, and compatibility between different systems to ensure safe agentic transactions.

Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong stated that the government will build shared capabilities to achieve more than any single institution. He explained that scams are not confined to one bank because stolen funds can pass through several institutions within minutes. Gan noted that traditional lending approaches may not fully capture the future potential of newer startups with limited assets. He emphasized that AI agents must operate within defined limits and that businesses remain accountable for transactions made on their behalf. Gan also warned that Singapore will act against any companies that flout laws to bypass foreign regulations.

Small and medium-sized enterprises and startups with limited financial records are affected because traditional lenders rely on past performance and collateral. These businesses will be consulted to assess if the new AI solutions actually address their specific financing needs. The government is also working with companies affected by new US Department of Commerce rules regarding advanced semiconductor export licenses. These rules require licenses to export, re-export, or provide remote access to semiconductors for five countries, including Singapore. Authorities are currently engaging US officials to facilitate access and assessing the business impact of these restrictions.

The government first announced these AI missions during Budget 2026 to drive transformation in key sectors like financial services. The National AI Council was created to lead this effort and coordinate the adoption of artificial intelligence across the republic. The Monetary Authority of Singapore and the industry have already worked together to broaden AI adoption and deepen technical capabilities. The Future of Finance Institute will support the missions by coordinating partnerships and developing standards for the financial sector. These efforts occur as the government seeks to strengthen the responsible use of AI within the national economy.

The government will continue testing AI agents to see if they can make contractual payments after verified terms are fulfilled. The design study for the scam detection utility will initially focus on accounts and data located within Singapore. The Future of Finance Institute will continue testing solutions to determine if they are ready for wider sector use. The articles leave open whether the scam detection system will eventually expand to include cross-border cooperation with other nations. It remains unclear how the US chip restrictions will ultimately impact the computing capacity needed for these AI ambitions.

stories.Headline: South Korean stocks fall for a fourth day as AI concerns deepen
stories.Summary:
South Korean stocks sank for the fourth consecutive session on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, as lingering concerns over artificial intelligence dampened investor sentiment. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index lost 132.02 points, or 2.59 percent, to close at 4,968.48. The index fell below the 5,000-point mark to its lowest level in nine months. The Korean won weakened against the U.S. dollar. Trade volume was light at 183.09 million shares worth 14.19 trillion won, or $10.61 billion.

Decliners far outnumbered advancers 709 to 182. Foreigners sold a net 1.44 trillion won, while institutions and individuals bought a net 543.56 billion won and 421.79 billion won, respectively. Top market cap Samsung Electronics decreased 3.3 percent to 190,300 won, and chip giant SK hynix shed 1.96 percent to 1.1 million won. SK Square, the parent of SK hynix, retreated 1.31 percent to 679,000 won. Power equipment manufacturer Samsung Electro-Mechanics sank 3.95 percent to 754,000 won.

The Korean won was trading at 1,338.2 won against the U.S. dollar as of 3:30 p.m., down 1.7 won from the previous session's close. Bond prices, which move inversely to yields, closed higher. The yield on three-year Treasurys shed 1.8 basis points to 3.725, and the return on the benchmark five-year government bonds fell 0.5 basis point to 3.825. Kang Jin-hyuk, an analyst at Shinhan Securities, said the market came under pressure from continued fallout surrounding Nvidia. He also cited U.S. restrictions on remote access to Nvidia's AI chips and concerns over the sustainability of AI demand, which dampened investors' risk appetite.

On Wall Street, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped about 2.5 percent Monday, while AI chip giant Nvidia shares slid 4.1 percent. The Nvidia decline came amid continued uncertainty following the departure of its CEO, Jensen Huang, last week. Nvidia is scheduled to report its earnings Tuesday, with investors closely watching its outlook for AI chip demand and infrastructure spending. Investors are also keeping an eye on AI giant Anthropic's planned Nasdaq debut Thursday. The AI sector is also facing increased regulatory scrutiny after the U.S. government issued new rules Monday restricting remote access to advanced U.S. computing chips and servers.

An electronic board showing the Korea Composite Stock Price Index stood at a dealing room of the Hana Bank headquarters in Seoul on Tuesday. An employee stood before an electronic display board in Hana Bank's headquarters in central Seoul on Nov. 17. Financial data was shown on a screen in the dealing room of Hana Bank in Seoul after the market closed on Nov. 17, 2026. The Korea Herald published its report on Nov. 17, 2026, at 15:51:26. The Korea JoongAng Daily published its report on November 17, 2026, at 5:00 p.m.

Nvidia is scheduled to report its earnings Tuesday, and Anthropic's planned Nasdaq debut is set for Thursday. Investors are closely watching Nvidia's outlook for AI chip demand and infrastructure spending. The U.S. government issued new rules Monday restricting remote access to advanced U.S. computing chips and servers. The articles leave open what Nvidia's earnings will show and how Anthropic's debut will fare. The articles also leave open how the new U.S. rules will affect the AI sector.

stories.Headline: Baidu CEO Robin Li urges companies to monetize AI and overhaul organizational structures to avoid a bubble
stories.Summary:
Baidu CEO Robin Li spoke about the urgent need for artificial intelligence adoption during the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen on November 17, 2026. He explained that the actual spread of AI applications is moving more slowly than people expected despite the intense competition in the technology sector. Li argued that companies must prioritize the monetization of these tools to prevent the risk of a market bubble. He believes that the industry cannot sustain its current growth without finding clear ways to generate revenue.

The process of reaping the benefits of AI requires a complete overhaul of traditional organizational structures within a company. Robin Li stated that he has made radical attempts to break down the boundaries of traditional jobs at Baidu to better integrate these new technologies. This shift involves reorganizing how teams operate to ensure that AI is not just a tool but a core part of the business model. Such changes are necessary to keep pace with the rapid evolution of the global tech map.

As the leader of Baidu, Robin Li is responsible for guiding his company through this transition while advising other executives on the necessity of structural change. He suggested that the current way of organizing work is an obstacle to the full potential of artificial intelligence. By removing rigid job descriptions, he believes companies can become more agile and responsive to technological breakthroughs. He emphasized that those who fail to reorganize their internal systems will likely struggle to compete in the future.

stories.Headline: Maxine Dexter introduces bill to ban AI data centers on federal public lands
stories.Summary:
On November 11, 2026, Oregon Representative Maxine Dexter introduced a bill to ban AI data centers on federal public lands. This legislation aims to stop the construction of these facilities on national forests and lands managed by the Interior Department. Meanwhile, New Jersey introduced Assembly Bill A5607 on October 5, 2026, to regulate AI chatbots as consumer products. Both measures respond to the rapid growth of artificial intelligence and its impact on environment and consumer safety. These separate legislative efforts seek to increase oversight of technology companies operating within the United States.

The Protecting Our Public Lands from Data Centers Act requires sold federal land to return to government ownership if used for data centers. New Jersey's A5607 would limit chat log retention to two years and restrict their use for advertising, training, and profiling. This New Jersey bill also imposes civil penalties of 5,000 dollars per violation and allows users to sue for damages. Another New Jersey bill, A5090, introduced in May 2026, proposes civil penalties of 20,000 dollars for failing to prevent harmful conduct. These laws target various entities, including the Bureau of Land Management, OpenAI's ChatGPT, and Anthropic's Claude.

Representative Maxine Dexter stated that public lands belong in public hands and Oregonians must have a say in their management. She argued that her bill keeps treasured lands safe for future generations who hunt, fish, hike, and graze livestock. In New Jersey, sponsors Cody Miller, Marisa Sweeney, Joe Danielsen, and Anthony Angelozzi aim to hold chatbot providers more liable. EPIC counsel Kara Williams testified that the bill would limit the ability of providers to exploit the personal data of users. The Consumer Federation of America said this approach provides meaningful protections for users of tech products with little transparency.

Randi Spivak of the Center for Biological Diversity called data centers water-guzzling facilities that turn wildlife lands into corporate industrial sites. Former BLM leader Tracy Stone-Manning claimed the government wants to sell public lands to oil, gas, and data center companies. A Pew Research report found 54 percent of Americans believe data centers are bad for the environment as of September. In New Jersey, a 2025 Rutgers University study found 59 percent of residents favor strict AI regulation due to risks. EPIC warned that unregulated chatbots cause devastating harms, including suicide, financial scams, and mental health issues like AI psychosis.

The Trump Administration sought to build data centers on public lands throughout 2026, with the BLM reviewing 15 data center applications. The Interior Department's strategic plan for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 proposes selling federal land to states, tribes, and local governments. In July, the BLM approved an 86-acre AI data center near Lake Mead National Recreation Area, though it was paused. Meta operates a 2.4-million-square-foot data center in Eagle Mountain, Utah, while 14 proposed centers sit within ten miles of national parks. New Jersey's A5607 is based on a model bill developed by EPIC, Fairplay, and the Consumer Federation of America.

Dexter's bill is now with the House Natural Resources and Agriculture committees, but it currently has no Republican cosponsors. New Jersey's A5607 was referred to the Assembly Appropriations Committee on October 19 after a 5-1-1 vote in another committee. If passed by both chambers, Governor Mikie Sherrill must sign or veto the New Jersey legislation to make it law. The articles leave open whether the House will pass the federal ban or if the New Jersey bill will be amended. It remains unclear if other states will follow New Jersey's lead in treating AI chatbots as consumer products.

stories.Headline: Google raises Gemini chat retention to about two months even with history off
stories.Summary:
Google updated the Gemini privacy policy on Monday, November 17, 2026, raising the conversation retention period from 72 hours to around two months, as reported by Gizmodo, IBTimes and TechCrunch. The change was made by Google for its flagship AI tool Gemini, according to Gizmodo. Gizmodo reporter AJ Dellinger published his story on November 17, 2026 at 5:00 pm ET. The updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub page carried a notice that future chats will still be saved for around 2 months even if Gemini History is turned off. An archived version of the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub had a last update date of October 13, 2026, according to Gizmodo.

The retention period rises from 72 hours to around two months, and Temporary Chats will also be kept for around two months, according to Google's updated privacy documentation cited by IBTimes. Gemini History defaults to 18 months and can be changed to three months, 36 months or indefinite, and saved chats can be deleted at any time, Gizmodo reported. The Gemini History option in user settings still describes the retention period as 72 hours, Gizmodo said. Google's new settings let users keep their Gemini chat history while opting out of generative AI model training, and the new training controls are off by default, according to IBTimes. Conversations reviewed by human reviewers and associated information can be retained for up to three years even if users later delete their history, and feedback can lead to a conversation, attachments and other relevant information being reviewed and retained for up to three years, IBTimes reported.

Google declined to provide a comment to Gizmodo and instead directed it to a blog post titled "We're updating controls in the Gemini app." In that post Google said it was giving users more control over when Gemini chat history is used to train generative AI models. Google said the longer retention period was intended to strengthen safety and security protections as AI systems become increasingly capable, according to IBTimes. Google said retained information may be used to respond to requests, process feedback and protect the company, its users and the public. Google's updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub also cites potential system failures as a reason for retaining chats and says temporary conversations are not used to train AI models, TechCrunch reported.

OpenAI claims it holds onto temporary chats for up to 30 days, and Anthropic says conversations with Claude are held for 30 days by default, with both noting they may hold certain chat logs longer if necessary, according to Gizmodo. TechCrunch said OpenAI may keep temporary ChatGPT chats for up to 30 days and Anthropic retains incognito Claude chats for 30 days by default, though companies may keep some data longer for legal or safety reasons or to investigate policy violations. The Register reported Tuesday that archived versions of Google's privacy documentation confirmed the earlier three-day limit, IBTimes said. Under the updated policy, conversations may remain associated with a user's Google Account during the temporary retention period even though they do not appear in the user's visible Gemini History, according to IBTimes. Google says conversations sent to service providers for review are disconnected from users' accounts, IBTimes reported.

Until now, chat history and AI training were tied to a single "Keep Activity" setting, TechCrunch reported. Previously, retaining Gemini conversation history was more closely tied to allowing Google to use those interactions to improve its AI systems, according to IBTimes. Google's documentation states that future chat content will not be used to train generative AI models when the training setting is disabled, except in certain circumstances including when users voluntarily submit feedback, IBTimes said. Temporary Chats are also excluded from generative AI model training, although Google still retains them temporarily for operational and safety purposes, according to IBTimes. Google warns that deleting Gemini history does not necessarily remove information saved through connected Google services, which may follow their own privacy and retention policies, and advises users not to enter confidential information they would not want a reviewer to see, IBTimes reported.

The updates will begin rolling out globally over the coming weeks, according to IBTimes. Google did not answer TechCrunch's questions about what prompted the change and whether it would affect how conversations are accessed or reviewed. Gizmodo said the Gemini History option in user settings will presumably update when the change goes into effect. Users who want to review their choices can open Gemini, go to Settings and select History, and can also manage retention preferences through Gemini History, according to IBTimes. Individual users may see different options while the global rollout is underway, and for users who leave chat history enabled the default automatic deletion period remains 18 months, IBTimes reported.

stories.Headline: Marian Kamenistak builds a 123-automation AI executive assistant that saves an estimated 361 hours a month
stories.Summary:
Marian Kamenistak, VP of Engineering at Mews, published on hackernoon.com on 18 November 2026 an account of the AI executive assistant he built. He made an inventory of his automations on 25 October 2026 and found one job that had reported success for 48 days while its access key was being rejected. Another job sent LinkedIn messages on a Sunday because its schedule was off by one day, and a group of other jobs succeeded about 60% of the time and never alerted him. In late October 2026 he saw about 70% of his jobs failing on a dashboard he had built that weekend. He dropped meetings that were not critical and started fixing things, and found the root cause was that most jobs ran from his local PC, which was not plugged in.

The assistant is 123 scheduled automations, a set of AI skills and one dashboard he calls the Control Room, with 1,506 steps and 948 connections between them as captured on 15 November 2026. It saves an estimated 361 hours of work a month, about 4,330 hours a year, equal to 2.3 extra people at 160 hours a person a month. People cost avoided is €14,428 a month and €173,141 a year, or 352,415 and 4,228,980 Czech crowns, while the cost of running the automations is €464 a month and €5,569 a year, or 11,335 and 136,020 crowns, leaving €13,964 a month and €167,573 a year saved after costs. Euros are converted at the Czech National Bank fixing of 13 November 2026, 24.425 CZK per EUR, and 176 of the 361 hours are work he would otherwise have hired for, an SDR or a virtual assistant, about 1.1 people. With the tools he would pay for anyway the bill is about €811 a month, every subscription he pays is about €1,204, and none of the three totals includes his build time, which was one weekend for the dashboard and another 3 weeks to a month for the full monthly cycle.

He kept his personal human EA, Lucie, and calls it the best decision he could do, because she keeps him accountable and resolves everything on the spot. He says she was very persistent about making sure he invested his time into the right decisions and urges him to pay attention to non-business things, which go into relationships with his teammates. In invoicing the AI reads the bank lines and matches each one to a document, and Lucie finds the documents the AI can't, in Drive first, then Gmail, then the supplier portals. From July to October 2026, 79 of 248 bank lines were waiting for a document. He says the AI does the recurring work and Lucie does the part where somebody has to go and find the thing and decide on the spot.

ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini all answer "hybrid" when asked whether to replace an executive assistant with AI, and he agrees with hybrid and pays for it every month. Perplexity, asked on 15 November 2026, put an assistant stack at $20 to $200 a month and its upkeep at 2 to 8 hours a month, and ChatGPT leaned on vendor price pages such as Lindy's and cited a Forrester study commissioned by Microsoft for Copilot Studio where one customer says an agent saved 4 hours per user a month. He says those numbers are fair for one tool on one desk, while his bill is for a whole back office. The assistant serves five business streams: the Engineering Leaders Community, the ELC Conference, the Academy, hiring through Marian's List, and his mentoring at marian.coach. Tereza is Head of Community, and they have two recurring meetings, weekly preparation for the next week and checking the Control Room on the web, and monthly review of past KPIs and setting KPIs for the next month.

He spent 20+ years in software development and was VP of Engineering at Mews, where engineering grew from 8 to 80 teams, which is why he could build it himself. The plumbing needed an engineer, but writing down his niche, his ideal customer and his KPIs didn't, and that is the part that made the AI useful. The automations ran before the AI knew what business it was working for, and the fix was setting the niche, ICP and KPIs so the AI knows the context. Every stream must have a niche and a mission, one sentence each, max 160 characters, and concrete as to who, what and which geography, and his mentoring niche starts with one-to-one leadership mentoring for engineering and product leaders in Czechia and Central Europe. The ICP has 1 to 4 segments with consumers and companies kept separate, each saying who they are, what they buy and where that comes from, and one thing the company segment of his mentoring stream buys is a Mentor in Residence.

A watchdog now runs every hour in the cloud, off the Mac, and expects a heartbeat from each job, so a job silent past its schedule counts as failed and an unplugged computer can't hide. The AI may not fix outreach senders, finance and logins on its own, because a wrong fix on a sender goes out to real people, and there is a limit of at most 5 fixes a day and 1 per job per 7 days. A test on 15 November went from approved to fixed in 2 minutes, and he refurbished his 7-year-old MacBook Pro to run the local jobs. On 15 November 2026 the coverage page showed 140 jobs OK, 4 failing and 30 stale, the home page read "4 of 5 goals on track" with 1 goal behind, qualified mentoring leads, and 9 things wait for a person and 136 of 167 automations working. The 123 in the post is the count in the savings model of 14 November 2026, each page counts a different set of jobs and the set changes daily, and the system refuses to publish a stream missing its niche, ICP or KPIs, showing a target without a source as unsourced.

stories.Headline: Chinese entities use output from US AI models to train domestic rivals amid chip curbs
stories.Summary:
Chinese entities are using output from leading American artificial intelligence models to train domestic rivals. This practice has expanded into mainstream industrial use to offset tightening US chip curbs. A Reuters review of over 300 documents revealed this trend in late 2026. Beijing is encouraging this method to make AI easier to deploy in manufacturing. Washington announced further restrictions on chips from companies like Nvidia on November 16.

Distillation involves a teacher model generating answers to train a smaller student system. In November 2024, Shanghai Jiao Tong University used 5,000 OpenAI o1 answers for Alibaba's Qwen2.5-72B. Alibaba researchers used GPT-4 and GPT-4o for non-Chinese training material in April 2025. In February 2026, Meituan and Shanghai Jiao Tong University used GPT-4o for programming tasks. These efforts occur amid a November 18 to 19 APEC summit in Shenzhen.

US Commerce Department officials raised intellectual property theft concerns in Chengdu in July. They believe industrial distillation is why Chinese models narrowed the gap with American rivals. Chinese officials defended the technique as standard and said they would act against theft. The US Commerce Department and China's Cyberspace Administration did not respond to comments. A former Alibaba engineer said distillation makes one expensive query do repeated work.

OpenAI and Anthropic terms restrict using their output to develop competing AI models. Some sources argue that engineering, algorithms, and data also helped Chinese AI progress. Researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University warned that distillation could stifle original innovation. Chinese AI developers have asked the industry regulator for guidance on legal boundaries. These developers are affected by constraints on computing power and US chip curbs.

Eight Chinese agencies published a national AI+Manufacturing policy package in January. This guidance supports model training, fine-tuning, and distillation for various industrial applications. Cities including Shanghai and Shenzhen have encouraged techniques that reduce computing requirements. US authorities publicly accused Chinese companies of aggressive industrial distillation in September. Beijing aims to deploy smaller, cheaper AI systems across the second-largest global economy.

President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are expected to meet during the APEC summit. The US continues to restrict Chinese access to advanced chips from Nvidia. Chinese developers seek clarity on the line between ordinary use and organized collection. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology did not respond to comment requests. It remains unclear if China will make concrete commitments to stop IP theft.

stories.Headline: Alibaba Cloud expands global data center network to meet AI demand
stories.Summary:
Alibaba Cloud plans to expand its global data center network over the next year to meet growing AI computing power demand. This expansion was outlined by Yuan Zhiming during the company's Hong Kong summit held on Tuesday, November 18, 2026. Meanwhile, Amazon withdrew plans for four data center buildings on its Ashburn campus following an agreement reached on October 20. Loudoun County supervisors will vote on November 17 to pause new legislative data center applications for up to twelve months. These separate corporate moves reflect the intense global competition and local regulatory challenges surrounding the rapid growth of AI infrastructure.

The Alibaba expansion prioritizes Hong Kong because its three leased data centers there can no longer meet the current market demand. Amazon's withdrawn Ashburn project involved over 800,000 square feet on a 122-acre campus purchased for around 427.3 million dollars. Under Project Potomac Promise, Amazon will convey 25 acres to the county and seek to rezone the rest for housing. Loudoun County hosts about 233 data center buildings, which generated 1.2 billion dollars in tax revenue for fiscal 2026. This revenue accounted for 39 percent of the budget, with fiscal 2027 projections estimating 1.3 billion dollars or 40 percent.

Yuan Zhiming, the vice president of international business, stated that financial firms are adopting AI into their core business workflows. Amazon's Josh Weissman said the company took pointed community concerns seriously and chose a shared vision over costly litigation. Board Chair Phyllis Randall noted that the Ashburn campus was the wrong location due to resident opposition and needed infrastructure. AWS CEO Matt Garman cautioned that over 100 data center moratoriums are currently being considered across the United States. Amazon CEO Andy Jassy stated that capacity constraints continue to yield unserved demand despite adding 3.9 gigawatts of power.

Residents and Loudoun County supervisors opposed the Ashburn development, leading Amazon to abandon the Bridgefield Tech Center site plan. Governor Abigail Spanberger believes the decision to approve or block data center projects should rest with the community, not the state. State Senator Russet Perry has drafted a three-year statewide moratorium on data center approvals to address these growing local concerns. Dominion Energy requires new data centers to post 1.5 million dollars per megawatt in collateral to protect residential customers. Oracle is also affected, having issued a force majeure notice regarding its 2.45 gigawatt Project Jupiter in New Mexico.

Loudoun County previously used a 2000 zoning ruling that allowed data centers to be built by right as office buildings. Since March 2025, new data centers have required a special exception approved by a board vote rather than administrative processes. Amazon purchased the Ashburn campus in March 2026 and filed its site plan for the tech center in July. AWS reported 46 billion dollars in third quarter sales and a backlog totaling 578 billion dollars in the same period. Amazon's leases not yet commenced rose to 164.9 billion dollars in the third quarter, up from 137.2 billion dollars.

Amazon plans to spend meaningfully more in 2027 than the roughly 220 billion dollars it has planned for 2026. AWS and Nvidia plan to deploy over 2 million more GPUs on AWS during 2027 and 2028 to increase capacity. The county's final vote on November 17 will determine if new rezoning requests are delayed for up to one year. It remains open whether the 17 grandfathered applications totaling 11 million square feet will proceed without any further legislative delays. The articles leave open the final outcome of the air-permit decision regarding Oracle's Project Jupiter in Doña Ana County.

stories.Headline: Google threat group says attackers now use AI agents to automate finding and exploiting software flaws
stories.Summary:
Google Threat Intelligence Group reported on November 17, 2026 that threat actors are using AI-powered agentic workflows to automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation, which accelerates attacks to machine speed and reduces the time defenders have to patch systems. The group observed financially motivated and state-sponsored groups adopting these tools at large scale after earlier experimental use. GTIG highlighted the use of CAIRN, an open-source multi-agent penetration-testing framework, in an attack against the U.S. aerospace sector. Suspected North Korean hackers also used Claude Code to deliver malware, according to the report. Researchers estimate that unsophisticated, fully autonomous attacks requiring little human interaction will emerge within the next three months, while sophisticated fully autonomous agentic attacks are likely within six months.

The FBI warned last week that multiple threat actors have weaponized the ARTEX AI pentesting framework since August, with attacks targeting organizations in financial, government, technology, defense, and healthcare sectors. Google states that attackers systematically abuse open-source pentesting suites including ARTEX, CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI, and HexStrike AI, which facilitate adaptive attacks against internet-exposed endpoints vulnerable to low-complexity flaws that large language models can easily exploit. GTIG's AI Threat Tracker report cites a multi-agent system called exploit_agent that fully automated vulnerability finding and exploitation against French media, entertainment, and education websites. GTIG identified an exposed staging server hosting the framework, which integrates with multiple frontier and local LLMs, analyzes software updates on popular web apps to find flaws, and automatically attempts to exploit them. The deployment of such frameworks dramatically decreases patch time and produces false leads, as seen with PHP2Shell, where hundreds of purported AI-generated proof-of-concept exploits appeared quickly and added a significant burden on defenders who must verify code and develop protections.

Beyond automated attacks, Google also observed UNC6836 using modified Claude Code to deliver the SOMBERMEME backdoor against cryptocurrency firms. AI is also routinely used in influence operations by state-backed groups, commercial vendors, and political networks. LLMjacking has become widespread, with attackers exploiting this new revenue stream at significant cost to affected organizations. The New York Post reported that Russian AI bots pulled off the first fully automated cyber attack and that Google caught them.

stories.Headline: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw says AI can cut drug development from five to seven years to one or two
stories.Summary:
Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, Executive Chairperson of Biocon Ltd, said on Tuesday that Artificial Intelligence has the potential to drastically cut the time required to take a drug molecule from the lab to patients. She spoke on the role of AI in life sciences on the first day of the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026. She said the current timeline of five to seven years to get a molecule from lab all the way to patients could be compressed into a year or two. She called that compression the most fascinating outcome and impact. The summit is a three-day event that started on Tuesday, with global leaders, innovators, founders, entrepreneurs, investors and thinkers from different industries participating.

Shaw said drug development does not end in the labs and has to be validated in clinical trials, including picking the right patients and conducting trials in a way that gives early readouts. She said AI will be used for this in the future. She said the opportunity is not about making incremental change but about reimagining how discovery, development and drug innovation are done. She said that is the real opportunity AI gives and should not be lost. She said autonomous wet labs are already conducting high-throughput screening and real-time analytics using AI.

Shaw said science and biology are currently done one target at a time, which is not going to move the needle. She said that when you understand where a target functions and how it functions using AI, you will be able to develop next generation drugs, next generation diagnostics and next generation technologies. She stressed that regulations must keep pace with accelerated discovery and development. She said Karnataka can take a lead in this space and noted that discussions are underway on how to create a regulatory sandbox to validate proof of concepts much faster. She described biology as the most important frontier for AI to be deployed.

Shaw said AI will help simplify complex biological systems and allow scientists to connect the dots rather than studying one target at a time. She said converging genomics, chemical pathways and neural networks through AI will enable next-generation drugs and next-generation diagnostics, such as detecting the first cancer cell to overcome late-stage diagnosis, as well as advancements in agriculture and bioenergy. She said accelerating the journey from lab to clinic will unlock major opportunities in precision and personalised medicine. She said AI is about accelerating intelligence and is the greatest assistant, embedded in daily life and business, helping people prioritise tasks, improve efficiency and get back time. The Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 runs for three days.

stories.Headline: OpenAI funds $255,000 Effingham schools grant program as residents sue over data center secrecy
stories.Summary:
Three Effingham County residents sued OpenAI, local officials and others in November, alleging that plans for Project Camellia were kept secret until key decisions had been made, and the allegations have not been proven in court. OpenAI is the artificial intelligence company behind the ChatGPT platform. Project Camellia is OpenAI’s proposed $20 billion artificial intelligence data center campus at the Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub near Rincon. The proposal has drawn opposition from residents who raised concerns about transparency, electricity demand, water use, traffic and noise. County commissioners postponed a decision on the project’s preliminary site plan on Nov. 3 and were expected to revisit it Tuesday.

The District Innovation Challenge provides up to $15,000 for each of the Effingham County School District’s 17 schools, backed by $255,000 from OpenAI. Students and educators will work together on proposals that could address technology, STEM, artificial intelligence literacy, sustainability or other school and community needs. Following Tuesday’s districtwide kickoff, students and staff will develop project ideas, itemized budgets and presentations, and the district’s curriculum and technology departments will host presentations and question-and-answer sessions. In January, each school will review proposals and select a group of projects totaling up to $15,000 to represent it at the district level. Finalist student teams will present their ideas to a district panel in February.

Superintendent Yancy Ford said public education thrives when students are given real ownership over their learning and the resources to bring bold ideas to life. Ford said that through this partnership with OpenAI, students are not just learning about the future but are actively designing it for their classrooms, their schools and the Effingham County community. The panel will include Ford, school board representatives, district curriculum and technology leaders, and representatives from the data center and AI industries. Rather than serving as a high-stakes elimination contest, the panel will offer feedback and formally award funding to participating projects, the district said. OpenAI said it would continue working with county officials to address outstanding questions.

Supporters point to potential tax revenue and opportunities for local businesses from Project Camellia. OpenAI has pledged at least $80 million for community priorities tied to Project Camellia. The company also provided a $4.8 million grant to cover Effingham County students’ school breakfast and lunch costs for the 2026-27 school year. In October, OpenAI announced a $2 million grant for the first phase of Atlas Park, a planned recreation area at a former sand mine.

Students across Effingham County will have a chance to turn their ideas for improving their schools into reality through the new grant program. The Pike County Board of Commissioners will hold a special meeting on Wednesday, Nov. 18, to discuss and potentially approve a non-binding term sheet from SoftBank Energy and OpenAI for the PORTS-Pike data center project in Piketon. The special meeting will occur at 10:30 a.m. at the Pike County Administration Building, located at 230 Waverly Plaza in Waverly.

The county said the purpose is to consider, discuss and possibly act on the proposed non-binding term sheet, with possible actions including a resolution approving the term sheet and authorizing its execution and any related matters. The notice said the elected county board could also enter into a private executive session to discuss matters related to the data center deal. An agenda with more details has not yet been published for the special AI data center meeting. Japan’s SoftBank and OpenAI want to redevelop the U.S. Department of Energy Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant into a new data center.

The 3,700-acre U.S. government plant previously enriched uranium for nuclear weapons and later for nuclear energy plants, and it operated from 1957 to 2001. The plant property is owned by the U.S. Department of Energy, and adjacent privately owned properties have also been acquired as part of the planned AI data center development. At full buildout, there could be as many as 18 data center buildings at the southeastern Ohio site, and the AI development is projected to create 35,000 construction jobs and 2,500 permanent, operational jobs, according to the companies. AI chipmaker NVIDIA will provide the AI infrastructure at the data center, and the development also entails significant electricity infrastructure investments and upgrades.

stories.Headline: Education ministry assigns smart glasses specialists to CSAT sites and rules out postponing exam
stories.Summary:
The top scorer of the 63rd tax accountant exam turned themself in to police on the 15th, revealing cheating that used a miniature camera and AI, Kyunghyang Shinmun reported on the 16th. Police received the voluntary confession and launched an investigation, the articles state. Anxiety grew among students and parents ahead of the College Scholastic Ability Test on the 19th, the articles state. Reporting by Kyunghyang Shinmun on the 16th said concerns among CSAT examinees and parents grew after the confession. The articles state that cases of exam cheating using artificial intelligence continue.

The CSAT is the 2027 academic year College Scholastic Ability Test, held on the 19th, three days after the 16th, the articles state. The Ministry of Education said on the 16th that technological responses under review, such as signal blocking, face legal and time constraints, and that it is not considering postponing the CSAT. Shin Jin-yong, head of the Admissions Policy Division at the Ministry of Education, spoke at a briefing on the 16th at the Government Sejong Complex on countermeasures against cheating using smart glasses and micro-cameras. The ministry said it will assign at least one specialist for identifying smart glasses to each test site, the articles state. On the 11th, eight days before the 2027 CSAT, training for dedicated smart-glasses task-force personnel was held at the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education in Yongsan-gu, Seoul, where a company representative wore smart glasses and demonstrated solving problems.

Shin said that given the limited time remaining until the CSAT and the need for uniform test administration, the ministry is reviewing the introduction of AI cheating-detection equipment such as thermal imaging cameras with caution. He said that under current law, except for matters directly related to national security, signal blocking, so-called Jamming, is not permitted. He said that even if allowed, it could interfere with communications around the test sites or impede responses to emergencies. He said that a plan to search for smartphones and electronic devices carried by test-takers using metal detectors would require a legal basis and also faces time constraints. Shin said that if all students are treated as potential criminals and body searches are conducted, it becomes difficult to ensure a stable and comfortable testing environment, and he emphasized that the ministry is not considering postponing the CSAT.

B, a 12th-grader in Gyeonggi Province, said they usually wear horn-rimmed glasses and are concerned they might be misunderstood for no reason, so they feel they will not be able to focus fully on the test. C, a parent of a 12th-grader in Seoul's Yangcheon District, said their child has poor eyesight and sometimes wears glasses, and they are considering entering the room without glasses to avoid misunderstanding. Kwon, a 12th-grade student living in Incheon, said the school had advised students to be cautious about wearing horn-rimmed glasses, and that some friends said they did not intend to wear contact lenses instead of glasses because wearing lenses for a long time can worsen dry eye. D, a parent in Gyeonggi Province with an 11th-grade child, said most children will study and prepare diligently, and it would feel unfair if their efforts are not properly evaluated because of the cheating of a few students. C said one person committing a foul can have a butterfly effect that changes the lives and college admissions outcomes of hundreds of thousands, so it must be punished sternly, and D said creating a fair testing environment is the responsibility of the education authorities, not of individual students or individual schools.

Yang, who works at an optical shop in Eunpyeong-gu, Seoul, said that ahead of the CSAT there were a few cases in which students with horn-rimmed glasses switched to metal frames because they did not want to be inspected during the exam. Yang added that now, with the CSAT imminent, it would be hard to get used to new glasses, so getting a new pair may be difficult. Park, a high school teacher in Gyeonggi Province, said that in most cases, when the glasses are actually checked, the likelihood is high that it is not cheating, but it could lead to complaints if mishandled, and that they have no choice but to check cautiously. Kim, a high school teacher in Seoul, said that when asking students to undergo inspection, they worry about complaints and legal liability, and that although the education authorities have selected inspectors for smart glasses, once the exam begins it is not easy to detect them in the test room. Kwon said there are many ways to use AI, and she worries whether measures that take such possibilities into account can be prepared in the time remaining.

The articles state that smart glasses generally have horn-rimmed designs. A view of miniature cameras on sale at a camera shop in Seoul on the 16th accompanied the report, when the Ministry of Education said it is preparing additional measures, noting that for the 2027 CSAT there could be cheating not only using smart glasses but also with miniature cameras. The articles state that the education authorities have prepared measures such as assigning dedicated personnel at each test site to determine whether glasses are smart devices. The articles state that questions have been raised about whether measures focused solely on smart glasses can block the various forms of AI-enabled cheating. The articles state that detection measures still rely on proctors' visual inspections, raising questions about effectiveness.

The articles state that the Ministry of Education is preparing additional measures for the 2027 CSAT. The concentration began in the fall semester, and the ethical dilemmas posed by the technology are a big part of the specialized study, the article said. Ifeoma Ajunwa, one of three Emory Law professors leading the concentration, was named among the Top 50 Legal Innovators in Academia for 2026. The National Law Review and Wickard recently announced that national honor, which recognizes those shaping the future of legal education, according to the article. Emory Law is one of five law schools in Georgia, and the article said it is emerging as one of the top institutions in the country for making sure the next batches of attorneys know how to handle the technology.

The concentration includes formal courses in AI and the law, and Emory Law began the formal specialization in the fall, the article said. Other law schools offer AI-related courses but not a formal specialization, and Georgia State University College of Law is among the schools that have taught the topic, according to the article. Ajunwa said 21 years ago, during her education, there was no component around AI, and she said students would grapple with how to think about the technology. The article cited a survey showing that 65% of the largest law firms have fully implemented generative AI, 82% of lawyers use it, 32% of firms have implemented it across multiple areas, and 11% of firms have no plans to use it. The article also cited figures of 5,700, 202, 150 and 34 in connection with AI use and law firm practices.

stories.Headline: Telus ends partnership with Westbank to build two AI data centres in Vancouver
stories.Summary:
Telus Corp. ended its partnership with Westbank Corp. to build two artificial intelligence data centres in Vancouver. This decision was reported over the weekend before Monday, November 17, 2026. The company decided to pull out of these specific urban projects. Telus will still proceed with plans to expand a data centre in Kamloops. These three sites were originally intended to form a sovereign AI factory cluster.

The plan required a new 10-storey building at 150 West Georgia St. in downtown Vancouver. It also involved redeveloping an existing office building at 111 East 5th Ave. in Mount Pleasant. Telus previously planned to acquire over 60,000 advanced graphics processing units from Nvidia Corp. The company aimed to secure 150 megawatts of electricity for its B.C. data centres by 2032. These facilities were designed to set a new global standard for sustainable AI infrastructure.

Telus has not given a reason for exiting the Vancouver projects but will share its AI strategy later. Westbank confirmed Telus is no longer a partner but will proceed with the projects as planned. Westbank stated it will announce a new partnership in the coming months to create net-positive compute infrastructure. Rob Goehring said the Telus leadership team has been looking at cost-cutting measures and strategic alternatives. Goehring noted that several interconnected factors in the AI ecosystem likely made Telus skittish about proceeding.

Mayor Pete Fry said the new city council is not a fan of AI data centres. He agreed that the city might impose stricter requirements, such as fees and independent environmental reports. A motion proposes that developers commission third-party assessments on noise, heat, water use, and other impacts. These requirements would apply prior to rezoning or permitting for the data centre developers. Mayor Fry clarified that an AI data centre is not a defined land use under city bylaws.

Telus and Westbank first announced the partnership to develop the two Vancouver facilities in May. The Mount Pleasant location had a rezoning application that was paused in July before October elections. Municipal elections took place on October 17, followed by a request for further staff consultation. Quebecor made an unsolicited $31 billion cash and stock offer to buy Telus on Monday morning. This bid represents a 60 per cent premium on the recent price of Telus shares.

Westbank will announce a new partner for the Vancouver projects in the coming months. Telus will share more details regarding its artificial intelligence strategy in the months ahead. The city website announced an additional Q&A period for the Mount Pleasant project in mid-December. The articles leave open who will lead Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang stepped down following a scandal. It remains unclear if the city will officially adopt the proposed bulk data storage public impact requirement.

stories.Headline: US authorities ground flights as Microsoft outage and technical failures spark system stability fears
stories.Summary:
U.S. aviation authorities grounded planes across the country on Friday after a technology upgrade overloaded air traffic control equipment. A Microsoft network issue also disrupted services worldwide on the same day. Officials stated that neither of these incidents showed signs of malicious activity. The disruptions left many travelers stranded and prompted questions about technology reliability. These events occurred amid other chaos involving an AI billionaire and Silicon Valley.

The FAA ground stop lasted over four hours, causing intermittent communications and radar gaps. Microsoft reported its outage followed a network change and an earlier network capacity upgrade. This Microsoft issue is believed to have affected many millions of people worldwide. At San Diego International Airport on Saturday, 11 of 62 flights were canceled and 11 were delayed. Other Friday events included a cruise ship overturning in New Orleans and drones over a British air base.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said air travel was smoother by Saturday and schedules should return to normal by late Sunday. Microsoft stated on Saturday that its services had been fully restored. Both organizations denied that malicious activity caused their respective disruptions. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy pleaded Friday for tens of billions in more funding for air traffic systems. Administration officials explained that the aviation ground stop resulted from overloading antiquated equipment.

Chuck Amasio, 68, from Rahway, New Jersey, said the weird events made him think about wars crippling economies. Maxine Gustafson, a 34-year-old physician assistant from Minneapolis, felt afraid and helpless, wondering if it was a cyberattack. Tori Perkins, 34, from Hawaii, said she does not necessarily believe what the government says. Corbyn Wascher, a 37-year-old teacher, praised American Airlines staff while stuck at Charlotte Douglas International Airport. Caroline Ruiz, traveling to Australia, noted she had been betrayed by technology two days in a row.

Congress approved 12.5 billion dollars for an air traffic control overhaul that began last year. The FAA has replaced thousands of copper wire connections with fiber optic lines and upgraded hundreds of radio systems. The White House has pushed for an additional 30 billion dollars to complete this work. A bomb was also found near an ethanol plant in Illinois on Friday. Reports of an AI billionaire's affair with a suspected Chinese spy had previously caused Silicon Valley uproar.

The articles leave open whether the public will trust official explanations for these various technical failures. Stephen King tweeted that aliens landed to avoid worldwide panic, though this was not an official view. It remains unclear when the full air traffic control overhaul will be completed. The text does not specify the outcome of the suspected Chinese spy allegations. Future funding for the outdated aviation system depends on the requested billions from the White House.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO following a scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as the chief executive officer of Nvidia last week following a scandal involving a romantic affair. He admitted to being unfaithful to his wife in a memo sent to employees on November 8, 2026. The scandal involves an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang, who also worked for a Singapore based customer. This revelation caused Nvidia shares to slide 4.3 percent on November 9, erasing nearly 200 billion US dollars. The company is now facing internal board investigations and scrutiny from the United States government regarding national security.

The board is assembling a committee of independent directors and outside counsel to investigate reports of foreign intelligence targeting. Colette Kress has stepped in as the interim CEO of the Santa Clara, California based chipmaker during this transition. The company previously held a 5 billion dollar stake in Intel and provided a 105 billion dollar OpenAI backstop. JPMorgan strategist Michael Cembalest estimated that the broader financial commitments of the company may have reached 530 billion dollars. Nvidia also participated in a 2023 Series B round and anchored the 2025 IPO for cloud provider CoreWeave.

The Nvidia board stated it has confidence in Huang and no reason to believe that any company secrets were compromised. Jensen Huang said he is deeply sorry for hurting his family and is committed to supporting American national security. President Donald Trump defended Huang on November 8, calling him a fine person who should remain as the CEO. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun called the characterization of Alice Huang as a Chinese agent an unsubstantiated smear against China. The board promised that its inquiry will examine all available information regarding the alleged foreign intelligence effort.

Jim Cramer said the leadership shake up will not derail the AI boom because demand for computing power is strong. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon noted that the scandal brings the stewardship of a very important American company under debate. Futurum Group CEO Daniel Newman stated that there is no known succession plan or clear leader to step up. Investors are worried that the departure of Huang could jeopardize financial support for computing providers known as neoclouds. Google announced a broader array of AI chips on November 9 to capitalize on its role as a challenger.

The company reached a record market capitalization of nearly 5.8 trillion US dollars in October before it slipped below 5 trillion. Megaspeed International, based in Singapore, was accused of smuggling Nvidia chips to China and breaking United States export restrictions. The Justice Department took over an investigation into Megaspeed after a top Nvidia executive reached out to the government. Huang previously argued that closing off the Chinese market would risk turning China into a more powerful independent AI force. He also dismissed the need for AI labs to slow down their work to ensure technology does not threaten humanity.

Nvidia is set to report its earnings on Tuesday night, where interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to present a view. Jim Cramer believes a successful Anthropic IPO later this week could further restore investor confidence in the broader AI trade. House Republicans have requested a briefing with Huang to discuss his dealings with the former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. The articles leave open whether the board investigation will find that national security or company secrets were actually compromised. It remains unclear if the United States Congress will move to further cut AI chip sales to the Chinese market.

stories.Headline: Giga Energy signs $1 billion lease for 60MW Texas AI data center
stories.Summary:
Giga Energy, an AI data center developer based in the United States, announced on November 17, 2026 a $1 billion lease agreement with an undisclosed U.S.-based AI cloud provider for a 60MW GigaBase AI data center in Hunt County, Texas. The company broke ground on the project, called Project Clay, in July and will develop, own and operate the campus for the customer. The roughly 30-acre campus is scheduled to be ready for service in spring 2027 and will provide AI computing capacity for hyperscale and AI cloud customers. The project is designed to meet priorities that Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has called for, including protecting local resources, investing in dedicated infrastructure and ensuring communities benefit from growth.

The development is expected to create about 300 construction jobs during the build phase and 24 permanent full-time positions with estimated annual salaries ranging from $116,000 to $180,000. It is also expected to generate millions in new recurring annual tax revenue for local schools, infrastructure, emergency services and other public needs. The project includes an investment in new electrical infrastructure that taps underutilized capacity on dedicated power infrastructure in the county, and it is designed so it does not draw on distribution capacity serving existing homes and businesses. Instead of open-loop evaporative cooling, Project Clay uses a fully closed-loop system that operates independently of local water supplies, with the only local water used for sinks and employee bathrooms, on par with the usage of two homes annually.

Giga says the project will finish in under eight months, less than half the time of traditional builds, using a factory-first construction model in which much of the facility is manufactured off-site before final assembly in the community. Brent Whitehead, president and co-founder at Giga Energy, said the company believes AI infrastructure should leave a community stronger than it found it, through high-paying jobs, an expanded local tax base and long-term investments that benefit residents for decades. He said Hunt County is gaining an economic engine that will support schools, public services and future growth for generations. Whitehead also said the project is exactly the kind of AI infrastructure Texas needs, and that communities should not have to choose between economic growth and protecting local resources.

Giga Energy describes itself as a U.S.-based developer, operator and manufacturer of AI data centers, with factories in Long Beach and Houston, and says it has delivered gigawatts of sites and critical infrastructure across the country. The project aligns with Texas' growing emphasis on water-efficient data center development in drought-prone regions, according to the announcement. Giga Energy leaders say that as demand for AI infrastructure continues to accelerate across the United States, the next generation of data centers must do more than power technology and must also earn the trust of the communities where they are built. With this project, Giga officially unveils its GigaBase system, which the company says is engineered to address lengthy construction timelines, heavy water consumption and pressure on local utilities.

stories.Headline: Lansing residents oppose a data center ban vote as TeraWulf subsidiary sues the town
stories.Summary:
Lansing residents packed the Lansing Central School District Middle School Auditorium on Tuesday night, Nov. 17, 2026, to oppose a proposed data center, WSYR reported on Nov. 18, 2026. The crowd gathered for a special Lansing Town Board meeting held for public comment on a proposed local law. The law would amend the town code to define “cryptocurrency,” “cryptocurrency data mine,” “data center” and “general processing.” It would also list cryptocurrency data mines and data centers as disallowed uses in the town’s Schedule of Land Uses or Activities. That change would essentially ban data centers within the Town of Lansing.

The proposal would add the four definitions to the town code and place cryptocurrency data mines and data centers among uses disallowed under the town’s zoning code. TeraWulf, a company that started in bitcoin mining and is expanding into data centers, previously proposed a facility at the former Cayuga Generating Station along Cayuga Lake’s eastern shore. Lake Hawkeye, a limited liability company and subsidiary of TeraWulf, operates at the site of the former Cayuga power plant. Lake Hawkeye filed a suit against the Town of Lansing, the Lansing Town Clerk’s Office and town supervisor Ruth Groff. The town board is set to vote on the proposed ban during a regular meeting starting at 6:30 p.m. Wednesday at the middle school auditorium.

Pace Ralli, vice president of product development for TeraWulf, took to the podium to defend the proposal. He said it was an opportunity to put an unused industrial property back into productive use, create jobs and rethink what exists on the lakeside waterfront when the coal power plant is taken down. He also asserted the project could bring significant private investment and new tax revenue to the community, helping support schools, public services and local infrastructure. Town supervisor Ruth Groff, who is named in the suit, declined to comment. The suit seeks an order directing the Town of Lansing to conduct a legally sufficient search and produce responsive documents in response to the LLC’s two state Freedom of Information Law requests.

One member of the public said people often hear loons in the distance because sound really travels over the water, and contrasted that with a data center emitting over 50 decibels of noise 24/7 at the lake’s edge. Another speaker argued that going against the ban does not mean automatic support of a data center, and said it means individual projects should be thoughtfully reviewed as they come along. Many attendees showed support for the ban by wearing red, and one person in red said that with the same supply of electricity and more demand from data centers, everyone’s costs go up. The suit said Lake Hawkeye filed its FOIL requests to obtain information about back-channel discussions among Lansing Town officials seeking to thwart the construction of a data center on the site. The document claimed town board members took to a private Google Group managed by Karen Edelstein, the spouse of Town Board member Joe Wetmore, to discuss strategies to block the Data Center.

The suit said access to the group was strictly limited by Karen Edelstein, ensuring that town residents who supported the data center and the jobs it would bring could not join. It said Lake Hawkeye sought admission to the private group and was explicitly denied, so it was not able to participate in discussions of public concern to the Town. The suit contends that the alleged use of a private, exclusionary forum by a quorum of Board members to discuss and formulate official policy on the Data Center Project violates the New York Open Meetings Law, which states all of a public body’s meetings must be open to the general public. The document said the Town has not complied with FOIL and appears to have concealed documents responsive to the requests. The suit was filed in state court, according to the reporting.

The town board is set to vote on the proposed data center ban during a regular meeting, which starts at 6:30 p.m. Wednesday at the middle school auditorium. The articles do not say what the board will decide or how the vote will turn out. They do not give the outcome of the Lake Hawkeye suit or any response from the Town beyond Groff declining to comment. They do not say when the FOIL requests were filed or what documents were sought. They do not give the number of speakers, the size of the crowd or the vote count at the Tuesday meeting.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Baidu head Robin Li warns that artificial intelligence could be a bubble
stories.Summary:
Robin Li, the head of Chinese technology giant Baidu, warned that artificial intelligence could be a bubble on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. He spoke during a panel discussion with business leaders in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen. This event took place ahead of talks between the world's top two economies regarding the sensitive technology sector. The warning came as the city hosted the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting this week. Li expressed concern that the current global landscape for this technology is urgent.

Chinese President Xi Jinping is due to hold talks with U.S. counterpart Donald Trump on Thursday, November 19, during APEC. These leaders are expected to discuss the risks posed by AI and the need for cooperation between the two powerhouses. Baidu, a Beijing-based search engine provider, posted its sixth straight drop in quarterly revenue on Monday, November 16, 2026. The company has made an aggressive push into AI, but it faces a domestic consumer slump affecting advertising cash flows. Nvidia is also reporting quarterly results following the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang last week.

Robin Li stated that the expansion of AI into the application layer has arguably fallen short of the expectations of many. He questioned whether companies are seeing higher revenues or increased profits after adopting the technology, suggesting that for most, the answer is no. Li warned that the concern about an AI bubble could become a reality if these issues are not addressed. He acknowledged that there are headwinds in online marketing despite the tangible results seen in the AI strategy of Baidu. The CEO emphasized that there is currently intense competition occurring at the foundational level of the technology.

IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva told AFP in October that losing confidence in future AI returns could lead to worldwide financial stability risks. She noted that tanking stock market valuations could be a result of investors losing faith in the returns from these investments. Market jitters have been heightened by the resignation of Jensen Huang, who admitted to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. This scandal has increased scrutiny of how Chinese companies gain access to the most powerful Nvidia chips despite U.S. export rules. These events affect the global investment boom and the stability of the international stock market.

Baidu is sometimes called China's Google and has aggressively pursued AI development in recent years to stay competitive in the field. The company is currently struggling with a slump in domestic consumption that has dragged down the cash flows from its advertising. Nvidia is facing pressure from Silicon Valley, but the company has rejected an offer from Jensen Huang to return as CEO. The U.S. and China maintain a fierce rivalry in the field of AI while pushing for various safety steps. Tensions over chip exports continue to loom over the diplomatic relations between the two nations.

President Xi and President Trump will meet on Thursday to discuss the risks and potential cooperation regarding artificial intelligence technology. The world awaits the quarterly results from Nvidia to see if the investment boom remains healthy or begins to fail. It remains open whether the two tech powerhouses can find common ground despite their rivalry and the current chip tensions. The articles do not state if Baidu will find a way to reverse its six straight quarters of revenue drops. It is unclear if the global market will stabilize after the scandal involving the former head of Nvidia.

stories.Headline: Wichita Public Schools and Talkmate implement AI tools to personalize student learning
stories.Summary:
Wichita Public Schools began exploring generative artificial intelligence in January 2023 to save teachers time. By April, district leaders shifted their goal toward designing personalized learning experiences for all students. On November 14, Talkmate rolled out an AI agent for learners at the World Chinese Language Conference. A Russian student named Beliaeva Lian used this tool in Beijing to practice her Chinese. Sixty international students from over ten countries also participated in a Chinese learning hackathon.

The Brookings Institution created the Prosper, Prepare and Protect framework to guide schools in using AI. Wichita Public Schools uses grade-banded expectations, starting with simple talks for students in kindergarten through first grade. Students in second through fifth grades have no independent exposure, while those in sixth through eighth use approved tools. High school students critically analyze outputs, and the district follows guidelines from surrounding universities to restrict use. Talkmate launched a mobile AI agent to provide cultural outreach, study tours, and job matching.

Dyane Smokorowski, the digital literacy coordinator, says AI helps design for students in the margins. She believes students still need productive struggle because it is good for their brains and humans. Katelyn Schoenhofer, a technology instructional coach, says AI handles administrative work to free up teachers. He Hongzhi from Capital Normal University says AI provides scientific methods and authentic environments for learners. He believes AI can address the lack of sustained support for those learning the Chinese language.

Beliaeva Lian said she was surprised that the AI could understand her Chinese so accurately. She felt that the Chinese language was not actually that difficult after using the agent. The Brookings Institution notes that AI should deepen learning rather than replace the effort required to learn. Paraprofessionals are now being trained to use AI for one-on-one or small group student support. Families must also be educated to ensure that responsible AI use continues within the home.

Wichita Public Schools wants to avoid the bad habits students developed with previous technology like social media. The district uses scaffolds that are temporary and accommodations that some students will always need. Teachers receive training first so they can model critical thinking skills for their students later. Talkmate is a global partner of UNESCO that promotes a vision called Chinese Made Easy. The mobile agent aims to support learners worldwide at every step of their educational journey.

Wichita Public Schools will continue refining how to measure what is working with their AI tools. Training for paraprofessionals has only just started, so the final outcomes are not yet seen. Smokorowski suggests that districts should collaborate in partnerships rather than exploring these new possibilities alone. The articles do not state if other school districts have adopted the Brookings Institution framework. It remains open whether the Talkmate agent will be adopted by universities in Beijing.

stories.Headline: Bharat Semi raises $24 million to develop AI enabled image sensors
stories.Summary:
Delhi-based semiconductor startup Bharat Semi raised $24 million, or ₹215 crore, in seed funding to develop AI-enabled image sensors, as reported on 16 November 2026. The all-equity round was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures. Valour Capital, Micromax, Gaingels and individual investors also participated. The company plans to use the capital to expand its engineering team and prepare its sensors for commercial production. Bharat Semi expects to begin initial commercial production in 2027.

The startup is developing programmable image sensors that combine image capture, processing and AI capabilities on one chip, eliminating separate processing components. Co-founder Vrinda Kapoor told TechCrunch the architecture could reduce system costs by at least 70% compared with conventional systems. Bharat Semi says its sensors reduce data movement between components by up to 99% and lower system costs by up to 10X compared with conventional multi-chip modules. The company targets smart homes, industrial automation, surveillance and aerospace, and its technology could help air conditioners detect room occupancy and let drones process visual information without extra computing hardware. Bharat Semi was founded in 2021 by Vrinda Kapoor and Vinayak Dalmia.

Kapoor said the project remains under development, referring to a separate semiconductor fabrication project the company announced in India in 2024 involving a technology partnership with the US Space Force. The latest funding will not finance the proposed fabrication facility. Bharat Semi plans to follow a fabless model for its image-sensor business, outsourcing chip manufacturing while focusing on semiconductor design and software. The company currently employs around 75 people across India and the US, including engineering and business development teams in Santa Clara, California. It plans to increase its US workforce to around 20 employees by mid-2027 and has started hiring engineers in Europe.

Bharat Semi has secured design wins with US defence technology company General Atomics and India's Kaynes Semicon, a subsidiary of US-based Kaynes Technology, although its image sensors remain under development. Its first-generation sensors are already in prototyping, and its second-generation sensors will incorporate more advanced AI capabilities. The company expects these prototypes to reach development milestones by mid-2027 and plans to get the newer sensors to customers by the end of 2027. Inc42 reported that the startup is initially targeting consumer electronics and surveillance markets, where cost, power consumption and latency are key considerations, and over the longer term plans to extend its technology to robotics, automotive, aerospace and defence applications. Expected use cases include controlling ceiling fan movement based on visual capture of a sleeping subject, sharing alerts from door cameras when a person or parcel has arrived, and signalling to drones about obstructions in their flight path, all in real time without sending data elsewhere.

The funding comes amid India's efforts to establish a domestic semiconductor industry and follows the launch of the India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 earlier this year, with a budget outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore. Inc42 reported that edge AI is creating demand for hardware that can process information closer to where it is captured, reducing latency, power consumption and data movement. Bharat Semi is eyeing a share of the global image sensor market, expected to reach $49.8 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 7.7%. The global AI sensor market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 48.8% to reach $139.4 billion by 2033, according to Grand View Research. Bharat Semi will take on established players such as Japan's Sony Semiconductor Solutions and US-based OmniVision, alongside emerging startups such as Oculi and France-based Prophesee.

Bharat Semi plans to deploy the capital towards developing its next generation of products, expanding its engineering teams in India and the US, and accelerating go-to-market efforts with global customers. The company is yet to commercialise its technology. The articles leave open how much of the $24 million will go to each stated purpose and the terms of the design wins with General Atomics and Kaynes Semicon. They do not say when the proposed fabrication facility might be completed or what the technology partnership with the US Space Force involves beyond being under development. They also do not specify the size of Bharat Semi's planned European hiring or which customers the go-to-market efforts target.
