stories.Headline: Minnesota doctors and lawmakers say AI healthcare oversight lags behind the technology
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence is already shaping care in Minnesota, but doctors and lawmakers say oversight is not keeping pace with how quickly the technology is changing. At Fairview, AI helps predict where ambulances may be needed, gives families real-time updates and creates electronic medical notes from doctor and patient conversations. The health system also uses AI to check the quality of MRIs before patients leave, according to KSTP. Dr. Sameer Badlani, Fairview’s chief digital and AI officer, said the tools let people get picked up sooner and dropped off sooner, with better use of the fleet and crew.

Badlani said AI is definitely evolving faster than regulations are, and Minnesota currently has no blanket law requiring healthcare providers to disclose every time AI is used. Rep. Peggy Scott, a Republican from Andover, said she wants stronger protections for Minnesota patients and has already tried to put guardrails around AI in healthcare. Asked whether there should be disclosure any time AI is being used, Scott said 100%. The Minnesota Medical Association said bias is one of the main concerns with AI in healthcare, and a task force led by Dr. Rebecca Thomas studied the issue for more than a year.

That task force determined there is an urgent need for more oversight of AI in healthcare. Thomas said the question of who would be responsible if artificial intelligence makes a harmful mistake is not straightforward right now. Fairview said patient recordings from the note-taking tool never leave its secure network, have restricted access and are deleted within a few weeks after they are converted into medical records. Fairview said it already notifies patients about AI and plans to add a notice to its online patient portal so patients can opt out of the note-taking tool.

Articles.Title: AI already plays key role in healthcare. It’s also evolving faster than Minnesota laws.

stories.headline_source: AI already plays key role in healthcare. It’s also evolving faster than Minnesota laws.

stories.Headline: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress oversees a cautious shift in AI funding strategy
stories.Summary:
Nvidia is likely to recalibrate its aggressive financing strategy following a change in leadership. Former CEO Jensen Huang resigned on November 12, 2026, leading to this shift. Colette Kress has served as interim CEO since the resignation of Huang. The company is now expected to take a more cautious investment approach. Financial partners continue to discuss funding arrangements for various artificial intelligence companies.

The $500 billion initiative announced August 10 involves Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR. Nvidia may backstop 25 percent of transactions, which equals 125 billion dollars. An OpenAI data center in Ohio saw guarantees reduced from 250 billion to 105 billion dollars. Apple data center guarantees were cut from 500 billion to under 250 billion dollars. These specific guarantees are separate from the broader third-party capital initiative.

Interim CEO Colette Kress has overseen finances since 2013 and maintains a cautious stance. Former CEO Jensen Huang stated that the days of acting as a blank check are over. Huang told partners in Berlin they must build structures to raise their own funding. He suggested that companies seeking GPUs should collect upfront payments from their own customers. This approach aims to reduce the industry's total dependence on Nvidia's financial support.

UBS estimates that over 50 billion dollars in liquidity could disappear from the market. AI startups and neocloud companies with limited financial resources are directly impacted by this shift. These companies rely on guarantees to secure data centers and AI chips upfront. Low profitability and rising interest rates could make it harder for them to operate.

Morgan Stanley expects future capital to concentrate on large customers with stronger credit profiles. PitchBook reports Nvidia made 129 global investments this year, compared to 49 in 2023. This activity accounted for 27 percent of all global venture investment activity this year. The company projected 70 percent revenue growth for fiscal 2028 during a presentation in August.

Previous adjusted gross margins were 75 percent, with third quarter guidance set at 74 percent. Wall Street expects third quarter revenue of 109.1 billion dollars and earnings per share of 2.47. Nvidia will release fiscal 2027 third-quarter results on November 17 and hold an earnings call. Investors will watch the rollout of the Vera Rubin platform and its revenue contribution.

The company will provide written commentary on results at 6:20 a.m. Korea time, November 18. A $3 billion investment in Perplexity and talks with other startups remain under consideration. The articles leave open how rising memory prices will impact the company's gross margins.

stories.Headline: Kaiser mental health clinicians ratify contract with AI advisory role and 17% wage increase
stories.Summary:
About 2,200 Kaiser Permanente mental health clinicians in Northern California and the Central Valley ratified a four-year labor contract, with 97% voting in favor after more than a year of contentious negotiations. The National Union of Healthcare Workers said Monday that its group of some 2,200 Kaiser mental health therapists, social workers and psychologists had voted to approve the agreement. About 80% of workers cast ballots during a several-day voting period that concluded Sunday. The contract was ratified with 97% support, the union said. Kaiser said it could not immediately respond to a request for comment about the agreement.

The contract bars layoffs through late 2029 and gives clinicians a role in advising Kaiser on AI and other technology changes. The contract includes wage increases of about 17% over the course of the contract. The union's last contract expired at the end of September 2025, and the new four-year agreement retroactively covers a period beginning from that expiration. The company will be required to notify workers in advance of changes in its model of care, including use of AI or other new technologies. The contract creates a process for a union-appointed group of mental healthcare clinicians to give advice to management on the changes and for the union to bargain over effects if the company moves forward.

Kaiser social worker Ilana Marcucci-Morris, who has been involved in the bargaining sessions, called the contract "a big victory" but said the company's behavioral healthcare still falls below the mark. She said workers "bought ourselves some time to give public leaders and legislators time to put parameters in place around AI." She said they "didn't get fully what we wanted in the language" but that it is a win that gave them time to strategize and make sure mental health care stays human. Marcucci-Morris said Kaiser had largely held firm in rejecting union language saying AI tools could be used to support, but not replace therapists. She said the company also pushed to negotiate severance and other layoff provisions, indicating that industry headwinds around AI had made layoffs "a real threat," even amid climbing patient demand for mental health services.

Kaiser spokesperson Candice Lee previously told The Times that "AI does not replace human assessment and care," but that it "holds significant potential to benefit healthcare by supporting better diagnostics, enhancing patient-clinician relationships, optimizing clinicians' time, and ensuring fairness in care experiences and health outcomes by addressing individual needs." NUHW President Emeritus Sal Rosselli said that now that the contract is ratified, workers will need to "be vigilant" to "make Kaiser fully respect the work of its clinicians and the needs of its patients." Kaiser's mental health workers in Southern California who are also represented by NUHW reached a bargaining agreement last year after a nearly seven-month strike. Workers have accused Kaiser in recent months of implementing harsh productivity metrics on clinicians, cutting into their time to respond to patient calls and emails, record notes and prepare for appointments and pressuring the staff to overbook patients. Kaiser did not immediately respond to questions about the productivity metrics.

Last fall, a group of Kaiser workers traveled to Las Vegas to protest remarks by Kaiser Chief Executive Greg Adams and pass out fliers to conference attendees about staffing shortage problems. The union had held a one-day strike in March over AI language. In October, workers authorized a three-day work stoppage, but held off on moving forward with it ahead of a scheduled mediation session with Kaiser that month. Over the summer, the union filed a complaint with the California Department of Managed Health Care over Kaiser's use of digital algorithms to screen patients seeking care. The union alleged that the practice continued despite state law requiring that treatment determinations be made by licensed providers.

Kaiser has maintained that those decisions are still being made by licensed professionals, saying in a statement to news outlet CalMatters that the tool conducts supportive screening and "does not use AI to diagnose patients, make clinical decisions, or determine medical necessity." A Kaiser spokesperson said to the news outlet that patients could still reach a live person by calling a phone number displayed during the e-visit process, and that the online screening tool was "not the only path" to care. The state Department of Managed Health Care has not yet issued a determination about the complaint. Kaiser did not respond to questions from The Times about the complaint. Marcucci-Morris said Kaiser's shift in negotiations came after the Democrats' sweep during the midterm elections that indicated some voter backlash to AI.

Articles.Title: Kaiser mental health clinicians in California ratify labor contract with some AI guardrails

stories.Headline: Judge denies SpaceXAI request to split from AI antitrust class action
stories.Summary:
A California federal judge denied SpaceXAI's request to separate itself from a proposed class action on November 16, 2026, according to a Law360 report by Aneeta Mathur-Ashton. The suit was brought by artificial intelligence users who accuse the leading AI platforms of violating antitrust law through their collaboration. The order keeps SpaceXAI, which the report identifies as Space Exploration Technologies Corp., inside the case rather than letting it proceed on its own. The judge issued the ruling in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, where the case is pending.

stories.Headline: Henna Virkkunen hosts Brussels Apply AI Summit and presents first startup award
stories.Summary:
Nearly 1,000 high-level policymakers, start-ups, industry leaders and researchers will take part in the Apply AI Summit in Brussels on 17 November 2026, the European Commission has announced. They will discuss how artificial intelligence can boost Europe’s competitiveness across 10 strategic sectors and the public sector, according to the press release. The summit will also showcase concrete AI applications, European success stories and innovative projects. Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President for Technological Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, will host the summit and present the first Apply AI Startup Award to three European start-ups. The award recognises innovative European startups and scaleups developing AI solutions in the strategic sectors, the Commission said.

Alongside the in-person event, an online conference platform will run from 16 to 20 November, allowing an additional 2,500 participants to join part of the summit. The Apply AI Summit marks one year since the adoption of the Apply AI Strategy, which sets out how to speed up the use of AI in Europe’s key industries and the public sector. It concludes the first European AI Innovation Month, running from 14 October to 17 November 2026, organised by the European Commission in partnership with the Irish Presidency of the Council of the European Union. Virkkunen, as Executive Vice-President for Technological Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, is responsible for hosting the summit and presenting the first Apply AI Startup Award to the three winning European start-ups. The Commission organised the European AI Innovation Month in partnership with the Irish Presidency of the Council of the European Union.

The press release does not say what the three start-ups said or name them. The articles give no further statements from the hosts or participants. The summit is tied to the Apply AI Strategy, which the Commission adopted one year before the event and which sets out how to speed up the use of AI in Europe’s key industries and the public sector. The articles do not say what happens after the summit beyond the online platform running until 20 November. More to follow.

stories.Headline: JPMorgan and Hyundai Card complete AI agent forex transaction trial without human input
stories.Summary:
JPMorgan Chase and South Korea's Hyundai Card completed a proof-of-concept in which AI agents carried out simulated foreign exchange transactions without direct human intervention, the companies said. In the initial trial, a Hyundai Card AI agent requested a foreign exchange transaction to maintain euro liquidity in its Kinexys blockchain deposit account. JPMorgan said it was the first private blockchain-based autonomous bank-agent-to-client-agent test for corporate treasury management. The companies aim to expand testing in the first half of 2027 to more complex transactions involving multiple AI agents, according to Wee Kee Toh, global head of Kinexys Insights at Kinexys by JP Morgan.

JPMorgan has yet to set a timeline for commercializing the technology. Toh said building the technology itself was relatively straightforward, but establishing appropriate governance and internal controls proved more difficult, and he pointed to questions around accountability and the risks of allowing AI agents to execute financial transactions without direct human oversight. To address those concerns, Kinexys developed a framework that restricts AI agents to predefined transaction parameters and automatically rejects requests that fall outside authorized limits. Toh said an AI agent authorized to transact up to $5 million would be blocked from executing transactions above that threshold, and he described drawing a box around the agent that it can never act outside of.

The companies are also exploring whether to extend their collaboration to other businesses within Hyundai Motor Group, whose broader operations were one reason JPMorgan selected Hyundai Card as a partner, Toh said, and no specific projects have been announced. Hyundai Motor Group holds a combined 78.04% stake in Hyundai Card through Hyundai Motor, Kia and Hyundai Commercial, according to the card issuer's website. Hyundai Card said in July that it completed a proof-of-concept involving a $20,000 transfer using the USDT stablecoin between Hyundai Motor's U.S. and Mexican subsidiaries, with the transfer and verification process taking an average of seven minutes. Kinexys said in August that it had processed more than $4 trillion in transactions since inception, averaging about $7 billion a day, and JPMorgan launched a proof-of-concept for its dollar-denominated deposit token, JPMD, in June 2025, before making it available to institutional clients that November.

stories.Headline: South Korea and other allies sign a security pact to protect AI technologies and supply chains
stories.Summary:
South Korea joined the United States, Japan, and other allies on Sunday, November 16, 2026, to sign a security pact for artificial intelligence. This agreement, known as the San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity, aims to protect critical AI technologies and supply chains from hostile actors. The move occurred just before U.S. President Donald Trump is scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping this Wednesday and Thursday in Shenzhen. The pact is part of a larger State Department initiative called Pax Silica, which seeks to help allied supply chains withstand shocks.

The declaration was signed by the United States, Korea, Japan, Australia, Israel, Britain, India, Singapore, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates. It requires these nations to safeguard sensitive technologies that could provide a military or intelligence advantage if stolen or illicitly transferred. Participating countries plan to establish working groups, including one dedicated to creating economic hubs that attract AI investment. Jacob Helberg, the U.S. under secretary of state for economic affairs, expects Germany, the Netherlands, and Sweden to sign the agreement this week. Second Vice Foreign Minister Kim Jin-a signed the document in person as the head of the Korean delegation.

Jacob Helberg described the declaration as historic because partners agreed to treat the security of technology and infrastructure as a shared responsibility. He noted that chip design, equipment, and shipping ports are often located in different countries, necessitating this joint approach. While some view the bloc as an effort to isolate China, a source familiar with the matter stated that the text does not single out any specific country. Victor Gao, vice president of the Center for China and Globalization, warned that using recent scandals to pressure China would be a total miscalculation.

The timing of the pact coincides with a tariff truce between Washington and Beijing that lasts until January 10, 2027. Upcoming talks in Shenzhen may focus on a trade-off between Chinese rare earths and American AI technology. Tensions have also risen following allegations that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. These concerns about technology leaks have led to bipartisan calls in Washington for stricter export controls on AI chips. If no deal is reached this week, China may use its control of rare earths to pressure the United States.

Articles.Title: Seoul joins U.S.-led AI pact as Washington rallies allies before Trump-Xi talks

stories.Summary:

Responsibility sits with the new House speaker and the Senate president, who each set a priority as the term began. What happens next is not detailed beyond the speaker’s call for speed on AI and the Senate president’s affordability focus. stories.Headline: Marc Andreessen predicts AI job losses will be limited in regulated sectors but growth will suffer
stories.Summary:
Venture capitalist Marc Andreessen, who co-heads Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's task force on jobs and productivity, said on Monday, November 16, 2026, that artificial intelligence will have a dual effect on the job market. He predicted that job losses in sectors covered by government regulation will be largely insulated from major losses, but that those same regulations will limit economic and productivity growth. You might read that as good news, he said, because a revolution will not destroy all the jobs or kill everybody. You could also view it as very negative, he added, because productivity growth and economic growth simply may not grow very much.

Andreessen divides the economy into two categories of sectors, the first being fast-moving ones that see rapid technological and economic change along with rapid job turnover, such as consumer electronics and media entertainment. The second category is a combination of law and government, which is not structured to change rapidly and is typically characterized by extensive subsidization. He said the fastest-growing sectors will see their prices go down, while the slower-growing regulated or government-subsidized sectors will see their prices go up. Your iPhone is getting cheaper and the flat-screen TV on your wall is getting cheaper, he said, but college education is going to cost a million bucks, healthcare is becoming unaffordable, and good luck buying a house.

Andreessen is responsible for the prediction as co-head of the task force on jobs and productivity under Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh, and he set out the two-sector view himself in the remarks reported by Jennifer Schonberger of Yahoo Finance. The article gives no further comment from Warsh or from other members of the task force on the prediction. The report places the remarks against a backdrop of other warnings about AI and work, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's warning of 5% to 10% GDP growth with 10% joblessness, a combination he said is not one we have almost ever seen before. The article does not say what the task force will do next or when it will report.

stories.Headline: Genpact launches Onyx platform for building and governing enterprise AI agents
stories.Summary:
Genpact announced on November 16, 2026 the availability of Genpact Onyx, an Agentic Operations platform for building, running, and governing AI agents in enterprise operations, and the company had unveiled the platform at its Agentic Operations Day in New York on November 12. The platform is powered by Genpact's Process Intelligence Core, which the company describes as operating knowledge codified from decades of running mission-critical work for global enterprises, so that agents start with context on how the work gets done rather than learning it from scratch. Genpact Onyx is the foundation for Genpact's proprietary agentic solutions, starting with the Genpact Accounts Payable Suite, and for custom solutions Genpact builds for clients. The platform embeds into a client's existing technology stack, connects to the client's data and AI foundations, and supports a choice of leading AI models across Genpact's partner ecosystem.

The platform's capabilities include a Process Intelligence Core codified across finance, risk, supply chain, banking, insurance, and procurement, with prebuilt workflows and agents so clients are ready on day one, drawn from doing the actual work and capturing edge cases, exceptions, and human decisions. A learning loop feeds reviewed exceptions and expert decisions back into the core so intelligence compounds over time, and earned autonomy lets agents start by proposing actions for a human expert to approve and take on more of the decision as they prove themselves. Built-in governance makes every agent action controlled, auditable, and traceable to the reason behind the decision, with guardrails and a responsible AI framework built into the platform, along with security and data isolation that meet enterprise standards. Genpact said the platform was launched at its third annual flagship event, held at Spring Studios in New York, where hundreds of clients, partners, and industry analysts attended a program of announcements, product demonstrations, and client presentations, and leaders from Advantage Solutions, Wesco, USA Today, and Ryan Specialty shared how they are putting Genpact's agentic solutions to work.

Balkrishan "BK" Kalra, President and Chief Executive Officer of Genpact, said the company runs mission-critical operations for many of the world's largest enterprises and that is where the return on AI is decided, adding that Genpact Onyx codifies three decades of process intelligence and makes it the foundation for Agentic Operations, with agents running the work and Genpact's experts owning the outcome. Priya Vijayarajendran, Chief Product and Platform Officer, said enterprises get value from AI when they turn operating knowledge into trusted execution rather than simply by adding more agents, and that Genpact Onyx grounds agents in how the work actually gets done, builds governance into every step, orchestrates across agents and human expertise, and lets autonomy be earned one decision at a time. Genpact describes Agentic Operations as a new operating model in which AI agents handle the volume of execution and its domain experts bring judgment and accountability, combining process intelligence, data and AI, a combined human and agent workforce, a partner ecosystem, and governance and security. Genpact said it uses the platform for its own agentic solutions, for custom client solutions in areas where it does not yet have an agentic solution, and for solutions delivered with technology partners.

stories.Headline: Researchers in Mexico use a five-stage human-AI workflow to make shifts in violence representation visible
stories.Summary:
Researchers across institutions in Mexico, including the Metropolitan Autonomous University, Universidad de las Americas, and Tecnologico de Estudios Superiores de Ecatepec, published an exploratory study in Frontiers in Computer Science on how recursive human-AI interaction can make changes in the representation of violence visible. The authors developed a five-stage exploratory workflow grounded in mixed-initiative design, in which computational tools handle structured comparison and generative variation while human contributors supply critical judgment. The first stage involved an exploratory computational evaluation of a non-probability corpus containing 105 news items addressing violence in Mexico, applying techniques to identify recurring terms, prominent actors, geographic locations, and underlying semantic relationships. The team then organized and visualized these computational findings to prepare structured materials for subsequent participatory evaluation.

The second and third phases brought these computational visualizations into an interactive participatory workshop conducted with 15 participants. In the fourth stage of the workflow, the authors analyzed changes across textual and visual iterations. The fifth stage integrated the project findings through expert-supported synthesis, producing both an infographic and a video that summarized the workshop results. The results suggest that recursive human-AI interaction can make changes in the representation of violence visible by combining semantic analysis, participant interpretation, and visual synthesis.

The authors noted significant methodological boundaries, stating clearly that the study employs an exploratory design that does not attempt to estimate population parameters or establish causal relationships. They explained that the reported findings and observed narrative shifts remain specific to the non-probability corpus of 105 news articles and the 15 workshop participants. Despite these constraints, the study authors concluded that the collaborative, mixed-initiative framework effectively demonstrates how computational methods can support generative exploration and comparison while keeping human interpretation central to the analysis of complex media narratives. The article was published in Frontiers in Computer Science, volume 8, as Article 1877314, with a DOI of 10.3389/fcomp.2026.1877314, and was reported by Denise Maddox for Scienmag on November 18, 2026.

Articles.Title: Recursive Human-AI Interaction Can Make Changes in Violence Representation Visible

stories.Headline: Asia-Pacific university leaders urge redefining core missions as AI reshapes knowledge delivery
stories.Summary:
University leaders from the Asia-Pacific region met during the APEC meetings week in November 2026 to discuss how artificial intelligence is challenging traditional knowledge delivery. These educators believe that institutions must redefine their core missions to foster humanistic judgment and bridge the digital divide to ensure education equity. They argue that universities should transition from being the sole providers of teaching to becoming hubs for the co-creation of validated knowledge. This shift requires universities to reform teaching methods by using AI for content delivery while reserving class time for critical discussions and case studies. Angelo Jimenez of the University of the Philippines suggests establishing jointly recognized doctoral programs in bioscience and engineering to retain highly skilled talent.

Tatacipta Dirgantara from the Bandung Institute of Technology emphasizes the need for professor-to-professor partnerships and shared resources to foster intercultural understanding. These changes aim to strengthen foundational literacy and numeracy so that humans maintain control over advanced technology. Angelo Jimenez stated that humans must control legitimacy and validity because AI cannot replace the responsibility of human judgment. Tatacipta Dirgantara noted that while AI is an enabler like the calculator, it cannot replace empathy or the responsibility educators have toward the people. Yang Bin of Tsinghua University observed that some faculty are moving to industry for better computing resources and real-world data.

He believes that sustained dialogue during events like the APEC University Leaders Forum will help build consensus on academic credits and quality assurance. The academic community expects the center of gravity for global higher education to shift toward the Asia-Pacific region as it grows as an innovation hub. Many institutions used the recent APEC gatherings to sign new partnership programs or expand existing collaborations to address the revolutionary impact of AI. These leaders believe that mutual benefit and shared research interests will make these cross-border connections sustainable for the future. Future efforts will focus on mutual recognition of degrees to support the region's expanding role in global economic development.

stories.Headline: 16 Questions Law Firms Should Be Asking About SEO, AI Search and Online Visibility
stories.Summary:
The article, published on 17 November 2026 on the Social Media Butterfly blog, sets out 16 questions law firms should ask about SEO, AI search and online visibility. It was written by an author who says she has worked with law firms of all sizes. She says she has worked with firms whose attorneys have decades of experience, impressive client relationships and extensive publication histories. She says very little of that information appears on their websites. She calls that a missed opportunity as more people turn to AI tools to research legal issues and find lawyers.

The article says a smaller firm with 30 substantive, well-organized pages may perform better for its target searches than a firm with hundreds of generic articles. It names Chambers and Best Lawyers as organizations whose recognition firms should record. It cites New York Labor Law Sections 200, 240 and 241(6), contractual indemnification and risk transfer as topics a construction litigation firm may address on dedicated pages. It says a smaller firm may benefit from concentrating on three to five areas where it has a meaningful track record. It names Google Search Console and website analytics as tools for monitoring organic search impressions, keyword performance, traffic and inquiries.

The author says larger firms have extensive marketing resources and thousands of pages of content, while smaller firms may have only a handful of articles and relatively basic practice descriptions. She says the amount of content a firm publishes is only part of the equation. She says how well that content demonstrates expertise, answers relevant questions and connects to other credible information also matters. She says one of the biggest opportunities she sees is making better use of the experience and content firms already have. She says improving online visibility often starts with documenting accomplishments, strengthening existing pages and creating a more comprehensive picture of what the firm and its attorneys actually do.

The article says attorneys can often reference and link to articles they wrote at previous firms, but republishing the full content may require permission from the copyright owner. It says any description of prior work should accurately identify the attorney's experience and avoid suggesting that matters handled at another firm were handled by the current firm. It says recognition does not automatically improve search rankings or guarantee AI citations. It says different AI search tools use different methods for retrieving and citing information.

It says adding external links simply to increase their number is not an effective SEO strategy. The article says firms should review attorneys' historical articles, client alerts, CLE materials and conference presentations to identify content worth updating, summarizing or linking to. It says a CLE presentation can become an article, a series of FAQs and several LinkedIn posts. It says a webinar can generate a written recap, shorter practice-specific articles and updated content for attorney biographies.

It says an initial project might involve collecting attorneys' publications and credentials, expanding three priority practice pages, updating biographies and creating a centralized archive of news and recognition. It says outside marketing support can help coordinate the work without requiring a large internal team. The article says firms should monitor organic search impressions, relevant keyword performance, website traffic, engagement with priority practice pages and inquiries from prospective clients. It says firms can periodically test how AI-powered search tools describe their capabilities, whether they reference accurate information and which sources they cite.

The text of the article ends mid-sentence in the fifteenth question. The article does not give the sixteenth question. The article gives no figures on results achieved for any firm. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Malcolm Myers finds ten AI-exposed companies lose $206 billion in market value since 2021
stories.Summary:
Ten publicly listed companies operating in sectors exposed to artificial intelligence have collectively lost $206 billion in market value since the end of 2021, according to an analysis by Malcolm Myers, who works with marketplace and services platform businesses at EIV. The erosion in market value initially came despite relatively resilient revenue growth, as nine of the 10 companies recorded higher revenues between 2021 and 2025. Their combined revenue increased 47% from $22.2 billion to $32.7 billion over that period, even as investors questioned whether these businesses could withstand AI disruption. The disruption is now becoming visible in their financial performance, with revenue in the third quarter of 2026 declining 23% at Tripadvisor's hotels business, 25% at Fiverr's marketplace, 33% at Shutterstock and 40% at Chegg. The decline in valuations has been particularly pronounced across four segments that Myers noted in his analysis.

In price comparison and travel search, Tripadvisor has lost 77% of its market value since 2021, while LendingTree and TripAdvisor have declined 68% and 67% respectively, as these businesses largely depend on search traffic and referral fees. Booking.com, which facilitates the actual transaction, has gained 20% in contrast to those search-dependent platforms. Shutterstock has lost 97% of its value, while Wix and Adobe have declined 68% and 66% respectively, as AI increasingly enables users to generate content and applications on demand. Freelance marketplaces have faced similar challenges, with Fiverr losing 93% of its value and Upwork falling 72%, as businesses and consumers increasingly use AI to produce digital work they previously outsourced to freelancers. Chegg has lost 98% of its market value as large language models increasingly provide homework answers and educational assistance free of charge, Myers said.

Myers believes not all marketplaces face the same degree of risk, because platforms that aggregate unique supply, facilitate payments and manage fulfillment could prove more resilient as AI agents work alongside these businesses rather than replace them. He also sees an emerging opportunity in AI-native businesses that deliver completed outcomes instead of simply connecting customers with service providers or offering software to complete tasks. Examples include Corgi, which underwrites and issues insurance policies, Lawhive, which provides legal services through an AI-enabled law firm, and Mercor, which organises specialist work to deliver training data and evaluations. Mercor recently completed a $750 million Series D funding round at a $20 billion valuation, less than four years after its launch, and Myers believes the shift towards delivering completed outcomes could create some of the most valuable marketplaces and services businesses over the next decade.

stories.Headline: Hong Kong Monetary Authority explores agentic AI to detect crypto financial crime
stories.Summary:
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority began exploring the use of agentic AI to monitor crypto asset transactions on Tuesday, November 18, 2026. Executive Director Raymond Chan announced this initiative during a speech at a workshop hosted by the central bank to combat money laundering. This new technology aims to analyze both onchain transfers and offchain customer transactions to identify anomalies. The system would specifically flag rapid fund layering that occurs when users switch between cryptocurrency and fiat money.

This approach requires integrating blockchain analytics, scam intelligence, and customer due diligence into a single on-chain AI agent. Such a system would allow for the monitoring of suspicious wallets and the rapid freezing of illicit funds. Raymond Chan noted that illicit addresses received over 150 billion dollars in 2025, with stablecoins making up 84 percent of those transactions. He also highlighted the Virtual Asset Intelligence Taskforce, which was established in November 2025 to strengthen these efforts.

Raymond Chan stated that the central bank wants to make financial crime monitoring more effective and efficient through AI. He explained that criminal networks use digital assets for human trafficking and fraud because of their global reach and pseudonymity. Chan admitted that no single tool provides complete protection, so the city must rely on multi-layered safeguards. He noted that the primary challenge is quickly linking digital wallet activities to real-world identities to stop funds from disappearing.

The Virtual Asset Intelligence Taskforce treats crypto crime as an ecosystem issue involving regulators, law enforcement, and trading platforms. This public-private group includes the Hong Kong police, the Customs and Excise Department, and the Securities and Futures Commission. By collaborating with licensed crypto trading platforms, the task force has already improved the quality of intelligence. These agencies continue to work together to strengthen the prevention and detection of crimes across the entire digital asset landscape.

stories.Headline: Port Washington mayor Ted Neitzke leads tours of a $15M AI data center site as residents raise concerns
stories.Summary:
A $15 million artificial intelligence data center is under construction in Port Washington, Wisconsin, developed by Vantage in partnership with Oracle and OpenAI, and it is drawing both community curiosity and criticism. The 672-acre site, with an additional 1,000 acres reserved for expansion, is larger than the entire Village of Whitefish Bay, and the construction site sees 3,500 workers daily. Port Washington Mayor Ted Neitzke has been leading van tours of the site to engage locals and address their concerns about the project. The first phase includes four data center buildings, each with a footprint of 800,000 square feet, large enough to hold two Lambeau Fields.

Vantage says the center will be operational by early 2028, providing internet and cloud services while storing, processing, and distributing data. The project is expected to bring significant tax benefits by transforming agriculturally zoned land assessed at a few million dollars into a site valued at $120 million, which is anticipated to support the majority of city services. Construction on the data center began in December 2022 and is scheduled to be completed by 2028. Neitzke said almost everything visible at the site is manufactured, made or fabricated in Wisconsin, so it is not just a Port Washington thing but a statewide one.

Neitzke said he was surprised and caught off guard by the unexpected backlash, saying he did not see that coming. He has emphasized transparency during the tours, addressing concerns about water usage, power supply and electricity rates, and he said the center does not use a lot of water and that power is protected and rates do not go up. He believes data centers are the newest of all the utilities, something everyone needs alongside clean water, clean sidewalks and electricity, and now information. He has also been advising elected officials across the country on how to navigate similar projects, saying local communities are in an amazing position to negotiate.

Clean Wisconsin and other groups have raised concerns about the environmental impact of AI data centers and the power plants required to support them. A Clean Wisconsin representative said Wisconsin is incredibly vulnerable right now to AI data centers, and that a project as large as the one in Port Washington will be vastly bigger in terms of energy needs than anything the state has ever seen. The representative said those are resources everyone relies on and that the conversation needed to happen well before now, when construction is going on and almost done. One contentious meeting resulted in the arrest of three women, and Al Poull, whose family has lived on a nearby farm for 126 years, acknowledged the changes, saying things change and it is just the way it is.

stories.Headline: Chinese bottle-cap manufacturer challenges AI automation hype at Shanghai conference
stories.Summary:
Zhu Shihui, a manufacturer of bottle caps, presented a critical perspective on artificial intelligence during an AI Engineer conference in Shanghai in early November. The speaker challenged the prevailing hype by arguing that the final stage of implementation represents half of the total journey. Zhu criticized consultants who believe every industrial process can be easily automated regardless of the existing infrastructure. This presentation highlighted the practical difficulties of integrating advanced technology into traditional manufacturing environments.

The speaker explained that many factories rely on pre-digital equipment and employ workers, averaging in their late 40s, who lack deep digital skills. Furthermore, these companies often operate on margins so thin that they cannot afford a complete digital transformation. Instead of using an aggressive approach, Zhu suggested that the best method is to exercise humility. This requires seeking out the tacit knowledge of an organization to serve as the foundation for any technological change.

Zhu argued that the current trend of ignoring human expertise in favor of automation is a mistake. The presentation served as a reminder that technical capabilities must be balanced with the reality of the workplace. Other attendees, such as Ryo Lu, also questioned how self-worth is measured when code can be written by machines. Lu expressed a desire to build tools that increase human involvement rather than proving that people are needed less.

The conference showcased a relaxed attitude toward artificial intelligence in China, where practitioners view it as a marketing tool rather than a global threat. Demos included a 35 billion-parameter model from AutoArk running on an iPhone 16 Pro and robot hardware from DYNA. The event also featured a significant number of women engineers, contrasting with the gender dynamics often seen at similar events in America or Australia.

stories.Headline: Jassy says Amazon is talking to outside AI agent companies about shopping access
stories.Summary:
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on Tuesday at Semafor's Silicon Valley & The World conference that Amazon has not permanently closed the door on outside AI shopping agents making purchases on its platform. He said the company has not said it will never open things up, but that any arrangement has to offer a good customer experience and a fair exchange of value. In September, Amazon publicly blocked Meta's Muse agent from making purchases on its platform, saying the block helps ensure a safe, secure, and reliable customer experience. Amazon has said it applies its policies evenly, and users have also reported that Instinct AI and OpenAI's Dots struggled to buy items on their behalf on Amazon.

Jassy said Amazon is talking to every one of those companies, and he added that every retailer should have the right to decide how it interacts with agents. He said he believes the primary way people will use agentic shopping is in concert with the retailer they like to use, telling an app to buy the deodorant they normally buy using past orders, shipping information, and payment information. Amazon is also betting heavily on its own AI shopping tools, including Alexa for Shopping and Buy for Me, which are guided by Amazon's About You customer dossiers. The outside agents, which include Meta's Muse, Instinct AI, and OpenAI's Dots, are advertised as capable of taking action on a customer's behalf, including making online purchases.

That capability could cut retailers out of the browsing experience they have long controlled, and it raises thorny questions about ad sales, account security, identity verification, and who is on the hook when an order goes wrong. Other companies have taken a different tack, with Shopify openly embracing outside AI shopping agents. Home Depot's chief information officer recently told Business Insider that the home improvement store's online marketplace wants agents to identify themselves first. The article does not say what happens next beyond Jassy's comments that Amazon is talking to the agent companies.

stories.Headline: Anthropic prepares a $60 billion IPO this Thursday despite AI market fears
stories.Summary:
Anthropic is preparing to sell stock to the public during a volatile period for artificial intelligence companies. The company plans to launch its initial public offering this coming Thursday. This move comes as investors fear an AI bubble and financing costs rise. The company is pressing ahead despite a shaky market and political headwinds. This blockbuster sale could raise more than 60 billion dollars.

The offering uses the ticker name ANT and sets a price range of 70 to 78 dollars per share. At the top range, it could raise 64.4 billion dollars and value the company at 1.4 trillion dollars. Nvidia has agreed to buy an estimated 10 billion dollars of stock after the debut. Anthropic has 6.2 billion dollars in debt and plans to spend 70 billion dollars next year. Total computing and infrastructure spending will reach 900 billion dollars in the coming years.

CEO Dario Amodei told Jamie Dimon of JPMorgan Chase that the company is very paranoid about AI safety. Amodei stated that the firm focuses on enterprise customers and coding tools to remain synergistic with safety. He said he spends 40 to 50 percent of his time on talent and company culture. Amodei noted that the company avoids hiring jerks or people not oriented toward the public benefit. He believes cognition is exponential and will open new markets like scientific research.

Investors are jittery, and some fear that the AI bubble could burst soon. CoreWeave stock plunged 15.5 percent on October 14 before surging 25 percent and then dropping 7 percent. Newly elected Democrats in Texas and Georgia vow to stop new data center construction. These politicians and a Congressional effort seek a national moratorium on new data centers. This political environment threatens to slow the growth of the artificial intelligence industry.

Nvidia stock dropped 4 percent after CEO Jensen Huang resigned over affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. In 2021, nearly 400 companies went public, but only 71 did so the next year due to recession fears. President Donald Trump's Liberation Day tariffs in April 2025 caused StubHub and Klarna to postpone their offerings. Firmus, an Australian data center company, called off its IPO last month. Robert Shiller's measure shows stocks currently trade at 40 times their long term earnings.

Anthropic will beat rival OpenAI to the public market if the offering proceeds as expected. The company may fetch top dollars for shares before Democrats take office in January. The articles leave open whether the company will postpone the IPO at the last minute. It remains unclear if the company can find a clear path to profitability. The final pricing and total haul of the offering are not yet determined.

stories.Headline: China integrates artificial intelligence into national education to create an AI-native generation
stories.Summary:
Beijing is currently pushing to integrate artificial intelligence into its national education system to create an AI-native generation of students. This state-led effort involves nearly 200 million primary and secondary students across the country in a massive learning experiment. The government wants universal AI literacy for all school children by the year 2030 to ensure economic success. This initiative aims to nurture homegrown innovation to help China win its technological rivalry against the United States. President Xi Jinping has declared that AI education is fundamental to the reform of the national schooling system.

The Beijing New Talent Academy costs 39,000 dollars annually and serves over 2,000 students on a 12 hectare boarding campus. Shanghai mandates 30 hours of annual AI teaching per grade, while Beijing plans 100 AI pilot demonstration schools. Ningxia and Gansu plan to include AI literacy in high-stakes entrance exams by 2027, and Yunnan will record 14,000 classrooms. Guizhou uses AI facial recognition and behavioural analysis, while Shanghai deploys systems for monitoring the mental and physical health of students. The education ministry has encouraged AI courses, teacher training, and pilot programmes since the start of 2024.

President Xi Jinping vowed to make AI for all during his debut at the top tech summit in China. Headmaster Liu Wei stated that AI should be an everyday tool for most students rather than just for future scientists. Headmaster Yang Tianliang said AI agents do not suffer from fatigue and never make students feel stupid for asking questions. An Alibaba spokesperson noted that the Cloud for Youth Programme gives students direct access to AI tools and education. Ted Mo Chen of ClassIn said implementation is all over the place and few schools integrate AI effectively.

Parents like Rita Luan worry that AI might shortcut learning and require close supervision to ensure children digest the solutions. Students using AI three times weekly showed lower memory, comprehension, analytical, and creative skills than those who used it less. A study of 27,000 teenagers found an 18 per cent homework score increase but a 20 per cent exam score decline. Rural students may be more vulnerable to device addiction and cognitive outsourcing, where they delegate mental tasks to the technology. Many educators are grappling with how to deploy AI without reinforcing the rote-learning habits that policymakers want to move beyond.

The US relies on non-binding guidance and lacks dedicated funding or state-level teacher standards, according to the 2026 Stanford AI Index. Government procurement records show at least 31 million dollars spent last year on AI classroom equipment, training, and teaching platforms. iResearch estimates 2025 spending on education digitalisation at just under 83 billion dollars, with generative AI taking 46 per cent. Funan County Qinqing High School in Anhui uses AI to solve teacher shortages for 4,000 pupils who are migrant children. This school uses AI models from Z.AI, ByteDance, and Alibaba's Qwen to generate interactive lessons, text, images, and videos.

China has not yet established a standard framework for measuring AI literacy, leaving schools to experiment without a clear scorecard. Selena Guo of China Policy noted that mature assessment rubrics for compulsory school-level AI competency are still being built now. The education ministry did not respond to requests for comment, and ByteDance and Z.AI also did not respond to inquiries. It remains unclear if the short-term gains in homework scores will lead to long-term intellectual development or cognitive decline. The articles leave open whether the government can successfully balance AI efficiency with the need for independent and critical thinking.

stories.Headline: IDB report finds broad AI adoption could raise Latin America and Caribbean GDP by 5.1% over a decade
stories.Summary:
The Inter-American Development Bank published a report finding that broad adoption of artificial intelligence could boost Latin America and the Caribbean’s gross domestic product by 5.1% over a decade. The report, “From Digitalization to Artificial Intelligence: Turning Promises into Productivity,” is the 2026 edition of the Development in the Americas series. It was published on Monday, November 16, 2026, and covered by GlobeNewswire and EL PAÍS. The Washington-based organization also projected that wages could rise 4.2% over the same period. The analysis stresses the need for reforms to capture these gains.

The 422-page document states that in a high-adoption, high-productivity-impact scenario, the region’s total factor productivity could increase by 2.3%. It reports that 35% of adults used generative AI in 2025-2026, compared with 43% in European OECD countries and 58% in the United States. Only 26% of adults recently interacted with government digitally, compared with 70% in OECD countries, and only 27% recently made purchases online, compared with 66% in OECD countries. While 63% of digitally engaged firms surveyed use generative AI, 82% rely on off-the-shelf tools or light adaptations rather than solutions integrated into operations. The report cites studies showing productivity increases of 59% among writers, 26% among software developers and 15% among customer service providers who use AI.

IDB Group President Ilan Goldfajn said artificial intelligence can become a powerful accelerator of development, but its benefits will not come automatically. He said the Partnership for AI Adoption brings together governments and leading technology companies to help the region harness AI’s potential to raise productivity and translate gains into better jobs, better public services and shared prosperity. Laura Alfaro Maykall, IDB chief economist and economic counselor, said the report moves the discussion from potential to evidence. She said the research quantifies how AI could affect productivity, growth and wages across the region and identifies the conditions for countries to capture those gains. Julián Cristia, lead economist at the IDB, said governments must promote AI adoption while the digital agenda is still unfinished.

Cristia said 90% of people in the region can submit taxes online, but that is a time-saving rather than a decisive organizational change. He said the big change would be prefilled tax declarations drawing on public and private sources, so the taxpayer only needs to accept the return. The report calls for targeted training and enhanced income support for displaced workers, education systems that promote adaptability, and greater private and public investment in cybersecurity including data privacy. It endorses regulations that carefully weigh costs and benefits to households. IDB officials note that smaller and informal firms often lack the managerial capacity, financing and technological support needed to adopt AI effectively.

The findings were fundamental to September’s meeting of the IDB Group-led Partnership for AI Adoption, which convenes governments from the region and technology companies such as Google, Anthropic, Microsoft and Nvidia. The report notes the region has struggled with weak productivity growth for six decades. It says digital technologies are already improving business operations and public services, and AI adoption can expand these gains. In Mexico, an AI-based app helped reduce users’ depression by 20%, and in Costa Rica an electronic single-window system increased export values by 46%. In São Paulo, Brazil, a digital health platform serves 3.4 million users and has delivered 2 million teleconsultations.

The report offers three prescriptions: strengthen enabling conditions by investing in institutions, digital skills, data, cybersecurity and reliable digital infrastructure; transform government by integrating public-sector systems and redesigning services around AI with human oversight; and accelerate business adoption through access to finance, technical assistance, training and innovation. It concludes the region can turn technological change into lasting development gains by strengthening institutions, skills, data and digital infrastructure. The IDB, founded in 1959, works with the region’s public sector and promotes growth in 26 countries. The articles leave open how the projected gains would be distributed and which reforms governments will adopt.

stories.Headline: Asian investors sell off AI stocks ahead of Nvidia earnings and Anthropic IPO
stories.Summary:
Asian investors sold off artificial intelligence stocks on Sunday, November 15, 2026, as they reduced their exposure to the volatile tech sector. This market movement occurred because investors are cautious ahead of a crucial week for the boom in artificial intelligence technology. The selloff caused benchmark stock indexes in Taiwan, South Korea, and Japan to slump, with the Taiex plunging more than 4 percent. US Nasdaq 100 futures fell 0.5 percent after the cash index dropped 1.2 percent on the previous Friday. These actions reflect a fragile market sentiment as traders await several major corporate and economic events scheduled for the coming days.

Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday, while Claude chatbot maker Anthropic prices its initial public offering on Wednesday and debuts on Nasdaq Thursday. Interim CEO Colette Kress, the former chief financial officer, must now shore up investor confidence following the resignation of Jensen Huang. Huang left the company last week after revelations of extramarital affairs, leaving a leadership void at the signature AI bull market stock. LSEG data shows Nvidia lost 1.9 trillion dollars in market capitalisation since early October due to concerns over debt-fuelled AI buildouts. Additionally, Democrats won the US midterm elections earlier this month, which threatens to bring more stringent regulations on data-centre expansion.

Interim CEO Colette Kress is responsible for managing the company, but media speculation suggests Jensen Huang might discuss a possible comeback. The Financial Times reports that Nvidia has approached Rene Haas, the CEO of British chipmaker Arm Holdings, for the leadership role. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on Sunday that the company needs to find a leader outside the firm. Elon Musk stated on X on Saturday that Nvidia would lose critical deals if Huang is not at the helm. These figures believe the leadership crisis is a primary driver of the current pressure on the artificial intelligence trade.

Investors in Asia are the most affected by the current slump, though European markets have remained more resilient during this volatility. The lower concentration of AI shares in Europe has bolstered the continent's appeal as a haven, with futures rising in Germany. US consumers are also in focus as earnings from Home Depot, Lowe's, Target, and Walmart provide insight into their resilience. Retail sales data on Tuesday will further clarify the economic state of the consumer during this period of tech market instability. Market participants are now watching to see if the AI trade can recover from this recent series of shocks.

The AI boom has been led by a four-year tech-led bull market, but sustainability concerns have grown since early October 2026. Inflationary pressures have raised market bets to about 8 percent for a supersized half-point interest rate hike in December. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh will speak in San Francisco on Monday about how AI will reshape the entire US economy. The Federal Reserve is also under scrutiny following hawkish comments from officials regarding the current state of national inflationary pressures. These background factors have created a tense environment for investors who are weighing tech growth against broader economic risks.

The Federal Reserve will release the minutes of its October policy meeting on Wednesday, and several Fed speakers will talk this week. Markets will monitor the retail sales data and the specific earnings results from Nvidia to determine the next direction for stocks. The debut of Anthropic on the Nasdaq will serve as another major test for the current sentiment regarding AI investments. It remains open whether Jensen Huang will return to the company or if Rene Haas will be appointed as CEO. The articles leave it unclear how the new tech boom will evolve and on what specific timetable it will progress.

stories.Headline: US stocks drop as investors sell AI shares before Nvidia earnings report
stories.Summary:
U.S. stock markets experienced a sharp decline on Monday, November 16, 2026, as investors sold off artificial intelligence shares. This downturn occurred just before Nvidia was scheduled to release its quarterly financial results. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 739.38 points, which is 1.41 percent, while the S&P 500 dropped 145.08 points, or 1.92 percent. Additionally, the Nasdaq Composite Index fell by 626.52 points, representing a 2.5 percent decrease.

The market shift saw nine of the eleven S&P 500 sectors end in the red, with technology falling 2.98 percent and communication services dropping 2.82 percent. Nvidia shares fell 4.12 percent following the recent resignation of chief executive officer Jensen Huang, whom the board is not considering rehiring. Other chipmakers suffered heavily, as Intel, Micron, Marvell, and Arm each dropped over 6 percent, while Advanced Micro Devices fell 5.58 percent and Broadcom fell 3.92 percent. Dell Technologies and Oracle declined nearly 7 percent and 5 percent, respectively, while the VIX volatility index hit a high of 24.52.

David Kelly, the chief global strategist at J.P. Morgan Asset Management, stated that there are many doubts regarding technology currently. He advised investors to diversify their holdings in artificial intelligence because the trade is entering a more volatile period. Meanwhile, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh spoke in San Francisco about three different economic scenarios regarding artificial intelligence. These models range from a productivity boom to increased unemployment or a disappointing payoff that could lower share prices.

Other economic indicators showed the Empire State manufacturing index fell to 7.8 in November from 25.5 in October. West Texas Intermediate crude oil dropped 3.21 percent to 85.72 U.S. dollars a barrel due to recovering shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. In contrast, Tyson Foods rose 8.72 percent after reporting fiscal fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of 61 cents per share. Looking ahead, Anthropic plans to price its initial public offering on Wednesday and begin trading on the Nasdaq this Thursday.

stories.Summary:
The AI trade unwind continued on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, which pushed global stocks lower. Investors prepared for the stock market launch of Anthropic later in the week. Nvidia released its quarterly results, and the stock rose 4% in choppy trade. Solid US retail sales and hawkish Federal Reserve comments kept expectations for higher interest rates alive. Jamie McGeever reported these events from Orlando, Florida.

The S&P 500 tech sector fell 20% since October 6, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor index dropped 30%. Nvidia lost nearly 40% since October 6, shedding over 1.7 trillion dollars in market value. Alphabet lost 640 billion dollars, SpaceX lost 450 billion dollars, and Micron lost 300 billion dollars. Eli Lilly added 250 billion dollars, while gold fell to a one-year low of 3,950 dollars per ounce. Japan stocks fell 1.3%, Europe and UK stocks fell 1.8%, Nasdaq fell 0.7%, S&P 500 fell 1%, and Dow fell 1.6%.

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the economy likely requires several interest rate increases before spring 2027. He believes current policy is a full percentage point below where it should be, suggesting four hikes. Interim CEO Colette Kress hosted the Nvidia earnings call after the company's third quarter results landed. Former CEO Jensen Huang said he would be honored to return to the chipmaker as leader. The US Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia, and Huang agreed to appear before Congress.

Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, said diseases like cancer and Alzheimer's will be relics in less than a decade. Eli Lilly CEO Dave Ricks disagreed on X, stating that progress will likely be steady and incremental. BofA's Michael Hartnett named healthcare among the groups most vulnerable to downside in a recent report. He also listed semiconductors, discretionary, and homebuilders as most vulnerable to upside over the next eight weeks. Investors in tech and chips were affected by heavy selling, while the US dollar hit a 19-month high.

AI stocks lost about 5 trillion dollars in less than a month during October. Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk gained 92% on average in 15 months after the October 2022 low. Novo Nordisk lost three-quarters of its value from its June 2024 peak during the subsequent two years. Trump's China data center curb advanced despite lobbying from Amazon, Google, and Meta. Nvidia's daughter, a senior director of product marketing, helped shape the defense of ties to Megaspeed in Singapore.

The market awaits the US FOMC October meeting minutes and UK and Euro zone inflation data on Wednesday. European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde is scheduled to speak, along with Fed officials Michael Barr and John Williams. Neel Kashkari is also scheduled to speak as the market looks for signs of a fourth rate hike. The articles leave open whether the rates futures curve will price in more than three 25 bps increases. stories.Headline: US and nine allies form coalition to protect AI technology and infrastructure from China
stories.Summary:
The United States and nine allied nations formed a coalition to protect critical technologies associated with artificial intelligence. This strategic partnership was established to secure the supply chains and infrastructure necessary for advanced computing. The group intends to create a protective barrier against the influence of China in the technology sector. These nations are working together to ensure that sensitive AI models remain secure from foreign adversaries. The coalition is operating under a new framework known as the Pax Silica initiative to manage national security.

This effort requires the implementation of strict export controls on high-end semiconductors and specialized AI hardware. The partners are coordinating their policies to prevent the leakage of intellectual property to rival states. They are focusing on the protection of critical infrastructure that supports the development of large-scale AI models. The governments of the ten participating countries are responsible for overseeing these new security measures.

Officials stated that the collaboration is essential to maintain a technological edge over global competitors. They believe that fragmented policies would allow adversaries to exploit gaps in the global supply chain. The leaders emphasized that collective action is the only way to safeguard the future of democratic technology. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Applied Materials plans to double equipment output by 2028 to meet AI chip demand
stories.Summary:
Applied Materials announced plans to double its equipment output by 2028 to meet rising demand for artificial intelligence chips. The company shared these details during an earnings conference call held on November 12 local time. This growth is driven by increased investments in advanced packaging, DRAM, and advanced logic chips. The firm expects wafer fab equipment demand to grow more than 30 percent next year from 2026. This strategy follows a period of rapid earnings growth for the US semiconductor equipment maker.

The company aims to more than double its manufacturing and research facility capacity by 2030. Brice Hill stated the output goal for 2028 is compared with the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. The Santa Clara, California firm operates a facility in Austin, Texas, as part of Apple's American Manufacturing Program. China sales rose 35 percent to 2.64 billion dollars, though they were 25 percent of fourth quarter revenue. The company also opened a 600 million dollar plant in Singapore that adds 1,000 jobs.

Chief executive Gary Dickerson said that major customers are placing orders earlier and updating their demand forecasts for eight quarters. He noted that the company continues to receive requests to ramp up production and accelerate deliveries to clients. Dickerson stated that no customers were seeking to delay equipment deliveries during the recent earnings conference call. He expects 2027 to be another record year for both the market and for Applied Materials. The company is benefiting from chipmakers racing to meet extraordinary AI led demand for chips and memory.

Bob O'Donnell of TECHnalysis Research said that actual market metrics show that the current demand is still very strong. He added that the results show foundries and chipmakers are buying as much equipment as they possibly can. The company's growth affects its partners and the broader semiconductor supply chain across the United States and Singapore. Short term supply constraints for certain components have already created some challenges for the company's recent revenue. These constraints prevented the company from securing all the components needed to reach a higher quarterly revenue forecast.

Fiscal 2026 ran from October 27, 2025, to October 25, 2026, with record revenue of 34.45 billion dollars. This marked the seventh consecutive annual revenue record for the company since the start of fiscal 2020. Fourth quarter fiscal 2026 revenue hit a record 10.41 billion dollars, which was up 53 percent from last year. Operating income for that quarter reached 3.66 billion dollars, while the annual operating income climbed to 11.09 billion dollars. The company's stock has risen about 48 percent throughout 2026 as AI chip demand continues to fuel spending.

Applied Materials forecast first quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of 11.1 billion dollars, plus or minus 500 million dollars. This represents a 58 percent increase from a year earlier and exceeds Wall Street estimates of 10.89 billion dollars. The company identified more than 20 projects for new fabs and line expansions starting operations in 2027. Over 10 additional major projects are scheduled to begin operations in 2029 or 2030 according to company data. The articles leave open how the company will resolve the short term supply constraints for certain equipment components.

This initiative is part of the Galaxy AI Classes launched in January 2025 for upper grade elementary and middle school students. The program has already seen over 200,000 graduates and expects to reach more than 250,000 after the second semester.

Samsung Electronics is responsible for the program and is refining the curriculum using feedback from current teachers. The company also utilizes a content advisory committee made up of internal and external experts to improve the lessons. For the second semester recruitment this year, 173 schools representing about 22,000 students applied on the first day. Samsung plans to educate approximately 70,000 students during this second semester to expand the reach of its AI literacy efforts.

The broader context involves Samsung integrating intelligent agents into its mobile operating systems to streamline device performance. An AI financial analyst named ARTi launched in July to provide investment research. Hong Kong listed companies and family offices made strategic investments in the startup. The tool can also generate investment research reports for its users.

Delin Holdings, listed as 1709.HK, made a strategic investment in the platform. C Capital provided 1.5 million US dollars in Pre-A round funding in June. This investment gave the company a pre-money valuation of 30 million US dollars. The product reached 70,000 users within four months of its official launch. It connects to communication platforms like WhatsApp instead of requiring a new App.

CEO Eason Zhang said the tool solves the problem of information overload. He stated that every investment judgment made by the AI must be verifiable. Zhang believes professional agents need specific data sources and financial analysis frameworks. He noted that general large models often prefer guessing over admitting uncertainty. The team uses multi-model collaboration to establish a system for result verification.

High-net-worth investors and beginners, including Hong Kong university students, use the service. Some users from Delin's wealth management business provide core customer feedback. These professional investors require continuous tracking and clear frameworks for their research. Many users have expressed a willingness to pay for these professional services. The product currently serves as a value-added service for certain high-net-worth clients.

Eason Zhang previously served as a strategic consulting partner at a global firm. He founded a fintech enterprise after leaving that consulting role in 2015. The startup combines Silicon Valley AI technology with Hong Kong financial business resources. CTO Steve brings experience from Silicon Valley entrepreneurship to the technical architecture. A chief scientist from a Silicon Valley laboratory serves as an expert consultant.

The company has started its Series A financing to grow the business. ARTi plans to launch a subscription model with various monthly paid packages. stories.Headline: Claroc finds Grok Build exposes corporate data for thousands of users
stories.Summary:
Security firm Claroc discovered that Grok Build exposed corporate data for thousands of users recently. This vulnerability was caused by default sharing settings and a flawed URL design. The platform is operated by SpaceXSI, which is the new name for xAI. The breach occurred because the system used capability based access control. This method relies on the secrecy of the URL to restrict access.

The system generates randomized subdomains ending in grok.me, such as failing chassis traders. Claroc found 37,571 online subdomains, and 35,578 of these exposed data without a login. The default sharing permission was set to anyone with the link. This design allowed passive DNS services to collect hostnames and reveal application addresses. These flaws affected 24 internal applications created by SpaceXSI and X employees.

Claroc notified SpaceX about these security findings on November 8 but received no response. Ars Technica reported that SpaceXSI removed links to its 24 internal apps after an inquiry. However, Claroc stated that no access restrictions were implemented for applications created by other users. The company noted that private access should be the default for all platforms. They urged companies to require security reviews for all AI generated software.

The breach affected Fortune 500 companies, defense contractors, and a Peruvian construction company. The construction firm exposed medical records for 3,784 workers on an occupational health dashboard. Tesla exposed the names, productivity, and bonuses of 22 mechanics in a performance report. A U.S. Navy contractor lost personnel rosters, and an IT firm exposed a hardware bill. A Norwegian Finnish aerospace group exposed explosives inventory and handling procedures at a U.S. facility.

Vibe coding allows non developers to build software using natural language and simple prompts. Other platforms like Lovable, Bolt, and Replit may also be vulnerable to passive DNS searches. Moltbook previously exposed 1.5 million tokens, and Cal AI exposed 3.2 million user records. Red Access found 5,000 exposed assets across Lovable, Base44, Replit, and Netlify in early May. Meta Muse suspended its sharing feature on October 20 after a similar discovery.

SpaceXSI has removed its own internal apps, which now display an app not found message. The articles leave open whether other users have secured their specific application visibility settings. It remains unclear if SpaceXSI will change the default sharing permissions for all Grok Build users. The reports do not state if the affected defense contractors or Fortune 500 firms were notified. No timeline is provided for fixing the underlying passive DNS vulnerability.
