stories.Headline: Diligent Institute finds only 15% of APAC boards very confident in overseeing major risks
stories.Summary:
Diligent Institute published its APAC Governance Outlook 2027 report on 18 November 2026, based on an online survey run during August and September of board members, C-suite leaders, general counsel, company secretaries and other governance leaders across Asia-Pacific, with Australian-headquartered organisations making up 63% of respondents. The report found that cybersecurity, data protection and privacy were the leading strategic priority for 69% of respondents, with AI deployment next at 54% and operational cost optimisation at 52%. Despite that focus, only 15% said they were very confident their board had the information, expertise and processes needed to oversee significant risks, and the most commonly cited barriers were insufficient time at 26% and a lack of relevant expertise at 17%. Respondents also described a broader risk backdrop, with 55% expecting economic downturns to disrupt their organisations over the next 12 months, 53% naming geopolitical events as a major threat and 48% identifying cyber and data privacy incidents as a likely source of disruption.

On AI, 29% of respondents said adoption was outpacing governance, 25% said governance was keeping pace and 8% said governance was ahead of adoption, while a quarter said they used approved AI tools for governance workflows, 17% reported informal use of general-purpose or consumer tools and another 25% had no foreseeable plans to use AI in those settings. Asked about the main opportunities from AI, 78% pointed to improved data analysis and reporting and 58% named workflow automation, while 66% cited security and privacy as their leading AI concern and half named hallucinations, misinformation or disinformation. Digital technology, including AI and data management, was the most frequently cited board skills gap at 62%, more than double the 29% who named cybersecurity, and 65% said more time for strategic planning or dedicated planning meetings would improve the boardroom while 26% said their board lacked time to discuss emerging risks. Nearly half called for more formal development, with 49% selecting mandatory director training or continuing education and 48% wanting greater access to outside parties or experts on specific issues and risks.

Dottie Schindlinger, executive director of Diligent Institute, said effective oversight is not about adding every emerging issue to an already full agenda but about understanding how risks intersect, identifying what matters most to the organisation's strategy and decisions, and ensuring management is taking action. She said boards can start by asking for clear, integrated reporting that connects emerging risks to business priorities, dedicating time to challenging assumptions, and gaining a clear understanding of where and how AI is being deployed, including in their own governance processes. The articles say the findings come as boards in Australia face regulatory scrutiny over operational resilience, cyber governance and executive accountability, and that the concentration of Australian respondents gives the results particular relevance for local boards as organisations deal with cyber threats, data governance questions and pressure to demonstrate clearer oversight of AI use. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the report's findings and recommendations.

stories.Headline: Microsoft and over 40 partners launch AI Transparency Initiative to set open standards for accountable AI
stories.Summary:
At Microsoft Ignite on Tuesday, Microsoft Chairman and CEO Satya Nadella announced the AI Transparency Initiative, a collaborative effort with customers and partners. The initiative is a common, open approach to security and governance across models and providers. Microsoft launched it with organizations across industries to strengthen enterprise trust in AI models and agents. The announcement came from Redmond, Wash., on Nov. 17, 2026. The initiative reflects a principle that greater AI autonomy requires greater transparency.

The initiative has three parts, the first being that Microsoft will expand its participation in the National Institute of Standards and Technology's SI Agent Standards Initiative and draw on its research. Second, Microsoft is collaborating with more than 40 organizations, including Accenture, Adobe, KPMG, Mastercard and Volvo Cars, to help develop open standards for AI systems that are accountable, independently verifiable and safe by design, regardless of the model or provider. Third, Microsoft will incorporate this work into Microsoft AI, Microsoft Foundry and Microsoft Copilot, enabling customers to use the resulting evidence with their security and compliance tools, whether from Microsoft or other providers. The initiative is designed to work across models and providers, including closed and open-weight models, so developer teams can change or update the models powering their agents without compromising IT and security teams' ability to govern them securely or compliance teams' ability to audit their actions. Organizations interested in helping shape the initiative or following its progress can learn more and sign up at aka.ms/learnmoreAItransparency.

Hayete Gallot, Executive Vice President, Microsoft Security, said every organization needs greater transparency into the model itself for security controls to be effective. Gallot said the work will bring more transparency to all models and called it a critical step in making containment smarter and stronger, allowing better accountability and traceability. Aanchal Gupta, Chief Security Officer, Adobe, said security teams need clear visibility into what agents are accessing, what actions they are taking and how those actions can be verified. Gupta said building a common approach to AI transparency across the industry is essential to strengthening trust and helping organizations innovate with confidence while maintaining security and accountability. John Israel, Global Chief Information Security Officer, KPMG International, said clients want to move faster with AI and should not have to choose between innovation and safety.

Israel said trust in AI requires transparency, explainability and responsible oversight, and that KPMG is proud to work with Microsoft on the initiative to help establish open, industrywide standards. Harpreet Sidhu, global cybersecurity lead, Accenture, said organizations taking the next step in their AI reinventions need a solid foundation of trust and confidence to build from. Sidhu said initiatives like this from Microsoft to take an open, industry-driven approach to AI transparency can help as Accenture secures AI models and fits them with controls and governance. Enterprises are connecting AI models to data, tools, credentials and infrastructure, enabling agents to take actions without human approval at every step. Agents with access to data, tools and credentials carry the risk profile of a privileged insider but operate at machine speed and scale, making independent oversight essential.

Existing controls can observe much of the activity around AI models, but they cannot see what happens within them or independently verify their accounts of their own behavior. This limits organizations' ability to understand the context behind an agent's actions, and that evidence gap creates security, compliance, audit and accountability risk. Security teams need a new trust architecture to address the growing insider risks posed by increasingly capable AI agents. Accountability stays with the organization, and when something consequential happens, leaders answer to customers, employees, boards, auditors and regulators.

Blaming the AI isn't an answer, and "trust the model" isn't a control. Microsoft believes every organization should be able to see what AI systems access and do, verify their actions independently and control what they are permitted to do. On seeing, organizations should know what the AI was asked and authorized to do, which model and runtime were used, what data and tools it accessed, and what actions it took, and monitor agent activity and risk signals continuously against policies and thresholds. On verifying, agents cannot be the sole source of truth about their own behavior, and frontier models cannot be trusted to govern themselves.

Evidence covering agent identity, delegated intent and actions should identify its source, the model, the runtime around it, or independent systems such as identity and policy, so model-reported signals can be checked against independently observed records. Organizations should be able to independently verify AI activity using their own security and compliance systems, without relying solely on the model provider's account of its behavior. On controlling, clear evidence of each workflow's purpose, owner, data and delegated authority helps organizations enforce their policies before consequential actions occur and reconstruct what happened during investigations, containment, recovery and audits. That evidence should stay with organizations when models and providers change, and organizations should retain control over what data their agents can access and how that access is governed, regardless of the model or provider.

Microsoft and industry leaders will share insights at Microsoft Ignite on how organizations can manage AI models and agents with confidence. More is available on the Microsoft Security blog, and press can contact Microsoft Media Relations, We. Communications for Microsoft, at (425) 638-7777. The articles leave open what the open standards will contain and when the work will reach Microsoft AI, Microsoft Foundry and Microsoft Copilot.

stories.Headline: IBM study finds only 18% of chief AI officers control AI investment decisions
stories.Summary:
The IBM Institute for Business Value published a study on November 17, 2026, dated from Armonk, New York, finding that only 18% of surveyed Chief AI Officers have full control over AI investment decisions. The global study surveyed more than 1,600 Chief AI Officers and equivalent enterprise AI leaders. It was conducted in cooperation with Oxford Economics, which surveyed 1,667 senior executives responsible for enterprise AI strategy, governance, implementation, and value realization. Those surveyed included Chief AI Officers, Chief Data and AI Officers, Heads of AI, and equivalent AI leaders, whom the study refers to collectively as CAIOs. The survey ran from April to June 2026 across 33 geographies and 20 industries.

Just 29% of respondents say their organizations adjust decisions and resources quickly when AI performance insights identify opportunities to improve outcomes. Fewer than one-third of surveyed CAIOs say AI is reshaping the business model, including what the organization sells, how it prices, or how it captures value. While only 32% say AI is reshaping the business model, 35% say it primarily strengthens the existing model, and 26% expect it to reshape the model but have not made the necessary shifts. 48% of CAIOs say AI agents initiate and execute actions across workflows, yet 75% say governance, risk or compliance delays AI-driven action. While 73% of respondents have defined where human oversight is non-negotiable, only 61% say AI decision rights are clearly defined and consistently applied.

Joanne Wright, Senior Vice President, Transformation and Operations at IBM, writes in the study's foreword that few leaders have a broader view of how AI is creating value across the enterprise. She writes that the outcomes Chief AI Officers are accountable for often depend on decisions made by others. She says successful AI leadership requires more than technical expertise or operational oversight. She says it requires gathering evidence, influencing decisions, and measuring success. The study identifies a group of high-impact CAIOs whose organizations report stronger results.

High-impact CAIOs report that 63% of AI projects deliver measurable business outcomes, compared with 43% for all other CAIOs, and that 49% move from pilot to production, versus 33%. They scale successful initiatives enterprise-wide in eight months, compared with 13.5 months among all other CAIOs. High-impact CAIOs are nearly four times as likely to say they can quickly pause, adjust or redirect AI systems without disrupting operations, and 96% of them say AI-generated outputs can trigger actions autonomously, compared with 40% of all other CAIOs. Nearly all high-impact CAIOs say AI is embedded directly into workflows compared with 59% of all others, and 94% say they use business outcomes to determine which initiatives receive additional funding and talent and which do not. 96% of high-impact CAIOs say they stop or reduce investment in initiatives that fail to deliver, even when those initiatives have senior sponsorship, compared with 46% of others, and 95% say they reinvest AI-generated productivity gains in higher-value transformation, compared with 44% of other respondents.

Only 31% of all CAIOs say clear thresholds for stopping AI initiatives are critical to AI success, and 40% say decisions are discussed when performance insights reveal opportunities, but action is delayed. 71% of CAIOs believe their organizations risk falling behind competitors in AI transformation, and CAIOs rank workflows and business processes as the top priority for change. The findings link the stronger outcomes of high-impact CAIOs with differences in how their organizations manage AI autonomy and control, redesign business workflows, and make evidence-based investment decisions. Additional analysis examined organizational behaviors associated with stronger enterprise outcomes across governance, decision rights, workflow integration, operating-model design, value management, transformation execution, and business-model innovation. The IBM Institute for Business Value is IBM's thought leadership think tank, combining global research and performance data with expertise from industry thinkers and leading academics.

The full report is available at a link on IBM's website, and the media contact is Marisa Conway of IBM Corporate Communications. IBM describes itself as a leading provider of global hybrid cloud and AI and consulting expertise, helping clients in more than 175 countries. The articles do not say what organizations should do in response to the findings, beyond the report link. They do not give the names of any surveyed CAIOs or the identities of the high-impact group. They do not break the results down by geography or industry, though the survey covered 33 geographies and 20 industries.

stories.Headline: Fluke study finds 78 percent of data center operators hit electrical disruption in past year
stories.Summary:
Fluke Corporation published a study on November 17, 2026, finding that 78 percent of data center operators experienced electrical or power-system issues contributing to disruption, delays, downtime or serious near-misses in the past year. The study was announced from Everett, Washington, and distributed by GlobeNewswire. Fluke said the global race to build and expand AI data centers could face a major setback. The research raised questions about whether the infrastructure behind the AI boom can deliver on the industry's ambitious growth plans. Operators are racing to secure additional grid capacity while weaknesses inside data centers threaten to delay new AI workloads and disrupt existing operations.

Only 33 percent of operators say their electrical infrastructure is fully ready for higher-density AI workloads. 34 percent say electrical skills shortages have delayed infrastructure upgrades or new capacity. 29 percent say power-quality issues have reduced their ability to deploy or operate AI/GPU workloads. 29 percent report that electrical problems are only identified after performance or equipment failure, or downtime, has occurred. Fewer than half of operators, 45 percent, report real-time visibility across critical electrical systems.

Parker Burke, President of Fluke Corporation, said the industry has spent years asking where the power will come from. He said the findings show the focus should also be on how effectively data centers can use the power they already have. He said the electrical infrastructure inside data centers is becoming a critical bottleneck as AI drives unprecedented demand for computing capacity. He said that without addressing this last-mile challenge, the industry risks having the power to expand but not the infrastructure to deliver. Burke also said grid constraints are largely outside an operator's control, while what is within their control is how effectively they monitor, maintain and manage the electrical infrastructure they already have.

Six in ten operators, 60 percent, say recruiting qualified electrical technicians has become more difficult. Three-quarters of operators, 76 percent, say access to sufficient power and grid capacity is moderately or severely limiting their ability to expand. Operators report an average 12-month wait to secure additional grid connection or power capacity for AI and GPU-related expansion. The study was commissioned by Fluke on behalf of Censuswide and surveyed 1,300 data-center industry operators and professionals across six countries: the US, UK, Germany, France, India and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Censuswide is an international market research consultancy headquartered in London, with offices in New York, Dubai, Bristol and Glasgow.

Fluke Corporation was founded in 1948 and describes itself as the world leader in compact, professional electronic test tools and software for measuring and condition monitoring. Fluke customers are technicians, engineers, electricians, maintenance managers and metrologists who install, troubleshoot and maintain industrial, electrical and electronic equipment and calibration processes. The study examined the power, infrastructure and workforce challenges facing the industry as AI demand accelerates. The findings suggest the challenge is no longer simply securing power from the grid but ensuring data centers have the infrastructure and expertise to turn that power into reliable computing capacity. Burke said greater visibility into electrical systems and a proactive approach to maintenance will be increasingly important as operators look to maximize existing capacity, reduce disruption and support growing AI demand.

Fluke said data center operators can improve electrical reliability through regular electrical testing, power-quality monitoring, thermal inspections and preventive maintenance. Fluke said poor power quality can cause equipment malfunctions, overheating, unexpected shutdowns and downtime, and that voltage fluctuations, harmonics and electrical disturbances can affect the reliability of critical data center systems. Fluke said operators can help reduce the impact of electrical skills shortages by investing in technician training, standardized testing procedures and diagnostic tools that make electrical troubleshooting more efficient. Fluke said it provides electrical testing and measurement tools, power-quality analyzers, thermal imaging cameras and condition-monitoring solutions for data center environments. The articles leave open which specific operators or countries accounted for the reported issues and near-misses.

stories.Headline: Toobit launches SmartK and AI Trading Assistant for futures traders
stories.Summary:
Toobit, the global cryptocurrency exchange based in George Town in the Cayman Islands, announced on November 18, 2026 that it is showcasing two trading analysis tools available through Toobit Futures. The tools are called SmartK and AI Trading Assistant, and the company says they help traders assess market conditions, explore trading opportunities and plan potential positions. SmartK focuses on chart-based technical analysis, while AI Trading Assistant provides AI-generated market insights and structured trade references. Both tools are designed to complement traders' existing analytical approaches rather than replace them.

SmartK features five proprietary indicators covering market signals, entry scoring, multi-timeframe positioning, volume-price relationships and momentum divergence. Traders can pair main-chart and lower-panel indicators to compare technical signals, examine price trends and assess potential entry conditions. AI Trading Assistant offers AI crypto market analysis and AI trading opportunities, providing potential trade setups for scalp and swing trading. Its analysis includes directional signals, entry zones, take-profit targets, stop-loss levels and adjustable risk-to-reward ratios to support trade planning and risk assessment. Both offerings support independent trading decisions, allowing traders to incorporate technical analysis and AI-generated insights into their existing strategies while retaining control over their trades.

Toobit describes itself as an award-winning cryptocurrency derivatives exchange that provides zero-fee spot trading, AI trading tools and high leverage for both crypto and TradFi markets. The company says it maintains a fair, secure and transparent environment for traders to navigate digital asset markets. The announcement cites eToro's September 2026 Retail Investor Beat, which surveyed 11,000 retail investors across 13 countries, finding that 56% already use or are open to using AI tools to select or adjust investments. stories.Headline: Africa Tech Festival opens in Cape Town to advance AI development across the continent
stories.Summary:
The Africa Tech Festival 2026 officially opened on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, in Cape Town, South Africa, to advance digital transformation. This event focuses on positioning the African continent to seize various opportunities that arise in the current age of artificial intelligence. Organizers brought together leaders from the technology and telecommunications industries, along with investors, policymakers, entrepreneurs, and innovators, to explore emerging technologies. These participants gathered to foster new partnerships and advance digital development across the continent during this influential and large technology event. The festival aims to help Africa move from being a consumer of foreign solutions to a developer of its own technologies.

The 29th edition of the festival runs through Thursday at the Cape Town International Convention Centre under the theme Powering Africa's Digital Transformation. More than 13,500 attendees and 2,000 companies from over 130 countries joined more than 450 speakers and 350 exhibitors at the venue. Six content pillars guide the event, including Data Centers, Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Startups, Digital Transformation, and Telecoms and Connectivity, for all participants. The schedule includes keynote speeches, panel discussions, technical masterclasses, investment forums, roundtables, networking opportunities, and specialist industry sessions for the attending guests. An exhibition also features various startups and providers of AI solutions from across the telecommunications and technology sectors for the attendees.

South African Deputy President Paul Mashatile delivered a virtual opening address where he urged African countries to shape the global AI landscape. He stated that the continent must become an exporter of emerging technologies instead of remaining a consumer of solutions developed elsewhere. Mashatile argued that digital transformation is fundamentally about human development and must be inclusive and people-centered to ensure a prosperous future. He called for active participation in developing and governing these technologies to ensure they advance the developmental goals of the continent. The Deputy President also urged African countries to build their own capabilities by drawing on local talent to solve regional challenges.

Mashatile warned that millions of people could be left behind due to infrastructure gaps, skills shortages, and high connectivity costs. He noted that inadequate broadband access remains a significant barrier that must be addressed to make digital transformation truly inclusive for all. The Deputy President highlighted the African Continental Free Trade Area as a key opportunity to establish a single digital market across Africa. He argued that closer regional integration would help drive inclusive growth, investment, and innovation through harmonized regulations and stronger cross-border collaboration. To realize this, he said the continent must enable interoperable payment systems and trusted data flows between the different African nations.

The articles describe the Africa Tech Festival as one of the largest and most influential technology events currently held on the continent. This event covers key areas ranging from entrepreneurship and digital infrastructure to the growth of the broader African digital economy. Mashatile outlined five priorities, including investing in human capital, building future-ready infrastructure, and strengthening the innovation ecosystems found across the continent. He also emphasized the need for responsible digital governance and cybersecurity to build trust while deepening regional integration and continental cooperation. These priorities are intended to translate the digital potential of the continent into broad-based prosperity for all of its people.

The festival will continue through Thursday with various sessions designed to turn high-level discussions into tangible progress for the African people. Mashatile called for bold investment, decisive action, and stronger partnerships to build a more connected, competitive, and inclusive future for generations. He believes Africa will compete in the age of AI by creating solutions with global relevance rather than through simple imitation. The articles leave open how specific countries will implement these five priorities or how the single digital market will be established. They do not state which specific companies are exhibiting or provide the exact outcomes of the various investment forums and roundtables.

stories.Headline: Nvidia pledges disciplined support for AI infrastructure and raises fiscal 2028 sales forecasts
stories.Summary:
Nvidia announced on Tuesday that it will continue supporting AI infrastructure through investments and credit guarantees. The company reported third quarter results that beat expectations and raised its fiscal 2028 sales forecast. This news eased investor concerns following the recent exit of former CEO Jensen Huang from the firm. Neocloud and chip stocks rallied after the company disclosed its plans for selective and disciplined support. Nvidia stock rose 1.2 percent in overnight trading following the release of the quarterly financial report.

The company disclosed 32 billion dollars in neocloud commitments, which is down from 36 billion in Q2. Total guarantees reached 118 billion dollars, while 390 billion dollars were committed toward future supply and capacity. Revenue for the third quarter more than doubled to 115.8 billion dollars, beating expectations of 109.3 billion dollars. Data center sales rose 110 percent to 107.6 billion dollars, and current quarter revenue is forecast at 130 billion. Fiscal 2028 revenue growth forecasts were raised from 70 percent to 75 percent by interim CEO Colette Kress.

Interim CEO Colette Kress stated that neocloud operators are an important part of the global AI infrastructure chain. She explained that credit backstops only activate if partners can successfully build and deliver the necessary computing infrastructure. Kress noted that the company remains thoughtful and disciplined regarding how it commits capital to the AI ecosystem. She added that Nvidia is rigorously evaluating future investments as the market matures and more capital sources become available. Kress emphasized that neoclouds provide more customers with access to compute and expand the reach of the platform.

Analyst Daniel Newman called neoclouds the biggest sustained bet for Nvidia to create an ecosystem of powered hyperscalers. Wharton professor Mohamed A. El-Erian noted that the earnings highlight Nvidia's expanding role as a major AI creditor. Hedge fund manager Eric Jackson said the push into physical infrastructure for AI compute was the earnings highlight. Nebius and IREN rose over 10 percent, while CoreWeave gained 9 percent and Marvell Technology gained 5.7 percent. Arista Networks rose 3.7 percent, and chip heavyweights Intel, AMD, Micron, and Broadcom rose between 2.7 and 4.7 percent.

The company recently cut ties with 63 year old co founder Jensen Huang following a scandal involving extramarital affairs. One of these affairs allegedly involved a woman who is a Chinese spy, leading to his sudden departure. Huang previously played a central role in the deals that made Nvidia a de facto financier of AI infrastructure. The uptick in supply commitments was primarily related to the multiyear procurement of memory supply for the company. Shares of Nvidia had fallen 16.5 percent year to date as of the most recent market close.

Chairman Harvey C. Jones stated on an analyst call that Nvidia is not considering reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. The iShares Semiconductor ETF rose 3.8 percent as retail sentiment on Stocktwits climbed into the extremely bullish zone. One trader suggested that Elon Musk should act soon if he wants to buy shares of the company Nebius. The articles do not state when the current quarter ends or the specific dates for fiscal 2028 targets. It remains open whether other capital sources will reduce the need for Nvidia to provide these credit guarantees.

stories.Headline: ROBOTERA deploys humanoid robots across China Post network in Guangdong to tackle labor shortages
stories.Summary:
Beijing Xingdongjiyuan Technology Co., Ltd., known as ROBOTERA, deployed humanoid robots across the China Post Group Guangdong Branch network on November 17, 2026. This initiative represents the most geographically extensive use of embodied intelligence robots within the logistics sector to date. The rollout covers 11 postal hubs located in eight different cities throughout Guangdong Province. These cities include Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Dongguan, Jiangmen, Shantou, Shanwei, Jieyang, and Heyuan.

The project requires these robots to handle high-volume sorting and cross-regional logistics coordination in a demanding environment. Since a pilot began at the Guangzhou Postal District Center in March 2026, the robots have processed over 1,500 parcels per hour. The system utilizes a self-developed five-finger dexterous hand for flexible handling and adaptive speed control to prevent collisions. These technical changes allow the robots to reject irregular items and operate under various power options for continuous service.

ROBOTERA and the China Post Group Guangdong Branch are jointly responsible for implementing this large-scale industrial productivity project. The company stated that their robots fill capacity gaps by performing strenuous frontline tasks during peak shopping seasons. This shift allows human employees to move into higher-value roles such as quality control, operations coordination, and robot maintenance. ROBOTERA explained that they use an AI-native, full-stack technology approach to develop these general-purpose humanoid systems.

Guangdong serves as a critical testing ground because it is the largest province in China by express parcel volume. The region faces persistent labor shortages and high workforce turnover, which makes automated sorting essential for stable operations. Beyond this province, the integrated solution has already been deployed across various postal operations in East China. ROBOTERA intends to continue working with industry partners to integrate embodied intelligence into more real-world industrial workflows.

stories.Headline: Upstage and Cohere partner to build sovereign AI solutions for enterprises
stories.Summary:
The South Korean artificial intelligence startup Upstage announced a strategic collaboration with the Canadian firm Cohere on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. These two companies signed a partnership agreement on November 16, 2026, at the Seoul office of Upstage to develop sovereign AI solutions. This joint effort aims to help both organizations expand their presence within the global enterprise AI market. They intend to provide specialized services for businesses and institutions that must follow strict regulatory requirements.

The partnership requires the integration of the Solar Pro and Solar Mini large language models from Upstage with the North enterprise AI agent platform from Cohere. Upstage will also include its Document Parse processing platform to enhance the combined technical capabilities of the new solution. These services will be available through cloud-based virtual private clouds or via systems installed locally for maximum security. This approach allows organizations to maintain complete control over their own data while utilizing advanced AI tools.

Upstage CEO Kim Sung-hoon, Cohere co-founder and CEO Aidan Gomez, and Cohere Asia-Pacific President Chang Hwa-jin are the leaders responsible for this agreement. While the articles do not provide direct quotes, the executives indicated that the collaboration focuses on security-focused enterprise clients. They expressed a shared goal of providing sovereign AI solutions that prioritize data privacy and institutional security. The leadership team believes this integration will better serve the needs of high-security corporate environments.

The companies plan to move beyond the South Korean market to expand their partnership across the broader Asia-Pacific region. This expansion will focus on delivering enterprise AI solutions that allow various organizations to keep their sensitive data secure. By targeting this region, the firms hope to establish a strong foothold in the growing demand for sovereign AI. They will continue to develop tools that balance high-performance artificial intelligence with strict data sovereignty.

stories.Headline: Google Project Zero cuts vulnerability disclosure to 90 days as AI speeds attacks
stories.Summary:
Google's Project Zero team of security researchers announced on 16th November 2026 that it has replaced its long-standing "90 + 30" disclosure policy with a new approach it calls "Full X", under which a vulnerability is made public X days after it is reported to the vendor. As of 13th November, X stands at 90 days, meaning the extra 30 days of soak time that previously let patches reach users before technical details became public has now been removed entirely. The team said the change is needed because large language models now let attackers find vulnerabilities more efficiently and make it more likely that several parties will discover the same flaw independently. Project Zero said it is now finding several vulnerabilities a week in targets where it once found only a few a year, which has made the old system of negotiating with vendors increasingly unmanageable.

The policy sets out two further reductions on fixed dates, with X dropping to 60 days on 2nd February 2027 and the policy moving to "Full 30" on 3rd January 2028, when vulnerabilities will be disclosed just 30 days after reporting. The team also said AI has cut the time needed to reverse-engineer a patch and work out which vulnerability it fixes, adding that patch soak time is no longer meaningful when attackers can almost immediately determine bug details from a patch. Security researcher Marcus Hutchins said on X that he understands what Google is trying to do but does not agree with it at all. He said the number of CVEs found in 2026 is double that of 2025, so security fixers face double the workload while getting two thirds of the time to do it, and he warned that at some point the dam is going to break.

Ivan Milenkovic, vice president of risk technology at security vendor Qualys, said vendors will object and some have already warned Google that tight deadlines push them to fix the reported bug ahead of a more severe one, which he called a fair response, though he said the alternative was letting attackers set the deadline. He described the previous 30-day soak time as a comfort blanket that is now being removed, and warned that saying "we patch monthly" now means an organisation is slower than disclosure. He advised organisations to focus on the half-life of vulnerabilities as a key metric, saying boards should stop asking how many critical vulnerabilities they have and instead ask how many days a fixed bug stays unfixed in their estate. The articles do not say what further action Google, vendors or regulators will take beyond the scheduled reductions in 2027 and 2028.

stories.Headline: Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang posts AI video of Sam Altman in a furry suit to promote Muse
stories.Summary:
Earlier in November, Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, shared a short AI-generated clip on Instagram to promote Muse, the company’s consumer AI agent. In the clip, Wang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Jolly, the anthropomorphic mascot of Muse, appear together on a four-way video call. When Altman joins the call, he is dressed like Jolly, wearing a furry hooded suit and face paint meant to make him look like the cutesy character. The clip carries the caption “When the homies meet about openai product strategy,” a reference to the AI agent race and the recent popularity of Muse. Meta requires AI-generated videos that depict people to be labeled as AI, and Wang’s post carries such a label.

Static images, however, have no such requirement, which meant an AI-generated image of actress Mia Goth that gained traction in October had no disclosure at all. That image was shared by a fan account holding a blue verification badge given by Instagram, and Goth’s representative told The Verge it was “incomprehensible” that Instagram allowed the image to spread rather than focusing on the protection and integrity of a public figure’s likeness. Other celebrities, including Scarlett Johansson, are regularly the subject of sexualized AI imagery, and Meta has removed some accounts in the past that it found to be posing as someone else and using their likeness. Meta spokesperson Tracy Clayton, reached for comment, noted that Wang’s post is labeled as AI content. Clayton also pointed out that Altman has made his likeness available for AI content generation, as when OpenAI launched its Sora app and it was quickly flooded with fake Altman videos.

OpenAI did not respond to requests for comment. Wang has been doing a lot of what some have described as “anti-PR” to promote Muse, tweeting hundreds of times and referring to more traditional marketers as “corposlops.” Just a few years ago, AI content portraying real people led to strong public statements rebuking the use of the technology to imitate humans, and in some cases legal action was threatened. Now that content has become part of the texture of a new reality, especially on social media, and ahead of the midterm elections political groups ran millions of dollars’ worth of AI-generated ads attacking opponents. A major tech executive posting an AI video of a competitor is still notable, especially on a platform that has been criticized recently over AI-generated content.

stories.Headline: Apollo Hospitals' AI agent helps clinicians review adverse events and close over 60% of cases within three days
stories.Summary:
Dr. Rohini Sridhar, chief of medical services at Apollo Hospitals, led the daily review of adverse events at 1 p.m. on a Wednesday in Chennai. She and the clinical governance team analyze incidents such as falls, medication errors and readmissions to find why they happened. The Daily Tiered Huddle agent, an AI solution, assists them in guarding patient safety. It was developed with Microsoft Frontier Company's forward-deployed engineers using Microsoft Foundry.

The agent reads hospital data collected in Microsoft Fabric and flags patient-care incidents requiring review based on set parameters. The agent summarizes incidents, prompts clinicians for further information and suggests case assessments using Microsoft Work IQ. About 600 adverse events are reported monthly across Apollo's 55 main hospitals. Since rollout, over 60% of cases reviewed by the huddle are closed within three days. Dr. Sridhar said only the 40% are actually relevant for a deeper dive.

The number of patient falls and medication errors dropped over July to September this year compared to the same quarter in 2025. Dr. Sridhar said processing 600 cases per month with incomplete data and reaching a meaningful decision is difficult. She said they now have the data required to make an analysis. She said the team can intervene early, propose solutions and proceed toward prevention. She credited the FDEs, who were deeply immersed in the doctors' daily processes.

She said they devised a tool to draw in data from wherever it sits on Fabric and did it faster than she thought possible. James Edwards, one of four FDEs on the project, said he enjoys discovery with the customer and understanding what problems they face. He said the team brings technical expertise on what is possible at the cutting edge with AI. Ashokkan Somuveerappan, Apollo's chief information officer, said the FDEs were more glued to the outcome they needed to achieve.

Juliet Joji Varghese, Apollo's director of nursing in Chennai, said staff are ready to answer leadership's questions because the AI generated questions to help them prepare. She said they are learning from what happened at other Apollo hospitals. A year ago, Dr. Sridhar would have waited hours or days while answers were gathered manually from various records. Engineers used synthetic data for evaluations and testing, not Apollo's electronic health records.

The agent writes information back into Fabric, stored in accordance with the hospital's data-handling standards. This continuous learning loop is referred to as hill-climbing in AI. Somuveerappan said the number of times questions and recommendations are edited measures the accuracy of the DTH agent. The agent's cluster analysis is still a work in progress, and it flagged a cluster of central line-related infections in the bone marrow transplant unit.

Dr. Sridhar cited an almost 30 percent improvement in staff satisfaction in Apollo's annual safety culture survey this year. She hopes to apply the agent to tumor board review and doctor handovers. She also wants to use AI to predict what is likely to happen to a patient from admission and flag deviations from treatment pathways. She said the best organizations will focus on near-miss events and identify them before they occur.

stories.Headline: Anthropic likely prices IPO above $70 to $78 range and plans Nasdaq listing under ANT
stories.Summary:
Anthropic is likely to price its initial public offering above the current range of $70 to $78 per share, according to multiple sources who spoke to CNBC's David Faber on Tuesday. The artificial intelligence company plans to close its order books and lock in total demand at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, the people said, asking not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly. Anthropic is slated to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT" and to start trading on Nov. 19. If the offering proceeds as planned, the company will debut roughly five months after SpaceX went public in a record offering that raised $85.7 billion.

For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Anthropic said it generated $33.24 billion in revenue, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year, according to its prospectus. It reported a $104 billion net loss during that nine-month period, though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities, and it lost $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025. The prospectus included more than 90 pages of risk factors for investors to consider ahead of the listing. A group of researchers including CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after defecting from OpenAI, now its chief rival, and Anthropic is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude. Amodei said in Anthropic's roadshow video that if the company does this right, it can create an age of miracles where humanity is able to solve problems that have eluded it for millennia.

He said the company has to make sure that all the risks and all the ways things can go wrong with the technology are very carefully addressed as it brings the benefits and has a viable business at the same time. He also invited viewers to join the company on the next phase of this journey. Anthropic has long worked to establish a reputation as a safety-conscious AI company, and it underwent a period of explosive growth in 2026, driven largely by the popularity of its AI coding tool, Claude Code. Anthropic is facing a public market that has grown increasingly skeptical of the AI trade, as well as mounting and widespread antipathy toward the technology in the United States. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the planned closing of the order books on Tuesday and the start of trading on Nov. 19.

stories.Headline: Donald Trump Jr. says investors underestimated political pushback to AI
stories.Summary:
Donald Trump Jr. said in an interview at Axios' annual BFD summit in New York that investors had underestimated the political pushback to the AI ecosystem, speaking with Axios Pro Rata author Dan Primack on Tuesday. He appeared alongside Omeed Malik, co-founder of 1789 Capital, the venture firm Trump Jr. joined in 2024 and which has since grown from overseeing a few hundred million dollars to billions. Trump Jr. asserted that a lot of the pushback is manufactured, but he added that this does not mean it is not real. He said some founders of the biggest AI companies have probably not done themselves the best service as a marketing department, calling them probably not the best messengers when they say AI will rule the world and people should be thrilled.

The 2026 midterms reflected deep distrust of the AI race, with voters approving dozens of moratoriums on data centers, which President Trump rallied around. Asked whether investors, peers or the pair themselves underestimated the populist pushback to AI, Trump Jr. said he thought they saw that very clearly. He likened AI to any great innovation but said it will take some time for people to learn how to adapt it into their regular lives. Trump Jr. agreed that rage toward data centers represents a broader concern over growing AI influence.

That public anger is becoming key to candidates, and Democrats in six early 2028 primary states expect their presidential nominee to prioritize AI regulations, according to new polling data first reported by Axios' Maria Curi. Ahead of the midterms, Republicans took note of the sagging views of the data centers needed to power the AI boom, and while Trump has prioritized self-regulation for the industry, the November results raise questions about how Republicans will tackle the tech moving forward. Asked if there was anything Democrats and the White House could agree on after a November shellacking that could be good for business, Trump Jr. said they have got to focus on costs and inflation. He argued that the second Democrats win it is about investigations, which Trump Jr. could find himself targeted by.

stories.Headline: Microsoft AI launches MAI Image 2.7 editing models near top of leaderboards
stories.Summary:
Microsoft AI launched two MAI Image 2.7 models built for image editing on October 27, 2026, as a preview, and the pair arrived near the top of the industry scoreboards. The launch post describes the models as ranking among the best image-editing systems available, at lower prices, and the release has one job, which is improving pictures that already exist rather than generating new ones from text prompts. On Artificial Analysis's AA-Image-Editing v2.1 leaderboard, MAI Image 2.7 scored 1,193 Elo, which places it at second directly behind OpenAI's GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst, which leads with 1,199 Elo. The model also landed at third on Arena Edit, another editing leaderboard, and that result pushed Microsoft AI to the second spot overall among labs in that ranking.

The upgrade over MAI Image 2.6, which shipped in August 2026, is broad, and according to the Artificial Analysis tracking the new model improved across all ten use cases and all seven editing actions the platform measures. On the main AA leaderboard, the score for MAI Image 2.7 is a 42-point gain over its predecessor, and two specific categories saw especially big jumps. Composition and framing improved by 57 Elo, which covers how well the model arranges subjects within an image, and text edits rose by 49 Elo. The model tops or leads in several categories, including scene and style editing, text and symbol edits, reasoning-based edits, and enhancement and restoration.

MAI Image 2.7 is currently available through MAI Playground, Arena and Artificial Analysis, which are mostly testing and comparison venues rather than production pipelines. Specific details on API access and pricing have not been disclosed, and that creates a slight tension with the lower-price framing in the launch post, since businesses cannot yet put the cost claim to work in their own budgets. The release is the latest step in a fast cadence, with Microsoft AI releasing MAI Image 2 in March 2026, followed by MAI Image 2.6 in August 2026, and now 2.7 in October. That makes three image model releases in roughly seven months.

stories.Headline: Meta launches Muse AI agent as US ad revenue growth reaches 31%
stories.Summary:
Baron Capital released its third-quarter 2026 investor letter for the Baron Durable Advantage Fund, and in it the firm reported that Meta Platforms contributed 1.30% to the fund's returns during that quarter, with Meta shares rising 28.8% over the period. The letter said Meta's second-quarter results showed the core advertising engine getting stronger, with U.S. advertising revenue growth accelerating to 31% as new AI ranking and recommendation models lifted conversions. It also noted that Advantage+, Meta's AI-driven advertising suite, passed $75 billion in annual revenue run-rate. Meta closed at $626.41 per share on November 16, 2026, with a market capitalization of $1.60 trillion, and the stock had pulled back 9.77% over the past month while remaining up 4.81% over the last 52 weeks.

The letter described a bigger catalyst in September with the launch of Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, which reached number one on the U.S. App Store within days. At its Meta Connect conference, the company introduced real-time voice, a Mac app with computer use, and commerce partners including Stripe, Shopify, PayPal, Walmart and Best Buy, so that Muse can complete purchases. Meta also brought Muse to its smart glasses and to Charm, a new handheld device. The fund said these moves strengthened Meta's positioning and added new potential avenues for monetization while improving its contextual understanding of users, which should further advance its ability to match the right ad to the right user at the right time.

Baron said it believes current earnings understate Meta's earnings power because the company invests ahead of revenue, and it retains strong conviction that Meta's data, compute, distribution and founder leadership will make it a leader in consumer AI. The firm also said it believes AI will remain a tailwind for Meta's core business, helping the company sustain a long duration of growth. The fund returned 2.2% in the quarter, in line with the S&P 500's 2.3%, and is up 5.7% year to date, trailing the index's 12.8%. The letter cited the Federal Reserve raising interest rates, the 10-year Treasury yield reaching its highest since 2002, Middle East developments, inflation, and the AI build-out and AI bubble debate as influences on market volatility.

stories.Headline: Microsoft releases Windows endpoint security platform and previews baseline protection
stories.Summary:
Microsoft announced Windows security changes at Ignite 2026 in a blog post by Dana Huang, Corporate Vice President, Windows Security, published on November 17, 2026. Huang wrote that attackers are using AI to find vulnerabilities, build exploits and scale campaigns faster than ever. She said the time between a weakness being discovered and being used against an organization is shrinking. She said devices configured securely and patched quickly remain one of the most effective defenses. She said Windows can help enforce identity and security controls on devices where people, apps and data intersect.

The Windows endpoint security platform is reaching general availability on Windows 11, reducing reliance on kernel drivers while preserving capabilities security solutions depend on. Windows baseline protection is now available in preview, bringing secure boot, virtualization-based security and memory integrity into a single, versioned security state. Baseline protection will appear in an updated Windows Settings experience. Windows is expanding post-quantum protection in the Windows TLS stack, including pure post-quantum key exchange and authentication. Microsoft is extending Intune and Windows Autopatch to eligible Windows Server scenarios, in preview.

Huang said the fundamentals matter more than ever in this environment. She said the security strategy for users and data must now extend to AI and agents as well. She said Windows provides a trusted foundation with Microsoft security and management solutions and tools like Agent 365. She said the investments extend work shared at Build 2026. She thanked the partners who joined the journey on the endpoint security platform.

Microsoft said Windows Hello improvements make passwordless sign-in more consistent and get users to their desktop faster. New observability gives IT greater insight into whether users authenticate using biometrics or PIN. Expanded Web sign-in brings passwordless access to more devices. Administrator protection helps users operate with standard permissions by default and elevate privileges when needed. Microsoft Execution Containers, announced last month, provide governed boundaries for agent execution.

Last year, Microsoft shared how Windows was working with security partners to evolve the platform to better integrate with the ecosystem while remaining resilient. The work sits alongside the Driver Quality Initiative and broader efforts to reduce kernel exposure and strengthen recovery. Baseline protection will continue to evolve as more security capabilities are added. The post-quantum investments are described as practical steps organizations can begin taking now while preparing for a multi-year transition across applications, infrastructure and identity. Intune and Autopatch on Windows Server complement Azure Arc for cloud-native server management.

At Ignite, customers can explore the story through sessions including BRK405 on what's new in Windows security, BRK398 on building a more resilient Windows estate and BRK392 on preparing apps for evolving Windows security standards. Microsoft pointed readers to the Windows Security Guide and Microsoft Learn for practical guidance. The post did not give a general availability date for baseline protection beyond its preview status. It did not name the partners collaborating on the endpoint security platform. It did not say when the post-quantum TLS capabilities would ship.

stories.Headline: UBS analyst Karl Keirstead starts Meta coverage with a Buy rating and $815 target
stories.Summary:
UBS analyst Karl Keirstead assumed coverage of Meta Platforms on November 17, 2026, with a Buy rating and an $815 price target that implies roughly 30% upside from the stock's Monday close. He argued that enthusiasm around Meta's Muse AI models and Meta Business Agents could offset investor worries about rising spending and financing needs. Keirstead said Meta trades at about 20 times estimated 2027 GAAP earnings per share, a valuation he called attractive given recent progress in AI models and applications. He described CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Meta's leadership as building what he called an AI maximalist version of Meta after a significant overhaul of its AI strategy over the past 18 months.

Meta's third-quarter revenue rose 26% year over year to $64.6 billion, helped by a 10% increase in advertising impressions and a 14% rise in average advertising prices. Capital expenditures in the quarter reached $34.91 billion, and quarterly free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion. The company expects fiscal 2026 capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion, narrowing its earlier forecast of $130 billion to $145 billion. Management said it expects to keep investing aggressively in its core business and emerging AI initiatives in 2027, though it has not given a full-year revenue forecast.

Keirstead said UBS would focus mainly on the development and training of the Muse AI models, the rollout of Meta's personal AI agent and the expansion of business and enterprise applications. The firm will also examine the computing infrastructure needed to support these efforts, including its scale and associated costs. UBS said its coverage of cloud infrastructure providers, including Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Oracle and CoreWeave, would inform its analysis of Meta's AI investments. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits remained bearish on November 17, and Meta shares have fallen nearly 4% so far this year, while the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF has risen over 2% in the same period.

stories.Headline: Meta expands content protection to Instagram and adds spoken word matching to detect AI copies
stories.Summary:
Meta is expanding its content protection feature from Facebook to Instagram in an effort to reduce unauthorized copying of creators' original Reels through reposting and AI generation, according to the company's announcement. The tool automatically looks out for visual matches to creators' original videos and sends a notification when a match is found across Instagram and Facebook. Creators who receive a match have four options, which are to keep monitoring the post, make the post no longer viewable to other users, add an "original by" label linking viewers back to the creator's initial video, or allow the video to stay up. Meta said it has heard growing concern about AI-generated content that uses elements of original work but may not visually match it, and it is starting to show videos in content protection that match the spoken words in an original video even when the visuals have been replaced by AI.

To become eligible for content protection, creators must meet Meta's originality and integrity requirements, the articles state. Meta initially launched content protection on Facebook in November 2025, and since then it has altered its recommendation algorithms across Facebook and Instagram feeds to prioritize original content. In March 2026, Meta updated its content guidelines, further defining original content as a post filmed or created by the publisher or production company, as new episodes, clips or trailers of a show posted by the producers, talent or network, or as an enhanced version of something previously posted. By expanding rights protections to Instagram and unauthorized AI-generated duplication, Meta is trying to give creators more ownership over their videos while cutting out more replicated, reused content a user might see in their feed.

Meta is responsible for the feature and described its purpose in its announcement, saying the company knows how frustrating it can be to see aggregators benefit from creators' work. The company said the tool automatically looks out for visual matches and notifies creators when a match appears across Instagram and Facebook. Meta also said it is beginning to incorporate relevant additions to the detection process, including matching spoken words even when visuals have been replaced by AI. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the expansion and the detection additions.

stories.Headline: BNY Mellon and Microsoft use AI agents to negotiate a Treasury trade
stories.Summary:
Bank of New York Mellon Corp. and Microsoft Corp. used artificial intelligence agents to negotiate a US Treasury trade on November 17, 2026. These automated systems haggled over a price independently before human employees provided the final approval for the transaction. This event is billed by both companies as the first trade of its kind involving AI agents. The process demonstrated that computers can now deliberate and search for middle ground during financial negotiations.

The trade required Microsoft's treasury department to provide an agent with specific boundaries for a satisfactory transaction. BNY implemented a control layer to ensure authorized agents negotiated while maintaining an overlay for mutual confirmation of terms. This system, called the Agentic Negotiation Protocol, allows agents to interact within strict guardrails defined by the bank. BNY intends to expand this technology into other capital market areas such as foreign-exchange payments and repo deals. They also plan to apply these automated workflows to collateral terms and various contractual negotiations.

Laide Majiyagbe, the global head of markets at BNY, stated that this represents the start of an important evolution in the market. She explained that while high-touch human brokerage will not disappear, AI can fill the space between electronic trading and human negotiation. Majiyagbe believes this technology could lower the barrier to entry for players who previously found human capital investments impractical. She noted that the agents currently engage in a level of polite discourse rarely seen on Wall Street desks.

This proof of concept shows that AI can move beyond simple algorithmic trading into the complex art of client grappling. Trading desks already use AI to parse unstructured data and adjust pricing, but this trade marks a shift toward autonomous deliberation. The industry must now determine if these agents can be scaled across different asset classes during treacherous market conditions. Future tests will focus on whether these automated lieutenants can maintain fairness and efficiency in more volatile environments.

stories.Headline: Credo beats estimates for an eighth quarter as analysts set a $204 target
stories.Summary:
Credo Technology has beaten earnings estimates for 8 straight quarters, yet its shares sank 32% in a month, and that gap between results and price drives a BUY rating and $204 target. The stock is down 32.3% over the past month, 0.39% over the past week and 5.5% year to date. It is 54% below its 52-week high of $308.67 and 64% off its low of $86.48. Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue reached $479 million, up 114.7% year over year, and non-GAAP EPS of $1.20 exceeded the $1.17 consensus. The stock fell after that report on concerns about customer concentration and valuation, then lost more ground in a broad AI infrastructure selloff in November.

The 24/7 Wall St. price target for Credo is $204.20, implying 44.4% upside from the $141.41 close, with a BUY recommendation at 90% confidence. Management guided Q2 revenue to $525M-$535M, with results due in early December. Management expects more than $600 million of optical revenue in fiscal 2027, total growth above 85% and a non-GAAP net margin in the vicinity of 50%. OmniConnect could add thousands of dollars of Credo content per GPU starting in fiscal 2028. Of 20 covering analysts, 19 rate the stock a buy or strong buy, and their consensus target of $284.05 is about 101% above where the stock trades now.

The bull case reaches $332.77, and the bear case is $166.29, below today's price. The main reason for the buy rating is valuation: about 20x forward earnings for a company more than doubling its revenue. The case gets stronger if December results confirm the optical growth and new customers, and weaker if one of the largest customers cuts orders. Stock-based compensation reached $87.98 million. GAAP gross margin guidance of 62.9%-64.9% trails the non-GAAP range of 67%-69%, mostly because of acquisition amortization, a non-cash charge tied to the photonics deal that brought in Credo's first PIC revenue.

In Q1, the four largest customers made up 33%, 28%, 13% and 10% of revenue, making order cuts from any big buyer the key risk. Astera Labs is Credo's closest pure-play rival, selling retimers and cable modules to hyperscalers while trading at a 184 trailing P/E. Astera Labs has a $40.36B market cap and 153.67% latest-quarter revenue growth, against Credo's $26.58B and 114.7%. Broadcom has a $1.65T market cap and 85.5% growth, and its AI semiconductor revenue rose 221%. Marvell has a $148.2B market cap and 36.55% growth, and its non-GAAP gross margin of 58.9% trails Credo's 68%.

The 24/7 Wall St. price targets are $137.57 for 2026, $213.51 for 2027, $248.86 for 2028, $318.63 for 2029 and $353.81 for 2030. The estimates rest on Credo continuing to execute its current strategy. Hyperscaler spending changes or a successful OmniConnect launch could move results well above or below this path. The article says the AI expansion runs on more than GPUs, and the power, cooling and connectivity suppliers behind it are the subject of a free report on seven AI infrastructure names that aren't chipmakers. Most AI attention goes to NVIDIA, but every GPU cluster also depends on the cables, optics and retimers that connect it.

The article was published by Vandita Jadeja on Tue, November 17, 2026 at 10:33 AM CST. Credo sells the connectivity layer, and the article calls the December results the test of the optical growth and new customers. The article leaves open whether one of the largest customers will cut orders. It leaves open whether hyperscaler spending changes or a successful OmniConnect launch moves results above or below the target path. stories.Headline: Microsoft launches MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash, pitching cost per task over raw benchmarks
stories.Summary:
Microsoft AI announced two enterprise coding models, MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash, on November 17, 2026, positioning them on cost per task rather than raw benchmark superiority over rival models. MAI Code 2 is aimed at production changes, deep debugging, multi-file implementation, repository-wide reasoning and user interfaces, while the Flash variant targets high-volume jobs such as explaining code, making targeted edits, applying routine fixes and iterating quickly. Microsoft reports that MAI Code 2 delivers 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40% of its cost and 96% of Claude Opus 5.5's performance at 5% of its cost across four benchmarks. The company states explicitly that neither model has yet been tuned for fundamental science research or very long-horizon agentic work, which defines the release's scope around everyday coding work. Across DeepSWE 1.1, Terminal-Bench 2.1, SWE Atlas and FrontierCode v1.1, Microsoft reports a 63.2% average pass rate and $0.309 average cost per task for MAI Code 2, against 64.1% at $0.761 for GPT-6.1 Sol and 65.3% at $6.306 for Claude Opus 5.5.

All models in the coding comparisons ran at maximum reasoning effort, the cost figures for Microsoft's models use a 50% promotional price, and the company cautions that changing the workload, model configuration, reasoning effort or pricing assumptions can change the comparisons. For MAI Code 2 Flash, Microsoft reports a 61.0% average pass rate and $0.052 average cost per task across DeepSWE 1.1, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE Atlas, compared with 55.1% at $0.080 for GPT-6 Luna and 53.9% at $0.319 for Claude Haiku 5.5. In separate blind frontend evaluations covering user interfaces, games, data visualizations, 3D scenes and SVG graphics, Microsoft reports that 258 annotators preferred MAI Code 2 over GPT-6 Sol 67% of the time on aesthetics and functionality. Both models are available in GitHub Copilot, and MAI Code 2 Flash is also in limited-access preview in Microsoft Foundry, with releases planned for OpenRouter, Vercel, Hermes, OpenCode and Kilo. Microsoft has further optimized Code 2 Flash into MAI Work Flash for use across Microsoft 365 and Fabric IQ, reporting comparable accuracy and token efficiency with GPT-6 Luna on internal Excel customer-scenario benchmarks and similar quality and token efficiency on frequent PowerPoint tasks.

In Teams evaluations, Microsoft reports higher scores than GPT-6 Luna for decision tracking and knowledge gaps, adapting custom instructions and tool calling, with up to 28% fewer tokens on instruction following and tool calling. For Power BI semantic models, Microsoft reports a 0.77 overall score for MAI Work Flash in offline DAX query-generation evaluations, compared with 0.54 for GPT-6 Astra, 0.45 for GPT-5.6 Sol and 0.30 for Opus 5.5. The release is therefore also a distribution release, since Copilot gets two coding options while a Flash derivative moves into spreadsheets, presentations, chat and analytics. The reported numbers make cost per task the main competitive lever, with promotional pricing and the deliberately narrow workload focus determining how far the comparisons extend. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the planned releases on OpenRouter, Vercel, Hermes, OpenCode and Kilo and the limited-access preview in Microsoft Foundry.

stories.Headline: Dale Gillham warns investors against buying the AI narrative as Nvidia shares fall 18 percent this year
stories.Summary:
Nvidia’s recent quarterly results beat market expectations, yet the company’s shares have fallen about 18 percent for the year, according to a Ticker News report published on 17 November 2026. The decline reflects a broader trend in the technology sector, which has been one of the worst performers on the S&P 500 this year. Dale Gillham of Wealth Within said investors should focus on the future value of companies like Nvidia rather than their current valuations. He argued that the market prices in future potential rather than present value, and he warned against buying on the AI narrative alone. Gillham noted that Apple and Microsoft have also performed poorly this year, while sectors such as pharmaceuticals and energy have posted substantial gains.

He compared the current AI enthusiasm to the lithium market, where hype did not match reality and prices fell despite increased battery use. He also said many big tech companies are spending more on AI than they earn, and he asked whether revenue is coming in fast enough to validate that spending. Security concerns are adding pressure, with some businesses, including the Commonwealth Bank, moving toward internal AI solutions to reduce hacking risks. Gillham advised investors to focus on established businesses with a track record of profitability and to weigh broader economic trends rather than the AI story.

He said the market prices future potential, not present value, and he urged a strategic approach that evaluates individual companies and market dynamics. The report does not say what Nvidia or its executives said in response, and it gives no further dates or figures beyond those above. It also does not say what happens next for the company or its shares. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Replit extends its platform with Microsoft technology for enterprise apps and agents
stories.Summary:
On 17 November 2026 Microsoft published a customer story saying Replit is extending its platform with Microsoft technology to help enterprise teams build applications, connect to governed business data and bring agents into everyday workflows. Replit is building the foundation for self-driving companies, in which people set goals and exercise judgment while agents carry more of the execution work. Replit's Horacio Lopez, Solutions Partner Program Lead, built a partner portal himself using Replit. The portal ran on Microsoft Azure and was connected to the company's customer relationship management system, along with a Solutions Partner directory and application process. Replit President Michele Catasta said AI is fundamentally changing who is becoming capable of creating software.

Replit adapted its architecture to support containerized applications and virtual machine workloads on Azure, with compute, storage and platform services that scale with an application. Identity, networking and organization-managed security capabilities help applications operate within an enterprise environment. Microsoft Foundry supports model orchestration, multi-agent workflows and AI inference, depending on the application's requirements. Using the Rayfin software development kit, Replit lets builders create applications around governed data in Microsoft Fabric without first moving the underlying business records into another data store. Replit uses information about the data's structure plus company-owned semantic metadata to help generate the application, while the SDK provides back-end scaffolding such as data models, authentication and access policies.

Catasta said that as Replit moved further into the enterprise, customers asked for more choice and control on where their applications are running and how they are running. He said Replit expanded to Azure to meet the needs of its enterprise customers while keeping the Replit experience at the center. Luis Héctor Chávez, Chief Technology Officer of Replit, said that for Replit to deploy to customers' cloud it had to essentially do a rearchitecture and rethink how it deploys software. Chávez said Replit's most security-conscious customers need their governed data to never escape Fabric. Lopez said work that might have taken months of an engineer's time took him just a few afternoon sessions, a tenfold to hundredfold shift in the time it takes to turn an idea into something useful.

Chávez described the opportunity as a zero-to-one shift, going beyond building software faster so that more people who understand a problem can begin solving it themselves. Replit's partnerships team had relied on a patchwork of tools that didn't fit the needs of the team or its partners. The team wanted a portal where partners could interact with Replit and track the deals they had referred. Lopez understood the partner experience, the sales process and what the portal needed to do, and he set the direction and evaluated the results, working with colleagues to refine what partners could see and do.

Replit is extending its accessible creation experience to applications while the data remains connected to the organization's Fabric environment. The story lists Replit as the customer, with Azure, Microsoft Foundry and Microsoft Fabric as the products, and gives its organization size as 50-999 employees. It gives the country or region as the United States, the business need as AI and Agents, and the industry as Software, Data and Platforms. Replit helps enterprises become self-driving companies, enabling teams to set goals and exercise judgment while agents carry more of the execution work.

Replit is extending that opportunity beyond the first build, connecting its creation experience with the infrastructure, AI capabilities and governed data that applications need in enterprise production. Replit is making it easier not only to create software but to put it to work inside an enterprise through agents, with team oversight. It says Replit is building the foundation for self-driving companies, where people define goals, exercise judgment and remain accountable while agents take on more execution and coordination. stories.Headline: Nvidia shares rise 4% after record revenue exceeds Wall Street expectations
stories.Summary:
Nvidia reported fiscal Q3 2027 results on November 17, 2026, which significantly exceeded Wall Street expectations. The company confirmed exceptionally strong demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure during this period. Shares initially surged nearly 4% following the release of these financial results. Revenue reached a record $115.8 billion, which increased more than 103% year over year. This total exceeded the analysts' consensus estimate of $109.33 billion.

The Data Center segment reached $107.6 billion, while Hyperscale revenue was $60.1 billion. AI Clouds, Industrial and Enterprise revenue hit $47.5 billion, and Edge Computing reached $8.2 billion. Adjusted earnings per share were $2.68, and net income hit a record $65.3 billion. Q4 revenue guidance is $130 billion, with operating expenses expected to be $10.7 billion. A new $150 billion share repurchase authorization increases remaining capacity to $227.3 billion.

Board chair Harvey Jones stated the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Jones said the board is proactively dealing with immediate consequences and enhancing oversight capacity. He declined to answer questions regarding Huang's resignation and the ongoing investigation. The company intends to use its repurchase program through fiscal 2028. This implies average buyback spending of $45.46 billion per quarter over five quarters.

Investors are focusing on the sustainability of profit margins and component costs. The US Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia, possibly regarding shareholder communications. Shareholders of record on December 2, 2026, will receive a $0.25 dividend on December 23. Customers beyond the largest cloud providers are now playing an increasingly important role. The company faces leadership uncertainty and rising expectations regarding returns on AI investments.

Nvidia generated $2.5 billion from Chinese entities, though it excludes these sales from forecasts. Purchase commitments rose to $390 billion, while cloud and lease commitments hit $102 billion. Maximum exposure under guarantees increased to $118 billion, including $105 billion for SB Energy. The company also disclosed $20 billion in equity investment commitments for AI laboratories. Free cash flow reached a record $43.8 billion, with $28.1 billion returned to shareholders.

Nvidia established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to improve regulator cooperation. The company will continue operating without its longtime leader in the near term.
