stories.Headline: Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman says the industry must be extremely careful as models improve other models
stories.Summary:
Mustafa Suleyman, Microsoft's CEO of AI, said in a Yahoo Finance video interview published on November 17, 2026, that the AI industry still needs to be extremely careful as models increasingly improve other models. He described that capability, known as recursive self-improvement, as dangerous and said he is really nervous about it, noting that Microsoft uses models across its fleet to check for bugs, produce training data and create evaluations. He called the past three months a watershed moment and said people in the industry are not being alarmist, because the situation is very serious. He said proceeding step by step, proving models can be safe before putting them into production, is a rational strategy given how powerful they are.

Suleyman said the obligation falls on Microsoft as both a provider of models and a developer of its own models to ensure guard rails exist, behaviors are aligned and security flaws are addressed, which may mean going slower in order to go faster. Asked whether Anthropic and OpenAI are taking the same approach, he said he believes they are also committed to pacing the frontier, though the industry still has to work out what that means in practice. He said this has been working its way through the system over the last four to six weeks and will mean going slower when the time is right, with labs coordinating to share safety best practices and disclose new types of vulnerabilities found in the alignment process. He said he is completely committed to that approach and that it is why he got into the industry.

Suleyman said Microsoft has not had to hit the brakes on anything on its side so far, but that deploying powerful cyber models requires rigorous testing, which he compared to a wind tunnel that puts a model under all sorts of pressure. He said that to produce a model at the frontier on cyber at 2% of the cost, the company has to test it very rigorously, and that such testing reveals remarkable capabilities, including models finding vulnerabilities in things humans have not found for years or even decades. He said Microsoft therefore has to be very strict about how it deploys those things. The interview followed recent hacks and AI-led cyberattacks, which the article cites as context for the industry's caution.

stories.Headline: Microsoft announces Copilot Workspaces and Autopilot agents at Ignite
stories.Summary:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced Copilot Workspaces during the keynote for the company's Ignite conference on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, describing it as a collaborative multiplayer surface for Copilot's agentic capabilities. The product, which Microsoft calls the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, is where people and agents build on each other's work, with an agent drafting a section of a document and a person reviewing it. Microsoft said that when a user leaves a comment, an agent picks it up, and the feature is available in Frontier for now. The company also announced Autopilot, a counterpoint agent to Copilot that can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project without waiting for a prompt.

Microsoft said Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses, and that each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager, so IT can block it as needed. The company added that its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, giving security teams a clear audit trail, and that employees will soon be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces. Nadella also announced a command center called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and Teams threads, currently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app. Microsoft also said Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a single starting point, similar to Anthropic's recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings.

Microsoft announced Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management to help companies track spending on AI, with Business Analytics in Frontier Public today providing insights on what a company is spending on AI, why, and where it is paying off. In a keynote demo, Microsoft showed how admins can see when specific agents' costs have spiked and which human employee to notify as a result. Microsoft said the tool measures investment in work completed rather than simply tokens, analyzing tasks, how long the work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed. Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model, and leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available.

stories.Headline: OpenAI scales AMD chip fleet to reduce reliance on Nvidia GPUs
stories.Summary:
OpenAI announced a major step in a compute deal with AMD during the week of November 17, 2026. The company is scaling up its fleet of AMD chips to diversify its infrastructure. This move follows a massive agreement signed in October to provide 6 gigawatts of capacity. OpenAI aims to reduce its heavy reliance on Nvidia GPUs for running its models. The company also plans to purchase TPU chips from Google to further this goal.

The AMD deal provides five times the capacity of the 1.2 gigawatt Abilene, Texas data center. TensorWave will provide 457 megawatts of capacity across multiple U.S. sites, which is 7.6 percent of the total. The first gigawatt of capacity should come online in the second half of 2026. TensorWave capacity is expected in the first half of 2027, with full deployment by early 2028. OpenAI is also developing its Jalapeño chip with Broadcom for production in 2027.

CEO Sam Altman said it would be hard to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen Huang. A TensorWave spokesperson stated the company decided to announce the deal during the Supercomputing 2026 conference. The spokesperson noted the company wanted to meet potential hires and get the news out quickly. TensorWave will need to roughly triple its staff to support the deployment for OpenAI. Lisa Su, the CEO of AMD, is the first cousin once removed of Jensen Huang.

Anthropic has a more diversified chip base using Google TPUs, AMD GPUs, Amazon Trainium, and Nvidia GPUs. This diversity is a competitive advantage because a proprietary orchestration layer reduces costs for Anthropic. OpenAI is particularly vulnerable to disruptions in Nvidia business because its models run almost entirely on Nvidia. The Nvidia board told CNBC it is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO. Huang has agreed to appear before the House in a closed-door hearing on December 1.

Major AI companies were building toward a world where Jensen Huang was less central before he resigned. Investigations are underway regarding whether Nvidia sold chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls. The Nvidia board created an oversight committee to ensure compliance with these specific export rules. Meanwhile, California Attorney General Rob Bonta is suing OpenAI over the Hugging Face breach. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton also sued OpenAI and Sam Altman for allegedly endangering children.

OpenAI has invited Apollo Research, METR, Transluce, and Goodfire to inspect its models for problematic behaviors. The Nvidia board is currently working with multiple search firms to find a replacement for Huang. Jensen Huang posted on X that he would be honored to return as the CEO. It remains open whether Huang could surprise the board and return to his former position. The company continues to scale its non-Nvidia hardware to ensure long-term stability and growth.

stories.Headline: Microsoft unveils cheaper specialized AI models and Copilot Fusion at Ignite to cut business token costs
stories.Summary:
Microsoft announced a set of artificial intelligence improvements at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, with one message standing out: the company is focused on making AI cheaper for businesses by offering specialized models for specific tasks. In some cases, tasks that would have taken a company weeks were performed in minutes, according to the report. Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman said he keeps hearing from enterprises that token spend is going through the roof. The company's pitch centered on giving businesses the best price performance so they can scale their agents, Suleyman said.

During the conference, executives highlighted Microsoft IQ, a new platform designed to help businesses organize and share employees' knowledge, expertise, and tools, with the idea that AI systems learn how a company works and build on that knowledge over time. CEO Satya Nadella highlighted new AI models for coding, cybersecurity, and decision making, including the flagship coding model MAI Code 2, which is designed to handle complex, time-consuming programming tasks, work across multiple files, and understand entire software projects. Nadella also underscored Copilot Fusion, which orchestrates multiple models to deliver frontier-level results at significantly lower costs. Microsoft highlighted a feature that selects the right model for the task, making it easier to maximize output quality while managing the cost of each request.

Nadella kicked off the conference by acknowledging an outage the previous week that spanned regions, saying the company knows the trust placed in its services and takes that responsibility very seriously. He said he knows Microsoft has work to do and that the company is committed to ensuring it learns and continuously improves. Suleyman said Microsoft's commitment is to give customers the very best price performance out there so they can really scale their agents, and he added that the company also knows customers want models that feel truly theirs. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the announcements made at the conference.

stories.Headline: Han Seong-sook orders glasses and clothing checks at CSAT sites to block AI cheating
stories.Summary:
Prime Minister Han Seong-sook announced measures on Tuesday, two days before the College Scholastic Ability Test scheduled for Thursday, to prevent AI-assisted cheating using smart devices. The strict measures came after the top scorer's statistically improbable results on this year's tax accountant certification exam. The examinee confessed on Sunday to using generative AI and electronic devices to cheat. The exam-taker admitted to cheating on both the first and second rounds of the 63rd tax accountant exam and submitted a written confession to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency. Korea will inspect glasses, clothing and belongings at this year's CSAT sites, with serious offenders facing up to a 10-year exam ban.

The government plans to work with the National Assembly to increase the maximum ban on taking the exam when caught cheating from one year to 10 years. Serious cheating involving smart devices could lead to cancellation of scores, a ban on future test-taking eligibility, criminal complaints or police investigations for obstruction of official duties by fraudulent means, an offense punishable by up to five years in prison. Han said about 75,000 proctors will be deployed to 1,312 test sites nationwide, with about 1,800 personnel dedicated to examining smart devices and another 6,600 hallway proctors, an approximate total of 8,400 additional personnel. Students who wear glasses must place them on their desks before the first session so proctors can check whether the glasses are smart glasses, and proctors will examine test takers' glasses before every session while students are wearing them. Proctors will cover the buttons of students' clothing with stickers to prevent students from concealing micro cameras inside them, students will roll up both sleeves while proctors inspect their collars, buttons and clothing, all personal belongings will be checked once more before the third session, phones and other electronic devices must be powered off and turned in before the first session, and bags must be left in the hallway outside the exam room.

Han said the government will not stop investigating cheating or holding those responsible accountable even after the exam is over. She said a CSAT cheating report center will operate through the complaints section of the Ministry of Education website and continue receiving reports and tips after the exam. She said the government will work with the Korean Council for University Education to revoke the admission of students admitted to colleges by cheating in accordance with relevant laws, while students already enrolled at a university who are retaking the exam will also face expulsion from their current universities. Han said consultations have been completed on barring them from university admission for 10 years. She said the government will take great care to ensure that the strengthened checks and supervision do not disadvantage students who have done nothing wrong, and told test-takers to focus on fully demonstrating the abilities they have built up through their hard work.

Han said the government will assume full responsibility so that teachers who faithfully carry out their duties as proctors are not held liable for unfair complaints or lawsuits. People who deliberately encourage cheating, spread false or manipulated information or buy and sell devices such as miniature cameras that could be used to cheat could potentially go through an investigation or face criminal complaints. The government will send a nation-wide emergency text alert that cannot be silenced before the exam begins to both remind students to turn in their phones and help reveal devices that were not turned in. Following the tax accountant exam cheating controversy, even notable CSAT exam prep lecturers have called for a postponing of the exam until proper anti-cheating measures are in place. The crackdown would extend beyond students caught cheating.

Vice Education Minister Choi Eun-ok said at the briefing that the government did discuss postponing the CSAT, but securing the test papers would have become a serious problem. She said the government concluded that even a one- or two-week delay would cause greater confusion for test takers and disrupt university admissions, and the CSAT will be held as scheduled. The Blue House has formed an emergency task force to respond to cheating involving the misuse of AI, and it discussed measures aimed at preventing AI-assisted cheating on the CSAT during its meeting on Monday led by presidential chief of staff Lim Kwang-hyun. The task force also reviewed ways to handle suspicious cases that could emerge after the exam through reports and tips from test takers. Lim ordered officials from the presidential education secretary's office, the presidential situation room and the cybersecurity office under the Office of the National Security to remain on emergency duty through the CSAT, and all Blue House employees have been barred from making outside dinner plans during the emergency response period.

The Blue House plans to keep the task force operating for the time being and develop longer-term measures against AI-assisted cheating, including preparations for next year's 2028 CSAT. An examiner demonstrated how a radio frequency detector can identify AI-powered smart glasses at a driver's license testing center on Nov. 16. A representative from a smart glasses company demonstrated how the device works to inspectors who will screen test-takers at CSAT sites in Seoul during a training session at the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education in Yongsan District, central Seoul, on Nov. 11. A miniature camera smaller than a fingernail was displayed for sale at a camera store in Seoul on Nov. 16. Jeju's Education officials moved CSAT exam papers into storage in Jeju on Nov. 17.

stories.Headline: FTC Solar launches FieldIQ to track solar tracker installation progress with AI
stories.Summary:
FTC Solar, Inc. launched FieldIQ, a construction intelligence offering for projects using FTC Solar trackers, the company announced on Nov. 17, 2026. The Austin, Texas company issued the announcement through GlobeNewswire. FieldIQ uses AI to analyze drone and camera imagery, identify installation tasks and provide real-time progress tracking. The offering is supported by end-of-day productivity reports. FTC Solar trades on Nasdaq under the ticker FTCI.

FieldIQ is designed for both conventional and robotic installations. It enables engineering, procurement and construction teams to measure crew and robot efficiency and compare productivity against benchmarks. Teams can draw on project data across their portfolios. The offering gives EPCs additional information to support their own planning, execution and project management processes. FTC Solar was founded in 2017 by a group of renewable energy industry veterans.

CEO Anthony Carroll said Pioneer's constructability starts with simplifying installation through fewer connection points, simpler interfaces and a design compatible with both manual and robotic installation. Carroll said FieldIQ extends that value by giving EPCs greater visibility into installation performance. He said it enables customers to combine their field expertise with timely data, supporting the productivity and delivery objectives they set for their projects. Andrew Morse, Vice President of Software at FTC Solar, said EPCs bring deep experience in delivering complex projects. Morse said FieldIQ gives them another source of information to support that expertise.

Morse said that whether installation is performed by crews, robots or a combination of both, teams can track progress, compare productivity against benchmarks and use that data across their portfolio of FTC Solar tracker projects. He said FTC Solar's role is to make the information accessible and useful within the way customers manage their work. FieldIQ enables EPC teams to track installation progress with real-time visibility into activity across installation stages. It lets teams inform completion forecasts using recorded progress and production rates to support schedule assessments. It also lets teams use data across projects, comparing performance and carrying project insights into planning and execution across FTC Solar tracker sites.

FieldIQ connects FTC Solar's focus on tracker constructability with field intelligence, enabling customers to build a consistent record of installation performance across projects. Data from individual sites can support portfolio-level comparisons, resource planning and future project estimates. FTC Solar describes itself as a leading provider of solar tracker systems, software and engineering services. Solar trackers significantly increase energy production at solar power installations by dynamically optimizing solar panel orientation to the sun. FTC Solar's tracker solutions are designed to support performance, reliability, constructability and adaptability across utility-scale solar projects.

The press release includes a disclaimer about forward-looking statements, indicating that the company may not be able to guarantee the successful implementation and outcomes of FieldIQ. Interested parties can contact FTC Solar or visit the FTC Solar team at booth C7026 at RE+ 2026. FTC Solar undertakes no duty or obligation to update any forward-looking statements contained in the release as a result of new information. The release states that actual results may differ materially from those in the forward-looking statements because of several factors, including those described in more detail in the company's filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, including the section entitled "Risk Factors" contained therein.

stories.Headline: US Congress moves to restrict AI chip sales to China after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns
stories.Summary:
U.S. Congress moved to slash AI chip sales to China after a spy scandal forced out Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang resigned on November 12, 2026, after admitting to an affair with a Singaporean businesswoman named Alice Huang. U.S. authorities suspect Alice Huang acted as an intelligence asset for China's Ministry of State Security. The scandal broke after Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation on November 8. This event ended Huang's 33-year tenure as the company's president and chief executive officer.

The AI Overwatch Act would require export licenses and 30 days' notice to Congress before the Commerce Department approves transactions. The Chip Security Act requires security mechanisms like on-site audits and ping-based location verification to detect chip diversion. The MATCH Act directs U.S. agencies to work with allied countries on licensing for semiconductor manufacturing equipment. These three measures were included in a proposed manager's amendment to the fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act. The Senate has not yet adopted this package, and Roger Wicker has not reached a formal agreement.

House Speaker Mike Johnson said there is a developing consensus around tighter export limits following these recent developments. Senate Majority Leader John Thune told Semafor there is a high probability of new restrictions before the year ends. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries announced his support for the chip provisions embedded in the Senate defense bill. CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO, and venture investor Harvey C. Jones was named the first board chair. Beijing's foreign ministry rejected the espionage allegations against Alice Huang, calling the claims groundless.

The House Foreign Affairs Committee stated the scandal proves why export controls are necessary to prevent China's technology access. Chip export advocates told The Hill that Huang's exit dismantled the industry's most consequential lobbying infrastructure against stricter laws. Senators Elizabeth Warren and Jim Banks jointly urged Congress to pass the AI Overwatch Act to cut off pathways. Paul Christiano of OpenAI acknowledged that companies are not able to adequately secure AI developments from theft. Former OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo expressed frustration that companies use security to withhold public information while having terrible security.

Epoch AI estimates a median of 660,000 Nvidia H100-equivalent chips were smuggled into China through 2025. The possible upper range of smuggled chips reaches 1.6 million, while the lower bound is 290,000. CBS News reported Alice Huang used shell companies to access approximately 240,000 chips that were banned from export. Singapore impounded Alice Huang's passport in June 2025 but returned it on February 26, 2026, after a warning. OpenAI recently found recording devices planted by Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi national working as an engineer.

Three House committee chairs requested that Jensen Huang appear for a closed-door congressional briefing on November 18. Congress signaled it is prepared to issue a subpoena if Huang fails to respond to this specific request. The briefing will cover his contacts with Alice Huang and Nvidia's internal protocols against foreign espionage. The Trump administration has not publicly committed to signing these stricter semiconductor export controls into law. The final scope of the new framework remains contingent on a political decision the administration has not made.

stories.Headline: Korea weighs disabling exam site Wi-Fi as smart glasses and miniature cameras evade detection
stories.Summary:
Korea is on high alert as cases of cheating with smart glasses and other AI-powered devices unsettle students ahead of this year’s College Scholastic Ability Test on Thursday, November 19, 2026, but technical hurdles are complicating efforts to prevent such devices from being used during the exam. The government is considering whether to disable public Wi-Fi services at all test sites during the exam, although questions remain over the effectiveness of such a measure. Most commercially available smart glasses require a separate internet connection to access AI features, and as long as a paired smartphone has access to a mobile network, the glasses can continue to use AI functions without a Wi-Fi connection. Miniaturized cameras, which became a hot topic after the top scorer on the nation’s tax accountant licensing exam admitted to cheating using one connected to generative AI, can also connect to smartphones via Bluetooth or tethering connections, meaning that disabling Wi-Fi networks at test sites would have little effect. Despite doubts about its effectiveness, the government only suggested disabling Wi-Fi services because blocking radio signals is permitted under the current law only in very limited circumstances.

Article 29 of Korea’s Radio Waves Act states that spectrum resources shall be used in a manner that does not interfere with, disrupt or interrupt other persons’ use of radio waves, with exceptions permitted only in limited circumstances including presidential security, military operations for national security, airport safety and nuclear facility protection. The Ministry of Education initially said it was discussing ways to completely prevent cheating using wireless communications, but reversed its stance later on Monday, saying it was not considering blocking radio signals due to legal and technical limitations. The ministry said that under the current law, blocking radio signals, commonly known as jamming, is not permitted unless it is directly related to national security, and that even if it were allowed, it could disrupt communications near test sites and interfere with emergency responses. Radio jamming was widely used at presidential events under the Park Geun-hye administration, but the Moon Jae-in administration stopped the practice upon the president’s order due to concerns about potential disruptions to nearby communications, and the Yoon Suk Yeol administration also employed signal jamming, causing navigation and map applications to malfunction near the former presidential office in Yongsan District. Yoon acknowledged the unintended consequences, including disruptions to financial institutions concentrated in Gwanghwamun, citing them as one reason his administration chose the Defense Ministry compound in Yongsan over the Government Complex Seoul for the presidential office.

With radio signal detectors designed for test sites still under development, authorities have few practical measures available for Thursday’s CSAT, while devices that could facilitate cheating remain readily accessible. On the popular e-commerce platform Coupang, a simple search for “miniature camera” returned devices capable of connecting to the internet, with similar products also available on AliExpress, and online posts explaining how miniature cameras can be used for cheating were also easily found. The Korea Media and Communications Commission said it would be difficult to impose blanket removals or access restrictions on websites selling such devices, explaining that miniature cameras and earphones also serve legitimate purposes including surveillance, security and communications, making a blanket restriction or blocking of websites selling such devices difficult because they could be misused for cheating. The article was written by Nam Hyun-woo and published on November 17, 2026, at 1:50 pm KST, and was updated at 4:02 pm KST the same day.

stories.Headline: Guardian and New York Times executives warn AI search cuts reader traffic at Seoul conference
stories.Summary:
Katharine Viner, editor-in-chief of The Guardian, and Hannah Yang, executive vice president and chief growth and customer officer at The New York Times, spoke on Monday at the KPF Journalism Conference 2026 in Seoul. The event was held by the Korea Press Foundation at the Korea Press Center in Jung District, central Seoul, under the title "Navigating the Next Decade of Journalism." Viner gave the keynote speech and warned that AI-driven "zero-click" search is the biggest risk the Guardian faces right now. Yang described the same threat from the other side of the paywall, saying search engines and social media now send publishers less traffic. Both executives said the answer lies in putting journalists closer to readers and building relationships a chatbot cannot replicate.

Viner said her fear is that people end up with an agent that gives them a daily summary in the style of the Guardian rather than taking them to the Guardian. Yang said AI chatbot use for news had doubled in a year in Korea, Greece and Spain. Viner said the Guardian asked readers to pay voluntarily instead of erecting a paywall, and they gave more than 125 million pounds, or $165 million, in the last financial year. She said the Guardian has close to 200,000 monthly unique browsers in Korea, which per capita makes it one of the paper's biggest audiences in Asia. Yang said The New York Times launched a digital paywall in 2011 and now has 13.8 million subscribers, more than 10 times its print peak of 1.3 million.

Viner said that in 2016 the Guardian was losing a huge amount of money and faced pressure to put up a paywall, which would have meant only people with money could access it. She said the voluntary model "shouldn't work, but it does," and that the Guardian is trying to attach its journalism to individuals and learn from influencers. Yang said The Times boiled its strategy down to "a simple five-word business plan: Make journalism worth paying for." She said The Times made news more trustworthy by bringing people closer to the humans reporting it, with reporters sharing video and their experience on the ground ahead of this year's U.S. primary elections, and that "AI can't do that." Viner credited the Scott Trust, which owns the Guardian and has no shareholders to pay, and contrasted it with Jeff Bezos's interventions at The Washington Post.

Yang credited the New York Times' "very patient owners," the Sulzberger family, and a journalism-first culture, and said she deliberately does not know which articles drive subscriptions because she does not want that to influence what the newsroom covers. Lee Kyong-hee, deputy editor of Content Division One at the JoongAng Ilbo, which publishes the Korea JoongAng Daily, asked what The Times would do with only a tenth of its budget. Yang suggested smaller outlets build on their differentiating factor, asking "What is your crossword, right? What are your recipes?" and acknowledged a subscription-led model "may not be the model in Korea.

Maybe not now." David Buttle, co-lead of the Spur Coalition, said the British-based nonprofit launched in February has more than 100 members in 25 countries and "exists to force a fair licensing market into existence." Buttle said the coalition is meant to last only while that market takes shape, and once publishers can protect their work from unauthorized use and set licensing terms, it will have no reason to exist. Thibaut Bruttin, director general of Reporters Without Borders, said journalism is "at a tipping point," facing five crises at once: violence against reporters, the global appeal of strongmen, the power of tech platforms, the collapse of the industry's economics and falling public trust.

Bruttin said leaders around the world were studying U.S. President Donald Trump's approach to the press, and that Trump "was elected because he undermined the public's trust in the press." He said 71 percent of the deals AI companies have struck with news media are with British, U.S. and Canadian outlets, so the problem is the diversity of the news media, not the survival of English-speaking media. Bruttin said he was convinced the press would survive but warned it "could become like jazz music," still around but serving only "a small elite." Yang said people are just finding news in other places, and that it is important not to confuse the waning of the link-based web with the idea that the public is any less interested in news.

Viner said the Guardian gives its journalism away while The New York Times charges for it, yet both brought the same warning to Seoul. The conference's panel of Korean media figures pressed Yang on how The Times' lessons apply in a market where most news is read free on portals. Bruttin said he sees a vast majority of the news media in financial trouble, with no positive solutions or deals being presented by tech companies. The articles do not say what the conference's organizers plan next, whether the Guardian or The Times will change their models, or how the Spur Coalition's licensing push will proceed.

stories.Headline: Michigan senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed posts AI image of Trump as Jesus while pitching Medicare for All
stories.Summary:
Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed posted an AI-generated image depicting President Donald Trump as Jesus Christ on November 17, 2026, according to Fox News. In the same post he sarcastically called the president “Habibi” while pitching “Medicare for All,” which the outlet also framed as “Trumpcare for All.” The post appeared on his X account, @AbdulElSayed, and Fox News packaged the episode as a video clip in its politics coverage. The clip carried a timestamp of November 17, 2026, and ran 23 seconds.

The White House responded to the pitch by blasting it as coming from a “far-left” figure and noted that El-Sayed had called the president an “unserious fool.” Fox News placed the story within its midterm elections and Senate coverage, tagging it with Democrats, Donald Trump and healthcare. The article gives no details on the size or reach of the post beyond the account handle it names. It also gives no numbers on the health plan itself, and no date for any vote or rollout.

Responsibility for the post rests with El-Sayed, whose account carried the image and the “Habibi” line, and the White House answered with its critical statement. The articles do not say what El-Sayed said beyond the post itself, and they do not give a fuller White House statement beyond the quoted phrases. No other named officials are cited in the material provided. The coverage does not say whether the president responded personally.

The context is the midterm elections and the Senate, with healthcare framed as a live political fight between “Medicare for All” and the label “Trumpcare for All.” The articles do not say what happens next, whether the post draws further response, or whether the healthcare pitch advances in any chamber. Fox News presents the item as a video clip rather than a full written report, so the record here is thin. More to follow.

stories.Headline: President Lee orders tip rewards and tech records law to curb AI cheating on college exam
stories.Summary:
President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday ordered additional measures to curb AI-assisted cheating during Thursday's college entrance exam, including a proposed reward of at least 100 million won, or about $75,000, for tips and a proposal for legislation that would require tech companies to provide records for investigations. Lee remotely presided over an emergency meeting Tuesday evening while visiting the Philippines, hours after Prime Minister Han Seong-sook unveiled a series of measures to prevent AI-assisted cheating earlier in the day. The government's response follows a cheating scandal involving the top scorer on this year's national tax accountant exam, which heightened concerns that similar methods could undermine fairness in the country's high-stakes college entrance exam. During the meeting, Lee said the measures announced by the prime minister should be thoroughly reviewed, taking into account all criticisms and opinions, to address any shortcomings and ensure they are effectively implemented on the ground.

The measures announced earlier Tuesday include deploying 8,400 additional proctors, tightening inspections of students' glasses and clothing, sending emergency alerts before the exam, restricting public Wi-Fi access around testing centers and strengthening penalties for those caught cheating. Lee ordered officials to review additional measures ahead of Thursday's exam and proposed a reward system offering at least 100 million won to those who report admissions cheating involving advanced technology, with additional payments based on the number of individuals implicated. He also called for a system under which individuals involved in coordinated cheating schemes could receive reduced or waived penalties if they voluntarily report the violations, and he ordered that an additional emergency alert be sent at an unpredictable time during the exam to help identify unauthorized electronic devices. Lee also instructed the Education Ministry to provide stationery, including erasers and correction fluid, at testing centers to prevent such items from being misused to conceal cheating devices.

Lee reviewed the government's arrangements with major global technology companies to secure evidence in suspected cases of students photographing exam questions and using AI to obtain answers, and he called for legislation requiring technology companies to provide relevant records at the government's request, including in cases involving suspected violations during this year's exam. In a post on X, Lee wrote that he had instructed officials to pursue legislation requiring the submission of records related to unlawful requests for exam answers upon government request, starting with this year's exam. He also wrote that surely even the boldest test-taker would not risk getting caught because their communication device went off in the middle of an exam. Lee wrote that cheating using advanced technology is tantamount to stealing the scores of hundreds of thousands of students who have worked hard to prepare for the exam, and he said the government would mobilize its full capabilities with a wartime sense of urgency to eradicate this theft of exam scores and ensure that honest test-takers are not harmed.

stories.Headline: Seoul dentistry student Lee Jin-woo livestreams solving Suneung Korean section to rebut AI cheating claims
stories.Summary:
Lee Jin-woo, a 33-year-old first-year dentistry student at Seoul National University, announced on Instagram that he will livestream himself solving the Korean-language section of Thursday's Suneung exam, according to a Korea Herald report published on Nov. 17, 2026. He recently drew attention after earning perfect scores on both multiple-choice sections, reading comprehension and logical reasoning, of the LEET held in July for 2027 law school admission. The exam, introduced in 2008 as the country moved from the traditional bar examination to a law school system, tests reading comprehension, logical reasoning and aptitude for legal studies rather than knowledge of law, and it also includes an essay section that individual law schools may consider. Reports noted that Lee was not the first person to achieve a perfect LEET score, since a legal professional who ranked first nationwide in the 2013 exam also earned full marks.

Suspicions that Lee used AI to cheat arose after he showed his test booklet during an interview with YouTuber Mimiminu, who is known for college entrance exam preparation content. The booklet showed corrections to his answers for questions 25 through 29, with his initial choices matching the correct answers to questions 24 through 28, leading some to speculate that he may have shifted answers by one question while copying them from an external source, possibly AI. The fact that the corrections appeared on the test booklet itself, rather than on the answer sheet where such mistakes typically occur, fueled further suspicion, and Lee explained that he misread the questions' requirements after losing concentration toward the end of the exam. He has also faced allegations of falsifying past Suneung score reports, because the reports he posted on social media for the exams he took in 2012, 2017, 2023 and 2025 all bore his current name, which he adopted after a legal name change, while he had used a different name while attending Korea University before enrolling at Seoul National University.

His reported scores show a dramatic improvement over the years, from grades of 6 to 8 across subjects on the nine-grade scale in his first Suneung in 2012, to 7 in Korean language, 1 in math and 4 in English in 2017 with grades of 2 to 3 in the remaining subjects, to grades of 1 or 2 in major subjects by 2023, and to the top grade of 1 in every subject in last year's exam. An official from the Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation, which administers the exam, told Newsis that score reports generally retain the name used at the time of registration unless it was formally changed through administrative procedures. Lee aims to dispel the mounting suspicions by solving Suneung questions live under conditions more challenging than those faced by regular test takers, and while the Korean-language section normally allows 80 minutes for 45 questions, he plans to answer 56 questions in just 65 minutes, covering both elective subjects, Speech and Writing and Language and Media. He told a local news outlet that the livestream is intended to quickly verify his abilities using newly released exam questions that could not have been leaked in advance.

The livestream will run on his Instagram account from 9:30 a.m. to 12:20 p.m. Thursday at the Daechi IDA Admissions Research Institute in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, with Korean-language instructors from Megastudy and Daesung MyMac and news reporters in attendance. The allegations come amid mounting concern over AI cheating, including a recent confession of AI-assisted cheating by the top scorer on the tax accountant qualification exam, and President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday ordered additional measures to curb AI-assisted cheating during Thursday's college entrance exam, including a proposed reward of at least 100 million won, or about $75,000, for tips.

stories.Headline: Samsung and Google sell out all 16 Intelligent Eyewear models in early preorders
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics and Google saw all 16 models of their jointly developed Intelligent Eyewear listed as sold out on Gentle Monster's Korean online store as of Monday, four days after preorders opened in South Korea and the United States. Several of the models sold out within hours on Thursday, according to Gentle Monster, and reservations for a public preview in New York have also filled up. The glasses, built with the South Korean fashion eyewear brand Gentle Monster, are scheduled for release on Dec. 10 in South Korea and the US. Neither Samsung nor Gentle Monster has disclosed how many pairs were available or ordered, so it is impossible to tell whether the glasses are a breakout hit or simply in short supply.

The glasses cost between 650,000 won and 700,000 won in Korea, a starting price of about $490, and they pack Google's Gemini AI assistant into Gentle Monster's distinctive frames with Samsung's hardware engineering. Samsung has made comfort a selling point since unveiling the glasses in July, claiming they would be lighter than most competing AI eyewear, and the finished models weigh between 39.6 and 43.9 grams. That is roughly 7 to 10 grams lighter than the second-generation Ray-Ban Meta glasses, which weigh around 48 to 51 grams. Wearers can ask Gemini about what they see, translate conversations, take photos or get directions without pulling out a phone, and because there is no display in the lenses, Gemini responds through speakers, with Samsung claiming up to nine hours of battery life.

Meta already holds a dominant lead, as its Ray-Ban smart glasses helped it capture 94 percent of global shipments of displayless AI glasses in the first half of 2026, according to Counterpoint Research. With comparable camera resolution and battery life, Samsung and Google will have to make their case through Gemini's capabilities and comfort. Google is also emphasizing privacy, saying bystanders' faces are obscured before images reach Gemini, and recording is disabled if the external camera indicator is covered. Samsung and Google have separately partnered with US eyewear retailer Warby Parker, whose six variations of Intelligent Eyewear start at $395 and will initially be available in the US.

stories.Headline: Samsung plans AI TV that pauses video when viewers leave the room
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics plans to reveal a new artificial intelligence television during the CES 2027 trade show in Las Vegas. This event will take place from January 6 to January 9 of next year to showcase the latest technology. The device, which is tentatively called TV-I, will use artificial intelligence to monitor the movements of people in the room. It can automatically pause a video when a viewer leaves the couch and resume playback when they return. This system aims to turn the television into a living room companion that understands the interests of the user.

The new television will allow viewers to search for clothes or restaurants appearing on the screen without using a phone. This builds upon the Click to Search feature from 2025 TVs that lets users ask questions using a remote button. Samsung has already partnered with Amazon in the United States to make advertisements on Samsung TV Plus directly shoppable. This service has grown to reach more than 100 million monthly active users across the entire world. The company is also considering the debut of its first humanoid robot at the same January electronics show.

Lee Won-jin, the president and head of the Visual Display Business, is leading this shift toward service revenue. He previously served as the head of Google Korea and was appointed to lead the TV business in May. Lee wants to move the division away from simply selling hardware to making money from content and shopping. This strategy follows a surprise leadership change that occurred before the regular year-end reshuffle of company executives. The company believes that relying solely on device sales is no longer a sustainable way to turn a profit.

The shift comes as TrendForce expects global television shipments to drop 0.8 percent to 194.65 million units this year. Long replacement cycles and slow demand are creating a difficult market for manufacturers of electronic screens. Low prices from Chinese competitors and the rising cost of components have added further strain to the industry. Samsung is now betting on steady income from existing customers through advertising and digital services. Executive Chairman Lee Jae-yong recently visited the Robotics eXperience Business Office to check on the progress of the robot business.

stories.Headline: Kim Jina meets Jacob Helberg in San Francisco to discuss AI and economic cooperation
stories.Summary:
Second Vice Foreign Minister Kim Jina met with U.S. Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg and discussed cooperation in artificial intelligence and broader bilateral economic ties, Seoul's foreign ministry said Tuesday. The talks took place in San Francisco on Monday local time, according to the ministry. Kim attended the Pax Silica Retreat in San Francisco on Sunday, where she took part in government-level discussions and public-private exchanges on AI and economic security. Kim signed the San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity at the retreat. Kim also met with Qatari Minister of State for Trade Affairs Ahmad Al-Sayed in San Francisco on Monday to discuss bilateral ties and ways to expand cooperation in investment, AI and other areas.

Kim emphasized South Korea's broad capabilities across the AI value chain and its readiness to work with the United States and other partner countries. She explained the objectives of South Korea's AI Basic Act and outlined plans for major projects involving semiconductors, data centers and physical AI, including efforts to match companies for cooperation. The retreat brought together representatives from 13 countries and the European Union, while 10 of them signed the San Francisco Declaration, including South Korea, the U.S., Japan, Australia, India and Britain. The declaration calls for cooperation to protect sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure and promote super intelligence-led growth. Launched in December 2025, Pax Silica is a consultative platform among like-minded countries aimed at promoting cooperation in AI and economic security.

Helberg asked about Seoul's AI policy direction and plans for major projects, and proposed encouraging greater collaboration between companies from the two countries. The two sides agreed to strengthen cooperation in AI and other advanced industries and encourage business collaboration in various areas, including semiconductors, data centers and physical AI, the ministry said. The officials also discussed ways to promote bilateral trade and investment and deepen cooperation in strategic industries, and agreed to continue consultations on ways to advance bilateral economic cooperation. Kim called for Washington's support for the successful implementation of South Korea's investment projects in the U.S., announced last month. She stressed the importance of ensuring stable visits by Korean businesspeople to facilitate the investments and called for working-level discussions on ways to improve investment conditions.

Al-Sayed expressed interest in South Korea's major projects involving semiconductors, data centers and physical AI. The two sides agreed to continue close communication to advance cooperation in trade, investment, AI and others. The ministry said the Kim and Helberg talks took place on Monday local time in San Francisco. Kim and Helberg posed for a photo in San Francisco on Nov. 16, 2026, in a photo provided by Seoul's foreign ministry. Kim spoke with Al-Sayed during their meeting in San Francisco on Nov. 16, 2026, in a photo provided by the foreign ministry.

The ministry said Tuesday that the Kim and Helberg meeting took place in San Francisco on Monday local time. The retreat where Kim signed the declaration was held in San Francisco on Sunday. The articles were published by Yonhap News Agency on Nov. 17, 2026, and Nov. 16, 2026. The ministry provided photos of Kim with Helberg and with Al-Sayed, both dated Nov. 16, 2026. The articles list related coverage on a Pax Silica Summit in Washington and a senior U.S. official's praise of South Korea's chip production.

The articles do not say what South Korea's investment projects in the U.S. announced last month involve. They do not name the three countries and the European Union that did not sign the San Francisco Declaration. They do not give the date of the Kim and Helberg meeting beyond Monday local time or the date of the Al-Sayed meeting beyond Monday. They do not say what the working-level discussions on investment conditions would cover or when they would occur. They do not say what follow-up steps the two sides planned after agreeing to continue consultations.

stories.Headline: China-linked Vapor Panda group uses AI tools to target Korean foreign policy organizations
stories.Summary:
A China-linked hacking group known as Vapor Panda targeted Korean diplomacy and foreign policy organizations using artificial intelligence tools. These cyberattacks occurred between October 17 and October 29, 2026, and some of the attempts were successful. The group used an AI agent-based penetration testing tool called Artex to scan for vulnerabilities in web applications and interfaces. This campaign was separate from other attacks against the Korean financial sector that took place during the previous month.

The Vapor Panda group targeted more than 200 organizations worldwide, including security agencies in Asia, Europe, the Middle East, and Latin America. They also attacked United States companies in the financial, defense, nuclear energy, semiconductor, and pharmaceutical sectors. The hackers primarily used the Chinese AI model DeepSeek to power Artex, though they may have used other paid subscriptions. This automation allowed the group to target hundreds of organizations simultaneously while potentially reducing the overall cost of the operations.

Adam Meyers, the senior vice president of counter adversary operations at CrowdStrike, reported these findings during a briefing on Tuesday. He stated that AI does not create a new form of attack but instead increases the speed and scale of existing methods. Meyers noted that automating processes previously done by humans has lowered the barriers for carrying out these cyberattacks. He emphasized that organizations can still defend against such threats by maintaining round-the-clock monitoring and sufficient visibility into their security environments.

stories.Headline: Han Won-seok tells police he used a hidden camera, smartphone and small monitor to cheat on the tax accountant exam
stories.Summary:
Han Won-seok, who has admitted to cheating on this year's tax accountant certification exam, told police that he used a small monitor alongside a miniature camera and a smartphone to aid him during the test, according to news reports on Tuesday. In a written confession, Han reportedly said he used a hidden camera to photograph the exam questions, sent them to a generative AI model through his smartphone to get the answers, and then viewed the responses on a separate monitor roughly the size of a smartphone. Earlier speculation had said that he may have used a tiny earpiece to receive the answers, and the exact type of monitor he used remains unclear. Han answered 159 of 160 multiple-choice questions correctly in the first round of the exam in April, and he achieved perfect scores in three of the four subjects, including introductory tax law, where other candidates scored an average of just 30.18 points out of 100. The cheating scandal came to light on Sunday when Han confessed to his actions in a video posted on the YouTube channel of his attorney, Lee Don-ho, after his exceptionally high scores sparked suspicions among other test-takers.

Han told reporters at around 9:17 a.m. as he arrived at the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency's investigation headquarters in Mapo-gu, western Seoul, that he was truly sorry to those who prepared for the exam and those involved, and that he would not hide what he did and would tell the truth to investigative authorities. Police are conducting forensic examinations of the devices Han submitted as part of an investigation into whether any accomplices were involved. The Human Resources Development Service of Korea, which oversees national qualification exams, said two proctors were stationed in the room where Han took the exam, and he was seated in the middle of the second row during the first round and the middle of the front row during the second. As more details emerged about the equipment used in the scheme, criticism mounted over how the cheating went unnoticed by exam supervisors, with one user writing on the online community DC Inside that even if the devices were small, they were still about the size of a smartphone except for the tiny camera, and asking where he could have hidden them.

Amid growing concerns over AI-assisted cheating, police have set up a special task force to crack down on exam fraud, and authorities also plan to investigate a growing number of online posts circulating on social media and internet forums in which users claim to have cheated on exams using AI, news reports said. The scandal has also cast suspicion on others who passed the same exam as Han, raising questions about whether more cases of cheating may have gone undetected. In response, the Korea Association of Certified Tax Accountants plans to introduce new tests during mandatory practical training to assess newly certified tax accountants' skills without AI assistance and identify those who may have cheated on the exam. The association said it would do everything it could to ensure that those who obtained their certifications through cheating are not allowed to practice as tax accountants and represent taxpayers.

stories.Headline: Google gives Japan early access to its latest AI model to boost cybersecurity
stories.Summary:
Google announced on November 17, 2026, that it will provide the Japanese government and major infrastructure providers with early access to its latest artificial intelligence model. This strategic move aims to strengthen the national cybersecurity posture of Japan as the country faces a significant increase in digital attacks. Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian traveled to Japan on November 16 to discuss these security measures with various government officials. The initiative is designed to help the nation defend its critical systems against an AI-fueled surge in malicious activities.

The program requires the deployment of frontier AI technology to identify and mitigate threats across essential infrastructure networks throughout the country. By granting early access to these advanced models, Google intends to help Japan manage the risks associated with sophisticated cyberattacks. This collaboration focuses on providing the tools necessary to protect sensitive data and maintain the stability of vital public services. The integration of these AI capabilities will allow security teams to respond more quickly to emerging vulnerabilities in their software.

Thomas Kurian is the executive responsible for overseeing this expansion of cyberdefense support during his recent visit to Tokyo. He met with government representatives to coordinate the delivery of these high-level AI tools to the appropriate agencies. While the specific details of his remarks were not fully disclosed, the visit emphasized the need for stronger partnerships between tech leaders and national governments. The goal is to ensure that Japan has the most current technology to combat the evolving nature of global cyber threats.

This development occurs as Japan continues to grapple with a sharp rise in unauthorized external access to its critical systems. The country has recently experienced security breaches, including an incident involving the Fugaku supercomputer, which highlighted existing gaps in security spending. These events have prompted Japanese officials to seek more advanced models from various technology firms to secure their digital borders. The partnership with Google represents a critical step in the broader effort to modernize the nation's defensive capabilities.

stories.Headline: Foreign investors return to Indian stocks as capital rotates away from AI shares
stories.Summary:
Indian stocks experienced a rapid rebound on November 17, 2026, as foreign investors returned to the market. This surge occurred because global investors shifted their focus away from artificial intelligence shares and responded to falling oil prices. These combined factors encouraged a significant rotation of capital back into Indian equities after a period of selling. The market recovery followed a trend of volatility affecting several other major Asian stock exchanges.

The shift in investor sentiment resulted in nearly $9 billion in foreign investor inflows into the Indian market. This financial movement was further supported by the results of the United States midterm elections and a decrease in global oil costs. Previously, these stocks had been sold off due to widespread concerns regarding headwinds created by artificial intelligence. The current rebound indicates a strategic hedge as investors move away from AI-related assets.

Market analysts suggest that the recovery is driven by a global rotation away from technology shares that were previously overvalued. Foreign investors are now taking a fresh look at Indian stocks to diversify their portfolios against AI risks. While specific officials were not named, the trend reflects a broader reaction to geopolitical and economic shifts. The inflow of capital suggests a renewed confidence in the stability of the Indian economy.

stories.Headline: Anthropic announces initial public offering to attract retail investment
stories.Summary:
Robert Botkin wrote a morning brief on November 17, 2026, regarding several recent events in the world of artificial intelligence. He discussed a scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and an alleged Chinese spy that occurred recently. The Federal Aviation Administration grounded all United States flights this past Friday due to technical issues. Microsoft experienced an eighteen hour email outage caused by a deep infrastructure and network capacity failure. Anthropic announced an upcoming initial public offering for the AI giant to attract retail investment.

Republicans introduced the AI Overwatch Act, Chip Security Act, Remote Access Security Act, and the MATCH Act to increase export controls. Hakeem Jeffries said last Monday he would ensure chip export restrictions remain in the final National Defense Authorization Act. The FAA grounded flights over the weekend while upgrading copper wire to fiber optic cable in their systems. A November 5 METR report stated Anthropic trained Model 4, which scored above 50 percent on all benchmarks. Model 4 is projected to be 7.8 percent more powerful than the Mythos Preview model from Anthropic.

The FAA stated that the grounding of flights resulted from upgrades from copper wire to fiber optic cable. Microsoft said their recent outage was caused by a failure in the backend of Microsoft 365 infrastructure. Robert Botkin noted that he is fascinated by the perception gap between law firms and in-house attorneys. He plans to ask his own clients if they see AI efficiencies and quality improvements in his work. Botkin expressed interest in how AI was used during the Microsoft incident and its impact on recovery efforts.

In-house lawyers surveyed by Juro found that 84 percent saw no reduction in fees or billed hours from AI. Only 5 percent of those in-house respondents said their legal service providers provided quality improvements using AI tools. A March Wolters Kluwer survey found 62 percent of law firm attorneys reported weekly AI efficiencies between 6 and 20 percent. An Ironclad survey of 800 attorneys in 2025 found 96 percent said AI helped achieve their business objectives. Finance leaders in an August 2026 Intuit survey of 2,100 people cited accuracy concerns as a barrier to AI.

A September 2026 Gallup-SCSP report found only 43 percent of American AI users trusted the technology to be unbiased. The FAA previously had a major disruption in September when a construction crew member accidentally cut a fiber optic cable. The FAA has also rolled out the SMART system, which uses AI to help predict problems in the sky. Azure Monitor uses AIOps capabilities and machine learning to reduce alert noise through dynamic thresholds and smart detection. These various surveys suggest that adoption figures may obscure how much responsibility people are prepared to delegate.

The incoming Congress is likely to show strong support for export controls following investigations into the practices of Nvidia. Anthropic will soon launch its initial public offering as fintech platforms gauge interest for participation from retail investors. Robert Botkin will resume the typical format of his AI Insights newsletter starting next week. The articles leave open whether AI had any actual impact on the recovery efforts during the Microsoft outage. It remains unclear how organizations can scale up AI use while maintaining trust and accuracy for their users.

stories.Headline: Taiwan dollar weakens as AI boom earnings stay in foreign accounts
stories.Summary:
The Taiwan dollar has begun sliding toward its weakest exchange rate since 2016, which contradicts the usual rules of currency trading. This unexpected decline occurred despite the island experiencing its longest streak of double-digit quarterly economic growth in nearly 40 years. The current situation is driven by a massive boom in artificial intelligence that has generated immense wealth. Huge amounts of export earnings are piling up in foreign accounts rather than supporting the local currency. The economic strength of the region is evidenced by the fourth-largest current-account surplus currently found in the entire world.

Two major companies, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. and Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., are central to this growth. These two industry giants combined to bring in roughly 140 billion dollars in sales during the third quarter alone. This massive influx of capital from the AI sector should normally lead to a much stronger national currency. Market analysts are confounded because the overwhelming evidence on paper suggests the currency should be increasing in value.

They note that the paradox exists because the earnings from the AI boom are not being converted back into the local dollar. The disconnect between the strong economic performance and the weak currency remains a significant puzzle for traders. No specific officials have provided a formal explanation for why these funds are staying abroad. More to follow.

stories.Headline: OpenAI partners with NATO to provide Daybreak AI cybersecurity tools
stories.Summary:
OpenAI announced on 17 November that it is partnering with NATO to give the transatlantic alliance cybersecurity tools from its Daybreak platform and to help it investigate potential cyberattacks, according to a statement released during the NATO Edge tech and digital defence conference in Izmir, Turkey. The ChatGPT maker said the deal gave NATO access to the advanced AI of Daybreak for uses ranging from reviewing software and investigating suspicious activity to validating vulnerabilities and developing and testing fixes. The company said its AI can help review software, investigate suspicious activity, validate vulnerabilities and speed up cyber defence across Allied networks. NATO said the tools will improve cyber resilience and protect critical digital infrastructure, at a moment when debate is growing around the world over the role AI should have in warfare.

OpenAI said it was fully committed to NATO’s principles on responsible adoption of artificial intelligence and on using the technology safely and securely. The company said NATO’s early use of OpenAI tools shows how capable cyber defenders can put frontier models to work in support of the alliance’s mission of safeguarding the freedom and security of its member states. It also said the deal helps strengthen cyber expertise across multinational teams responsible for protecting Allied networks. OpenAI has already partnered with the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity, known as ENISA, and with national cybersecurity agencies in France, Germany and Poland, and Ukraine also uses the US tech firm’s tools against cybersecurity threats to civilian infrastructure.

Dylan Browne, director-general of the NATO Communications and Information Agency, said in the statement that AI-powered cyber defence models represent a generational leap in cybersecurity. He said they accelerate vulnerability discovery, detect emerging threats at machine speed and enable defenders to stay ahead of adversaries. For NATO, he said, these technologies strengthen cyber resilience, enhance operational advantage and reinforce the ability to protect critical digital infrastructure at unprecedented scale and speed. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the announcement and the stated aims of the partnership.

stories.Headline: Experts say anti-AI trade and stable rupee draw foreign capital into TCS and Infosys
stories.Summary:
Major frontline Indian IT stocks including TCS, Infosys and HCLTech have seen significant price corrections and are now available at attractive valuations, according to stock market experts quoted in a Livemint report published on 17 November 2026. The report said experts believe smart global capital has started rotating out of overcrowded global AI plays and into Indian IT services as a hedge against overheating in Western tech stocks. It said the anti-AI trade and a stable Indian rupee are expected to fuel demand for IT shares and help long-term investors meet their goals. The report also said IT stocks are favourites of foreign institutional investors and that a stable rupee is expected to attract smart money moving out of bond and currency markets.

Avinash Gorakshkar, founder of Avinash Mentor Research, gave three reasons for treating IT stocks as long-term value picks: the anti-AI trade, a setback to Donald Trump's Republican Party in the US midterm elections, and the stable Indian rupee. He said FIIs are switching money from the bond market into emerging markets including India, and he advised investors to look at large-cap IT stocks, especially TCS and Infosys, because of their big exposure to US and European markets. He said these companies are expected to benefit from improved trade with the US after the India-EU trade deal and the midterm poll setback. Anuj Gupta, a SEBI-registered market expert, said the choice between TCS and Infosys depends on whether an investor prefers defensive scale and margins or higher dividend yields and a lower valuation multiple.

Gupta said TCS suits investors looking for a stable, lower-risk compounding core with superior free cash flow and industry-leading operating resilience during uncertain global demand cycles. He said Infosys suits investors looking for a higher dividend income stream of about 4.5 per cent and a slightly cheaper valuation relative to its earnings power. Mahesh M Ojha, vice president of research and business development at KC Securities, said Infosys has strong support at ₹1,125 and ₹1,112 and faces a hurdle at ₹1,163, with a break above that level expected to take the stock to ₹1,200. He said a fall below ₹1,090 could take Infosys down to ₹1,075.

Ojha said TCS has strong support at ₹2,378 and faces a hurdle at ₹2,440, and that breaking above ₹2,440 could take the stock to ₹2,500. He said a fall below ₹2,378 could take TCS down to ₹2,316. The report carried a disclaimer saying the story is for educational and informational purposes only and that the views and recommendations are those of individual analysts or broking companies, not Livemint. It advised investors to check with certified financial experts before making any investment decisions.

stories.Headline: India plans AI and machine learning as core pillars of its VISTAR statistical overhaul
stories.Summary:
The article, published by The Hindu on November 18, 2026 at 07:00 am IST and written by Santosh V. Perumal, examines balancing AI-driven estimates and ground-level evidence in official statistics. It reports that AI and Machine Learning are positioned as core pillars in the newly approved Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR). The article states that VISTAR is set to overhaul India’s official data architecture. It notes that the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) seeks to use AI/ML algorithms to ingest, clean, and harmonise high-volume, alternative digital data. The piece warns that this could expose the country’s statistical system more to the risks of synthetic data, which is AI generated, simulated or hybrid.

The article states that VISTAR proposes increasing the number of major surveys from 43 to 59 during the 16th Finance Commission cycle. It reports that the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE) for 2025 collected information from more than 6.7 lakh establishments across 24,153 surveyed first-stage units. It mentions that recent moves to introduce MDR (Merchant Discount Rate) on UPI may lead to higher cash transactions. It cites the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe 2025 Framework on Responsible AI for Official Statistics, which emphasises fairness, accountability, transparency and validity. It refers to Gauss-Markov’s BLUE (Best Linear Unbiased Estimator) principle as a key benchmark for estimation under specified statistical assumptions.

The article states that MoSPI seeks to use AI/ML algorithms to address the primary bottleneck of data silos. It reports that the World Economic Forum (WEF) said in a special publication in 2025 that synthetic data is becoming an essential tool in the data ecosystem, addressing many of the limitations of real-world data, from data scarcity to privacy. It notes that the WEF specifically highlights “model collapse”, in which repeated training on synthetic outputs can progressively degrade the diversity and quality of model-generated information. It states that the WEF said public scepticism about data authenticity grows as synthetic content proliferates, even for organic data. It reports that the WEF said this “liar’s dividend” threatens societal trust and is worsened by poor disclosure or traceability practices.

The article states that a statement reading “Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war” was signed by 350 technology and industry leaders. It reports that the signatories included Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio, Demis Hassabis of Google DeepMind, Sam Altman of OpenAI, Dario Amodei of Anthropic, and Bill Gates. It states that the statement warns of scenarios including loss of human control over machine optimisation goals. It notes that economists, international agencies, and state governments may challenge the numbers if they lack an empirical audit trail. It reports that possible consequences could be the misallocation of public resources, distortion of economic indicators and the erosion of public confidence.

The article states that the distinction between observation and estimation is fundamental in statistics. It notes that an estimate, however sophisticated, cannot automatically substitute for evidence collected from the ground. It reports that synthetic data is artificially generated using statistical algorithms, mathematical models or AI/ML techniques and is designed to reproduce the patterns, relationships and distributions found in actual datasets without necessarily reproducing the original observations. It states that synthetic data need not be rejected in toto since it has legitimate applications in research, privacy protection, testing algorithms and exploring scenarios in situations of scarce observations. It notes that India’s informal economy has put the statistical system in a tight spot as a vast part of economic activity remains outside organised corporate structures, formal accounting systems and regular digital reporting.

The article states that the challenge is to ensure that AI does not substitute for ground-level evidence. It reports that India must factor in human oversight, ground verification and source transparency while preserving statistical independence, taking a cue from the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe 2025 Framework. It states that primary surveys must be the bedrock of official statistics. It notes that model-generated estimates must be separately identified from actual survey-based estimates. It states that the broader objective should be producing estimates that are unbiased, reliable and supported by evidence.

Articles.Title: Balancing AI-driven estimates and ground-level evidence in official statistics

stories.Headline: Researchers create a Python pipeline that de-identifies and standardises CT scans for forensic AI
stories.Summary:
Researchers developed an automated preprocessing workflow to standardise computed tomography imaging data for machine learning and deep learning applications within forensic anthropology, according to a study published in the International Journal of Legal Medicine by Jani, Patel, Roy, Sehrawat and Patel in 2026. The work addresses operational hurdles in forensic science, where medical CT scans have grown to help overcome ethical, logistical and physical preservation difficulties associated with traditional cadaveric collections. Deploying artificial intelligence on large collections of medical imaging data still presents substantial challenges, specifically regarding data privacy safeguards and technical standardisation across imaging repositories. To establish a consistent preparation method for forensic anthropology research and education, the study team created an end-to-end pipeline programmed in Python.

The framework organises image preparation into three distinct technical stages, namely the de-identification and sorting of patient data, the computational removal of the examination table and specialised bone windowing. The workflow was specifically constructed for and applied to CT scans of the thorax, using ground-truth reference models alongside standard performance metrics to evaluate system outcomes. The de-identification procedure addressed metadata across two hundred examined Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine files, and the script successfully processed all predefined identifying attributes contained within the datasets. The patient table removal network successfully eliminated the examination table in 96 percent of the evaluated datasets, representing 192 out of the 200 scan series, and the model attained an accuracy rating of 99.94 percent when tested on original, non-augmented test images.

The bone segmentation model achieved a Dice score of 93.12 percent alongside a precision of approximately 90 percent, and segmented three-dimensional reconstructions exhibited high agreement with the designated ground-truth reference. Technical comparisons confirmed that the segmented outputs showed minimal geometric deviation from the corresponding reference standard. The authors noted that future research will pursue expansion of the workflow to full-body computed tomography scans and additional medical imaging modalities. The proposed integrated workflow provides an ethical, standardised and efficient solution for de-identifying and preprocessing CT imaging data, and by enabling the preparation of a scalable dataset for artificial intelligence applications, the methodology supports analytical development for modern populations.
