stories.Headline: OpenAI researchers report critical PHP vulnerabilities that attackers exploit before fixes are released
stories.Summary:
On August 11, 2026, researchers from OpenAI privately reported critical security vulnerabilities in PHP, a foundational technology powering much of the modern web, including millions of websites built on platforms such as WordPress and Drupal. Attackers targeted operational websites and critical systems supporting businesses, government agencies, and essential public services. Reported attacks included the theft of credentials and security keys, unauthorized access to vulnerable servers, installation of persistent malware, attacks against commercial and government systems, disruption of essential services, destructive file-wiping, and permanent loss of critical data. Security researchers reported millions of malicious probes and attempted exploits worldwide. Research published on November 12, 2026 confirmed that attackers exploited the PHP vulnerabilities to compromise production security gateways, install persistent malware, move into internal infrastructure, and conduct destructive attacks against victims.

One principal set of related fixes to PHP changed 423 files, adding 11,556 lines and removing 1,017. Developers spent more than two months developing and testing fixes for these vulnerabilities, while attackers began exploiting the weaknesses before the fixes were released and attacks continued afterward. Soon after the fixes were released, a verified crash resulted in new corrections. The available evidence indicates that PHP's automated regression tests are primarily designed, developed, and maintained by members of the open-source development community, rather than by a separate, independent professional software testing organization. The PHP Foundation describes its primary mission as funding PHP developers, rather than maintaining a separate professional testing organization.

Ed Kit, author of "Software Testing in the Real World" and CEO at Software Development Technologies, said he began his career developing software at Bell Laboratories and later worked at Tandem Computers. He said he knew some extraordinary developers and also saw extraordinary defects created by extraordinary developers, and that occasionally he was the developer. He said developers and professional testers bring distinct but complementary expertise, and that believing in your implementation influences what you think to test. He said professional testers are trained to challenge assumptions, asking what happens when a function fails halfway through, what survives into the next request, what breaks under load, and what hasn't been thought to test. He said he recognizes the PHP developers who added automated checks, used continuous integration and sanitizer builds, and worked with outside security specialists, but he has not found a comprehensive public, independently authored professional QA assessment of the broader release risks.

Kit said there is no publicly established evidence of a dedicated, independent team of professional test engineers responsible for test design and challenging developers' assumptions. He said that without an independent professional software testing organization there is no dedicated Test Manager to lead and coordinate testing, no independent Test Architect responsible for designing and maintaining a comprehensive test automation framework, and no separate team of professional test designers systematically identifying what needs to be tested. He proposed establishing an independent professional testing capability for significant changes to foundational open-source software, bringing experienced professional testers in early to challenge requirements and design assumptions, independently evaluate the test strategy, and address functional, integration, compatibility, performance, security, reliability, and regression risks. He said this would complement, not replace, the work of developers and security researchers, and that it needs funding, with corporate beneficiaries of open source supporting shared testing teams through foundations, grants, and sponsorships. He offered as a possible discussion point investing $1 in independent testing for every $2, $3 spent on open-source development, and said AI companies should also contribute.

Kit said the PHP vulnerability is much bigger than PHP, asking who independently evaluates the quality of foundational open-source software supporting businesses, hospitals, banks, governments, airports, space, and much of the internet, and citing Linux, OpenSSL, Apache, Python, and PostgreSQL as widely used projects. He said testing is risk management, that we can never test every combination of all possible feature variations, but that professional testers should be used to intelligently select the best combinations most likely to reveal the most significant failures. He said AI can now generate code at extraordinary speed, which makes designing the right tests more important, not less, and that developers, test designers, and test automation professionals are not competitors because critical software needs all three. He said he has long advocated Keyword Driven test automation because it separates the work of designing meaningful tests from implementing and executing them. He said emergency patching creates multiple obligations including eliminating the vulnerability and confirming that the service still works, and asked whether critical user functions were tested, whether the many PHP extensions were tested with the proposed changes, and whether there was a rollback plan.

The Software Development Technologies Board (www.sdtcorp.com) has committed to raising awareness of the urgent need for independent professional software testing and providing financial support to establish the Professional Independent Testing (PIT) Initiative, focused on foundational open-source software. The mission of PIT is to strengthen the quality of critical open-source technologies by establishing independent professional testing teams, led by experienced Test Managers and Test Architects, with dedicated professional Test Designers and Test Automation Engineers responsible for developing comprehensive, risk-based automated regression test libraries. The plan is to establish PIT as a private operating foundation and use Open Collective to help launch the initiative. Kit said we can debate the value of AI discoveries without a coordinated plan to fix vulnerabilities before attackers exploit them, but that the larger concern is that we depend on foundational open-source software without sufficient assurance that it has undergone comprehensive, independent professional testing. He said AI finds vulnerabilities, developers fix them, and independent professional verification and validation deserve equal attention.

stories.Headline: Druckenmiller exits AMD and Alphabet and adds SpaceX, Palantir and AppLovin
stories.Summary:
Duquesne Family Office's third-quarter 13F showed complete exits from AMD and Alphabet, alongside new positions in SpaceX, Palantir and AppLovin, according to MarketWatch's review of the filing. Stanley Druckenmiller is still buying artificial intelligence but changing which AI businesses he owns. The filing does not show his sale prices or exact trade dates, so investors can't tell how well the exits were timed. Since then, AMD has fallen 22.35% from its October 6 close of $649.42. Since the quarter ended, Alphabet has dropped 17.54%.

AMD's third-quarter revenue rose 44.7% to $13.38 billion, and Data Center sales grew 97% to $8.55 billion. The company guided fourth-quarter revenue to approximately $17 billion, and the stock trades near 191 times trailing earnings. GAAP EPS was $1.46 after a $1,097M customer warrant charge. Alphabet's Google Cloud revenue grew 103% to $30.71 billion, but capital spending reached $51.36 billion and free cash flow was negative $9.07 billion. Alphabet is now paying for its expansion partly through debt, at-the-market equity issuance and mandatory convertible preferred stock, and GAAP EPS of $2.12 missed the $2.97 estimate, ending a 12-quarter beat streak.

Palantir's U.S. commercial revenue of $984M exceeded U.S. government revenue of $953M for the first time, and the adjusted operating margin was 62%. Full-year revenue guidance rose to $8.53B, and CEO Alex Karp said the Sovereign AI moment is purpose-built for Palantir. Palantir trades near 228 times earnings, total contract value grew just 6% year over year, and shares are down 11.81% year to date. SpaceX reported revenue of $14.60B, and its Super Intelligence segment, which includes Grok and Cursor, brought in $7.60B, up 830%. That segment leases data center capacity to outside customers and expanded with the Cursor acquisition at an implied $60B equity value.

Starlink had 13.6M consumer subscribers, and SpaceX shares trade at $141.48, down 12.1% from their first available close on June 12. On Tuesday, MarketWatch reported that SpaceX got a vote of confidence from Nvidia. AppLovin's revenue rose 55.5% to $2.18B, and adjusted EBITDA reached $1.84B at an 84% margin. The company bought back $1.4B of stock during the quarter, and CEO Adam Foroughi said he believes this business can compound at roughly 30% annually over the long term. At about 38 times earnings, AppLovin trades at a far lower multiple than Palantir, and shares are up 46.53% over the past month but down 42.13% year to date.

Earlier this year, Druckenmiller said AI-linked stocks looked disturbingly heated. In a Morgan Stanley interview, he summed up the market's view that the consensus for AI is that it will be very deflationary and lead to massive job losses. The pattern points to a preference for companies that sell AI-driven results through software, ads and connectivity, with less exposure to the chip spending cycle. AMD now trades near 191 times earnings and Alphabet's spending turned free cash flow negative. Palantir's stock trades near 228 times earnings.

Four signals to track include whether AMD delivers its roughly $17B fourth-quarter revenue target as its Helios server racks scale up. Another is Palantir's fourth-quarter revenue against its $2.649, $2.653 billion guidance, and whether contract value starts growing faster. The next 13F will show whether Druckenmiller kept, added to, or cut these positions. The filing does not show his sale prices or exact trade dates.

stories.Headline: AT&T COO Jeff McElfresh says agentic AI agents are reversing internet traffic toward uploads
stories.Summary:
AT&T chief operating officer Jeff McElfresh said at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit on Monday, November 16, 2026, that the direction of internet bandwidth is undergoing a fundamental shift, because agentic AI agents tap the network around the clock rather than in the episodic patterns created by people watching video. U.S. household upload traffic grew 19.2% year over year in the second quarter, more than three times as fast as downloads, which grew 6.1%, according to OpenVault, which tracks broadband usage for internet providers. The average subscriber now uploads 58.2 GB a month, and while households still download about 11 times as much as they upload, that ratio was 16.6 times in 2019. McElfresh, who has been at AT&T for 31 years, said watching traffic from the network's control center used to be easy to read, with clear patterns like Netflix and YouTube traffic and traffic leaving cities for the suburbs at the start of the pandemic, when many work-from-home networks struggled and video calls glitched. He pointed to an autonomous vehicle connected to AT&T's wireless network that transmits more data up into the cloud to train a model than it consumes.

Mobile operators are seeing a similar shift, since in 2025, 43 of 55 service providers tracked by Ericsson saw uplink traffic grow faster than downlink, according to its June Mobility Report. Ericsson's scenarios have uplink traffic tripling or quintupling by 2031 if AI apps, smart glasses and agents take off, though it says mobile traffic is still expected to remain downlink-dominated in the near term and warns operators that current networks are not dimensioned for sustained uplink demand. Nokia's 2026 network traffic report forecasts that AI will drive 44% of global network traffic by 2035, and that for physical AI such as robots, cars and drones, more than 90% of traffic will start in the uplink, with Nokia writing that AI is challenging the asymmetric design of traditional access networks. AT&T has a business reason to tell this story, because fiber carries traffic equally fast in both directions while cable broadband, its main home-internet rival, has historically offered much slower uploads than downloads. McElfresh called fiber the gold standard, saying it is future proof and has all of the symmetrical capabilities to be very responsive to the AI future.

AT&T plans to reach 60 million fiber locations by 2030, about 1.5 times its footprint, and signed a supply deal with Corning worth more than $3 billion in September. OpenVault's numbers give AT&T something to point to, since fiber subscribers uploaded an average of 94.1 GB a month in the second quarter against 58.2 GB on cable's DOCSIS networks, though OpenVault CEO Mark Trudeau told Light Reading in October that he attributes the upstream growth to gaming, Zoom and Teams calls and a lot of AI content creation, and cable companies are also rolling out DOCSIS 4.0, which supports symmetric speeds. Corning CEO Wendell Weeks, who shared the stage, said customers will feel the shift at home through the combination of the bandwidth delivered and the type of products AI will enable, from robots to how people use their devices. Weeks said the next frontier is inside the data center itself, where copper wiring will give way to fiber, converting signals to light within a centimeter of the processor. McElfresh said AT&T technicians are installing fiber in 10,000 neighborhoods on any given day, adding roughly 4 million locations this year, toward the company's target of 60 million by 2030, while Ericsson's forecast window runs to 2031.

stories.Headline: Opsera adds security and governance features to Forge for legacy applications
stories.Summary:
Opsera announced new capabilities for its Forge platform on November 17, 2026, from Palo Alto, California, to help enterprises understand, assess and secure legacy applications. The company said the additions give greater visibility, earlier risk detection, security assessments and built-in guardrails as AI accelerates discovery of vulnerabilities in legacy software. Opsera described Forge as its AI-native Software Factory for the enterprise. The announcement said organizations adopting AI across the software development life cycle find rewriting code easier, but understanding complex applications and controlling modernization remain significant challenges. The new capabilities are available today to Forge customers.

Forge now includes enhanced built-in security checks that help teams spot risks early, flagging known vulnerabilities, exposed credentials and outdated components and explaining each risk in plain business terms. An expanded ForgeScore assessment provides A, F grades aligned with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, and the 8-dimension scorecard now grades each application against that framework for a board-ready view. Enhanced Application Discovery maps each application's business rules and dependencies and shares a unified view for product, security and engineering leaders. Configurable Pipeline Controls let administrators set modernization stages, approvals and goal scope so teams follow a clear process. For threats like PHP2Shell, Forge shows which applications an upgrade will affect before it ships.

Vishnu Vasudevan, CPO of Opsera, said frontier AI has made finding vulnerabilities easier, but fixing them inside legacy code nobody understands is still expensive. He said Forge acts as the AI harness around the models and agents teams already use, so every modernization project becomes a security remediation project. He said leadership gets a NIST-aligned grade they can take to the board. The announcement said frontier models such as Claude Mythos Preview helped surface more than 10,000 high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities through Anthropic's Project Glasswing. That work shifted the bottleneck from finding flaws to fixing them, and legacy code is where fixes are hardest.

Across its customer base, Forge powers mission-critical initiatives in diverse sectors, including regulated industries, with a 99.8% success rate and token spend savings of over 60%. Forge works with the models and coding agents enterprises already use, including Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub Copilot and Cursor. It connects to more than 150 development, security and delivery tools. Opsera directed readers to opsera.ai/forge/modernization to get a ForgeScore security and modernization assessment of their codebase. The announcement was issued through the SD Times Newswire.

The announcement said AI is being adopted across the software development life cycle, making code rewriting easier while understanding complex applications remains hard. It said identifying security risks and maintaining control over modernization are still significant challenges for organizations. It said AI accelerates the discovery of security vulnerabilities in legacy software. It said Forge provides visibility, risk detection and guardrails so enterprises address inherited risk as they modernize, not after. It said the new capabilities address security and governance throughout the modernization process.

The new capabilities are available today to Forge customers, and Opsera invited enterprises to request a ForgeScore assessment of their codebase at opsera.ai/forge/modernization. The articles did not say how many customers use Forge or which regulated industries they represent. They did not give pricing for the new capabilities or a date for wider availability beyond today. They did not say how many applications Forge has assessed or how the 99.8% success rate was measured. They did not say when Project Glasswing ran or which organizations received its vulnerability findings.

stories.Headline: Microsoft releases ARM-based Cobalt 200 chips to power AI agents in its cloud
stories.Summary:
Microsoft released its ARM-based Cobalt 200 chips for general availability on November 17, 2026. This hardware launch was executed by the technology company to support its cloud infrastructure. The release focuses on providing specialized processing power for modern computing needs. These chips are designed to enhance the performance of artificial intelligence agents. The company aims to improve efficiency for large-scale software development tasks.

The Cobalt 200 chips utilize the ARM architecture to change how AI agents operate. These processors are deployed within Microsoft data centers to handle specific artificial intelligence workloads. The hardware requires integration with existing cloud services to provide scalable computing power. This transition allows for better energy efficiency compared to traditional x86 processor designs. The chips are now available for general use across the Microsoft ecosystem.

Microsoft is responsible for the development and deployment of these new ARM-based processors. The company stated that these chips are critical for the evolution of AI agents. They explained that the hardware provides the necessary performance for autonomous software tasks. The developers noted that the Cobalt 200 series optimizes the cost of running AI. Microsoft believes this move strengthens its position in the competitive cloud infrastructure market.

Software engineering leaders and aspirational developers are the primary groups affected by this change. These professionals can now leverage more efficient hardware for their AI-driven applications. Industry analysts suggest that this move will lower the barrier for deploying AI agents. Users of Microsoft cloud services will see changes in how their workloads are processed. The shift impacts anyone building at-scale software development tools in the cloud.

The articles provide background on the growing demand for AI infrastructure and autonomous agents. There is a broader trend of cloud providers designing their own custom silicon for efficiency. Previous discussions at KubeCon highlighted the industry focus on moving AI agents into production. The move follows a pattern of optimizing hardware for large language models and vector indices. This context shows a shift toward specialized ARM hardware for cloud-native environments.

Microsoft will now integrate the Cobalt 200 chips into its broader AI service offerings. The company will monitor how these processors handle real-world AI agent workloads. Future updates may include further optimizations for specific software engineering tasks. The articles leave open how these chips will compare to Nvidia hardware in performance. It remains unclear when other ARM-based chip versions will reach general availability.

Articles.Title: Microsoft’s ARM-based Cobalt 200 chips go GA. Why it matters for AI agents. - The New Stack

stories.Headline: H2O.ai launches TimeH2O and TabH2O foundation models for time-series and tabular data
stories.Summary:
H2O.ai launched the next version of its Predictive AI capabilities on November 17, 2026, adding two new foundation models, TimeH2O for time-series data and TabH2O for tabular data, both generally available on H2O AI Cloud. The company is based in Mountain View, California, and describes itself as the trusted Sovereign AI Platform with software and expertise to run predictive, generative, and agentic AI in production. TimeH2O-v1 ranked first among 32 models on the fev-bench forecasting leaderboard as of October 23, 2026, without training on any fev-bench dataset. The release was announced through Business Wire, and the article carries a timestamp of Tue, November 17, 2026 at 11:28 AM CST. The article states that most of the decisions that run an organization live in time-series and tabular data: demand, inventory, cash flow, risk, and fraud.

TimeH2O is a 108-million-parameter time-series foundation model that forecasts zero-shot, predicting on data it has never seen with no model to build for each series. On fev-bench as of October 23, 2026, TimeH2O-v1 ranked first of 32 models with a 91.9% win rate, ahead of Timestral-209M at 89.6%, t0-gamma at 88.1%, Google's TimesFM-3, and Amazon's Chronos-2. It posted a 50.8% skill score across 100 forecasting tasks and never trained on any fev-bench dataset. It also posted the lowest aggregate MASE of 0.654 and CRPS of 0.441 among zero-shot models on Salesforce's GIFT-Eval leaderboard as of October 24, 2026. Organizations can fine-tune it on their own data for demand forecasting, inventory, financial planning, energy load, and healthcare resource planning, while TabH2O does the same for structured business data: risk scoring, fraud detection, and customer analytics.

Sri Ambati, CEO and Founder of H2O.ai, said that lifecycles of all customers, businesses, economies and people are time-series, and that transforming enterprises with prediction is the super power of AI with high ROI. He said TimeH2O is the foundation model that ushers the ChatGPT moment for predictions, bringing predictive super powers to the finger tips of business users and consumers. He said every agent fighting fraud, hedging capital markets, dynamically pricing products, managing inventory and supply chain or moving cash is acting on a forecast that will now be powered by TimeH2O, which is entirely pre-trained on synthetic and public datasets so customers can own the models and further fine-tune on their local data. He said TimeH2O and TabH2O are small enough that they are expected to be embedded into applications, agents and physical AI running where their action is happening and where data lives, instead of renting a frontier model by the token. The article states that both models join H2O Driverless AI, an AutoML tool, in H2O.ai's Predictive AI capabilities.

H2O MLOps, a model deployment and monitoring tool, takes TimeH2O and TabH2O into production on H2O AI Cloud, where organizations can fine-tune on their own data and adapt the models to their industry, datasets, and business. Organizations can deploy, monitor, and govern, managing the full model lifecycle in production with observability and audit built in, and run them where they choose. H2O AI Cloud is available as H2O AI Managed Cloud, which H2O.ai operates, as H2O AI Hybrid Cloud, a private cloud the customer operates in its own cloud, on-premises or air-gapped, or as H2O AI Cloud for Government, which is FedRAMP High certified. An agent managing inventory needs an accurate demand forecast, a finance agent needs to anticipate cash, and an operations agent needs to predict workloads and disruptions, and TimeH2O and TabH2O supply those forecasts. H2O AI Super Agent, the orchestration layer at the core of H2O AI Cloud, brings predictive, generative, and agentic AI together in one system.

TimeH2O and TabH2O are generally available now on H2O AI Cloud for production use and fine-tuning on an organization's own data. TimeH2O-v1's open weights remain on Hugging Face for research and evaluation under the H2O Model Non-Commercial License, and production use requires a license from H2O.ai. H2O.ai is holding a virtual panel on December 3 with the Kaggle Grandmasters behind TimeH2O. The article states that H2O.ai created the industry's trusted Sovereign AI Platform because organizations should own their AI: their agents, models, data, and results, run anywhere from cloud to air-gapped. It states that Super Agent orchestrates predictive, generative, and agentic AI in one system, with observability and governance, empowering regulated and public sector organizations to get value from AI.

The article states that moving from pilot to production takes expertise, from top-ranked data scientists, including Kaggle Grandmasters, to forward-deployed engineers embedded with customer teams. It states that H2O.ai is built on a decade of open source and is trusted by 20,000+ organizations, half the Fortune 500. It names AT&T, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, Workday, Progressive Insurance, and NIH as organizations that rely on H2O.ai to cut cost and risk and own their AI future. It states that through its AI for Good program, H2O.ai applies technology and investment to non-profits and academia solving hard problems in health, education, and the environment. The article gives full benchmark results at https://h2oai.github.io/benchmarks and lists Bruna Smith as media contact.

stories.Headline: InfoQ opens registration for six five-week online cohort workshops starting in January 2027
stories.Summary:
InfoQ opened registration on November 17, 2026, for six online cohort workshops that start between January 9 and January 22, 2027, the article by Artenisa Chatziou states. The six cohorts cover AI Engineering, Software Architecture, and High-Performing Teams, and each program runs five weeks. The workshops bring senior engineers, architects, and engineering leaders together to work through technical and organizational decisions with experienced practitioners. Participants apply frameworks from QCon and InfoQ to decisions from their own work and compare approaches with practitioners from other organizations. Working across different organizational contexts helps expose trade-offs and assumptions that may not emerge from an internal discussion alone, the article says.

Each cohort combines four hours of live facilitated sessions per week, independent application work, and a program-specific capstone, and participation costs USD 1,470 per person. The AI Engineering Program covers RAG architectures, agent design, platforms, and evaluation, and three January cohorts are planned. Hien Luu, an AI/ML leader and author of MLOps with Ray, starts January 9, with Saturday sessions at 09:00 PST. Adi Polak, Director of Developer Experience Engineering at Confluent, starts January 21, with Thursday sessions at 08:00 PST. Lan Chu, a principal engineer at Rabobank and author of Post-training LLMs, starts January 22, with Friday sessions at 14:00 CET, and her QCon London 2026 presentation examined a production RAG system built on more than 10,000 documents and used by more than 300 people.

The InfoQ Architect Program covers distributed systems, decentralized decisions, platform engineering, and AI architecture, and its capstone involves co-authoring a technical article examining AI's role in software architecture or platform engineering. Selected articles may be published on InfoQ. Both architecture cohorts start January 22 and are facilitated by Luca Mezzalira, an independent software architect and author of Building Micro-Frontends. Friday sessions are offered at 09:30 GMT and 10:00 EST. The High-Performing Teams Program examines team structure, ownership, delivery flow, AI responsibilities, and engineering metrics as one operating model, and its January 12 cohort is facilitated by Olimpiu Pop, an InfoQ Podcast co-host with experience in solutions architecture, engineering management, and CTO roles, with sessions on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 16:00 to 18:00 CET.

The article says faster coding does not necessarily improve delivery when reviews, approvals, or infrastructure dependencies become the constraint, and that AI agents change how responsibilities are divided and which work requires human judgment. Participants in the teams program evaluate constraints in their own team environments, compare approaches with peers, and develop a proposed target operating model covering responsibilities, workflow, and measurement. The live online workshops focus on discussion and application rather than recorded lectures, and participants work with an experienced facilitator and a small cross-company peer group. Sessions are not recorded, allowing participants to discuss organizational constraints more openly. Certification requires attendance, active participation, and successful completion of the program capstone.

The article lists related events, including QCon San Francisco from November 16 to 20, 2026, with early bird registration ending November 10, and QCon AI New York on December 15 and 16, 2026, also with early bird ending November 10. It lists QCon London from April 13 to 16, 2027, across 15 engineering tracks, with early bird ending November 10, and QCon AI Boston on July 8 and 9, 2027, with registration open. It also lists a High-Performing Teams Certification cohort on November 17, 2026, an AI Engineering Certification cohort on January 9, 2027, for the Americas, another on January 21, 2027, for the Americas, an AI Engineering Certification cohort on January 22, 2027, for EMEA, and an Architect Certification cohort on January 22, 2027. The article names InfoQ, C4Media Inc., and the author Artenisa Chatziou, and states that InfoQ.com and all content are copyright © 2006-2026 C4Media Inc. The article says the programs go beyond studying technical material, with participants returning to discuss what they tried and learned.

It says participants in the architect program apply the material to architecture decisions they currently own, compare trade-offs with peers, and practice communicating their reasoning to stakeholders. It says participants in the AI Engineering Program work through technical approaches and failure modes, applying them to AI systems or proposals from their own work. It says production AI involves decisions beyond model selection, including how context is retrieved and maintained, how much autonomy agents should have, and how reliability, latency, and inference costs are managed. It says architecture choices are shaped by system requirements, team boundaries, platform ownership, and organizational constraints. Full schedules, syllabi, and registration details are available on the InfoQ Online Certification Programs website, the article states.

The article gives no further information on the six January cohorts, on the facilitators beyond their stated roles, or on the capstones beyond what it describes. It does not say how many participants each cohort will take or where the live sessions will be held beyond being online. It does not say what happens to the co-authored articles that are not selected for publication on InfoQ. It does not give the dates of the five-week programs beyond their start dates.

stories.Headline: Linux Foundation finds 58% of development teams release code faster than security staff can review it
stories.Summary:
A Linux Foundation report published on November 16, 2026 found that 58% of software development teams are releasing code faster than their security staff can review it, according to DevOps.com. The report, State of AI Impact on Software Security and Cybersecurity 2026, surveyed 308 cybersecurity practitioners working in businesses and open source projects. It found that 60% of respondents said AI coding tools add external software dependencies to their applications, while just 16% reported fewer dependencies. Development teams review only 53% of indirect dependencies, leaving much of their software infrastructure without adequate scrutiny. Among experienced AI cybersecurity professionals, 93% expressed concern about software supply chain attacks, 90% about prompt injection attacks and 87% about the maintenance demands of frequent software updates.

Some 76% of experienced practitioners believe AI makes it easier for attackers to combine multiple vulnerabilities into more sophisticated exploits. Only 30% of surveyed teams have assigned specialized personnel to handle AI-related cybersecurity threats, a figure that rises to 35% among businesses but falls to 16% for open source projects. About one-third of organizations have adopted official security policies addressing AI, while 35% rely on informal guidelines, and while 76% identify approved AI tools, only 57% require human review of AI-generated code and just 36% include provisions for automated security scanning. Among teams with dedicated AI security personnel, 43% investigate and resolve most new security alerts immediately, compared with 23% among teams without dedicated AI security resources.

Practitioners credited AI-assisted security tools with identifying approximately 30% of the vulnerabilities they discovered during the previous year, and 69% of practitioners using these tools reported meaningful improvements in cybersecurity. Those tools helped practitioners complete security-related development tasks 17% faster on average, but inaccurate vulnerability alerts added an estimated 30% to workloads. Some 82% of respondents agreed that excessive dependence on AI tools weakens developers' fundamental security skills. The Linux Foundation recommends stronger controls over third-party software, formal AI security policies, continued developer training and greater use of automated security testing.

stories.Headline: Psychiatrist Cheng-Ta Li creates AI platform to assess treatment-resistant depression
stories.Summary:
Psychiatrist Cheng-Ta Li created an artificial intelligence platform to evaluate severe depression. He developed this tool to precisely assess patients with treatment-resistant depression. The news of this development was published on November 17, 2026. Dr. Li directs the Precision Depression Intervention Center at Taipei Veterans General Hospital. He also holds an appointment at the National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University School of Medicine.

The AI-PreDIC platform combines clinical information with biological measurements like EEG and FDG-PET brain imaging. This patented tool provides objective estimates of depression severity and how stubbornly it resists treatment. The Precision Depression Intervention Center opened in June 2022 as Taiwan's first center for this purpose. It has already provided clinical services for more than 20,000 treatment-resistant depression patient visits. Dr. Li views resistance as a road rather than a simple yes-or-no label.

Dr. Li stated that the key question is which treatment helps a particular patient at a particular stage. He believes that findings should be judged by evidence strength rather than where they were published. He expressed a fear of patients trusting unproven treatments and missing opportunities for appropriate care. Dr. Li also noted that he wishes he understood mental health better while his grandmother lived. He maintains a motto to stay curious, question beliefs, and persist in what matters.

Patients with severe depression who failed conventional treatment for years are affected by this work. Dr. Li's 2024 JAMA Psychiatry analysis showed that treatment-resistant depression often runs in families. First-degree relatives of these patients were 9.16 times more likely to receive the same diagnosis. This study used national health insurance data for all of Taiwan to reach its conclusion. The research emphasizes that biological adaptation may push a patient further along the resistance continuum.

Dr. Li began his career in Taichung and later trained in functional neuroimaging. He earned a PhD under Professor Jen-Chuen Hsieh and Professor Tung-Ping Su at the Institute of Brain Science. He completed a fellowship with Professor Robert Innis at the U.S. National Institute of Mental Health. His 2014 study in the journal Brain tested theta-burst stimulation for refractory depression. He also helped bring repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation toward regulatory approval for depression in Taiwan.

Dr. Li is now developing new treatments using brain stimulation and emerging approaches such as psychedelics. He wants to share knowledge through books, public lectures, social media, and AI-based mental health chatbots. He serves as a Councilor of the International College of Neuropsychopharmacology and founded the Taiwanese Society of Brain Stimulation. That society held its first annual meeting in August 2026 to discuss these advancements. The articles leave open how these new treatments and chatbots will be implemented.

stories.Headline: Ambience Healthcare adds rounding and discharge AI tools for hospitals
stories.Summary:
Ambience Healthcare announced on Tuesday that it has added two AI tools, Rounding Assistant and Discharge Readiness, to its hospital software, which already writes clinical notes and suggests billing codes for hospital stays. Rounding Assistant pulls together overnight events, changes in a patient's condition and a list of suggested tasks for each shift. Discharge Readiness flags medical, practical and social problems that could delay a patient going home, earlier in the stay. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins and the OpenAI Startup Fund, and it counts Cleveland Clinic and Mayo Clinic among its customers.

Much of the company's pitch is about money, because Ambience aims to raise hospitals' case mix index, a measure of how sick patients are that helps set what insurers pay. At Onvida Health, discharges handled with Ambience scored 6.5% higher than a year earlier, according to the company. Mike Lewis, chief financial officer of Onvida Medical Group, said Onvida needed roughly a 1.5% improvement in case mix index to justify the investment, and he said Onvida's own finance team checked the results. Ambience also says admission notes written with its tool captured 59% more of the diagnoses used in quality rankings, in one health system's review of 1,100 stays. None of the figures come from independent research.

Ambience ties its fees to results, and Lewis said the improvement was needed to justify the investment, with Onvida's finance team checking the figures. The company says its tools help care teams prioritise tasks and spot barriers to discharge earlier. AI note tools are still under scrutiny, because in August England's patient watchdog warned that AI scribes were getting drug names and diagnoses wrong. Rivals are growing fast too, with Heidi raising $340M in September and Google launching Gemini for healthcare last week.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO following a GPU cloud scandal
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO, and director of Nvidia on Thursday, November 14, 2026. This sudden departure followed reporting that focused on the business of GPU clouds. The scandal involves the Nvidia Cloud Partners programme and its relationship with specific chip providers. Huang's resignation was effective immediately upon the announcement by the company. The reporting suggests that his leadership style and specific associations led to this outcome.

The changes include the CFO becoming interim CEO while the board names its first chair. The board is now searching for a permanent replacement among internal and external candidates. The scandal involves Alice Huang, a former managing director of Megaspeed in Singapore. Megaspeed is a GPU cloud and an Nvidia Cloud Partner that may have exported chips to China. These events relate to a private dinner in Taipei seen by Reuters in May 2025.

Nvidia stated that Jensen Huang resigned from his three primary leadership roles effective immediately. The company did not provide further details beyond the resignation and the interim leadership plan. The board is now responsible for finding a permanent chief executive to lead the firm. They are currently reviewing candidates from both inside and outside the organization. The CFO will manage operations until a permanent successor is officially named.

Federal investigators and US intelligence officials expressed concerns regarding Alice Huang and her business dealings. Officials worried that she might have been acting on behalf of Chinese intelligence services. Indian startups like Gnani are affected because they rely on GPU clouds for AI compute. These firms use clouds like Yotta, Neysa, and E2E Networks to access Nvidia chips. Reliance Jio and Tata Communications are the only Indian firms with the advanced GH200 chips.

The background involves a supply chain where TSMC in Taiwan makes most of the chips. Jensen Huang previously told staff not to consider the risk of Taiwan being cut off. He ran the company with a temper that made employees afraid to question his decisions. Indian AI firms prioritize the availability of 256 H100 chips over the cost of rental. This creates a market where access to compute is the most valuable product.

Nvidia will continue to supply chips to the three main companies leasing AI compute in India. The company will likely continue releasing software that affects how these clouds operate. The board must still decide which candidate will take over as the permanent CEO. It remains unclear how the US intelligence investigation will impact other Cloud Partners. The articles leave open whether more executives will face scrutiny over chip exports.

stories.Headline: Together AI researchers delete megakernels and build an AI agent compiler that beats them by 28 percent on B200
stories.Summary:
Dylan Lim, Reyna Abhyankar, and Simran Arora wrote about the Together Compiler on November 16, 2026. This new framework uses AI agents to rewrite and fuse GPU kernels during a model's forward pass. The team previously built megakernels that executed an entire forward pass within one single fused GPU kernel. They deleted those megakernels this year to move toward a more flexible optimization system. This shift allows the company to handle increasingly heterogeneous AI inference and new model architectures.

The Together Compiler beats hand-written megakernels by 28 percent on B200 hardware. It achieved 2,118 tokens per second compared to 1,649 tokens per second on Llama 3.2 1B. Using multi-kernels and agent loops on H100 hardware reached over 1100 TPS for Llama 1B. The team found that CUDA Graphs and PDL on Torch Inductor kernels recovered 98 percent of megakernel performance. This new approach is more scalable than the previous system which served only one customer.

The authors stated that AI inference is becoming more heterogeneous with new architectures released every week. They explained that achieving peak performance across different regimes requires optimization frameworks that can keep up. The researchers noted that Torch Compile's heuristics and benchmarking leave performance on the table. They argued that the space of possible optimizations is too large for guessing the right flags. Consequently, they believe the system should search for optimizations systematically instead of relying on local heuristics.

The authors found that Torch Inductor's greedy fusion algorithm misses opportunities to merge beneficial kernels. They noted that Inductor's benchmarking ignores caching behavior, making isolated benchmarks 39 to 58 percent slower. This affects models like Llama 1B, where Inductor delivers 669 TPS without the new optimizations. Mixture-of-experts architectures like GLM 5.3 are also affected by unrealistic benchmarking inputs. These discrepancies lead to faulty compiler decisions that slow down the overall inference process.

The company spent two years investigating what a next-generation system for inference optimization should look like. They previously developed specialized implementations including FlashAttention, ThunderKittens, and the original megakernels. They discovered that enabling the freezing flag improved throughput by 10 to 26 percent at large batch sizes. However, that same flag caused a 49 percent slowdown when the batch size was one. As of Q3 2026, Inductor exposes 607 tuning flags to control memory and scheduling.

The team will share their journey in three parts, starting with the failures of Torch Compile. Part two decomposes megakernel performance gains into simpler primitives to explain why they are not always ideal. Part three will cover the bitter lessons learned from crafting agent-driven optimization infrastructure. The articles leave open the specific details of the final production system's internal agent loops. They also do not detail the specific results for the 40 plus models chosen for production.

stories.Headline: Nebius reports record third quarter revenue of $980.8 million, up 571%
stories.Summary:
Nebius Group N.V. held its third-quarter earnings call, Tipranks reported on Sunday, November 15, 2026, and the call carried a strongly optimistic tone led by record revenue, improving profitability and intense demand for AI computing. Nebius reported record third-quarter revenue of $980.8 million, up 571% from a year earlier and 68% from the second quarter. Management said most of the growth came from capacity added during the past 12 months. Nebius AI Cloud generated $973.8 million in revenue, a 643% year-over-year increase, and the segment represented about 99% of group revenue. Group adjusted EBITDA reached $465.8 million, compared with a loss of $5.2 million a year earlier and $236.2 million in the second quarter.

Agreements completed in the quarter exceeded $25 million per megawatt, compared with $20 million to $25 million in the prior quarter. Nebius said it was signing multibillion-dollar AI cloud agreements in the fourth quarter, following its first contracts worth more than $1 billion announced three months earlier. Databricks, Datadog and Snowflake signed multiyear agreements with Nebius for the first time during the quarter, while Palantir also entered into a multiyear deal. More than 90% of third-quarter contract value included a prepayment, and the weighted average share of prepayments rose by about 20 percentage points from the second quarter. These payments covered more than 100% of the capital required to bring contracted capacity online, up from 50% to 60% previously.

The payback period for new capacity shortened to one year and seven months from one year and 10 months in the prior quarter. Nebius ended the quarter with $7.4 billion in cash and equivalents, alongside a $775 million asset-backed financing facility and a $5.75 billion convertible notes offering. It also raised about $1 billion through its share program, while management cited more than $40 billion of similar committed revenue available for future asset-backed financing. The adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 47.5% from 40.6%, while the AI Cloud margin increased to 53.2% from 50%. Nebius builds its own compute infrastructure, racks and storage while developing its software platform in-house.

Management said AI-native companies still accounted for most of the more than $12 billion in contract value signed since the start of the third quarter. Token Factory accelerated in the third quarter and early fourth quarter, and management said it is on track for annual recurring revenue in the hundreds of millions. The company integrated the Eigen, Clarifai and Inferize acquisitions, and Inferize adds model-loading capabilities designed to reduce cold starts and improve GPU use for workloads with uneven demand. Most of the company’s next gigawatt of capacity is expected to come from owned sites, and Alabama, Missouri, two Finland projects and Pennsylvania were identified as important capacity locations.

Token Factory has acted as a launch partner for models from Meta, Reflection, NVIDIA and other developers. Several colocation sites, including New Jersey, are behind schedule, although management said none of the affected capacity had been canceled. Some deployments have moved into 2027, shifting part of expected 2026 revenue into the beginning of the following year. Vineland was delayed after DataOne decided to wind down temporary generation sooner than expected, and management said the site would still experience a gap and a delay of roughly two months.

Nebius reduced its 2026 revenue outlook to $3.0 billion to $3.2 billion from $3.0 billion to $3.4 billion, attributing the change to the timing of third-party capacity. The company now expects 2026 capital expenditures of about $27 billion, above its previous range of $20 billion to $25 billion. Nebius recognized about $325 million of nonrecurring revenue in the quarter from an asset-light rollout in which partners fund capacity and deploy Nebius’ architecture and AI cloud platform. Management said quarterly EBITDA margins can move when new sites incur rent, power and staffing costs before generating revenue, and fourth-quarter results will include some of these early costs.

For 2026, Nebius expects an adjusted EBITDA margin of about 40%, more than $10 billion in customer prepayments, contracted power of 5 gigawatts by year-end and ARR to exceed $7 billion in February. Nebius expects 2027 revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, with pretax breakeven targeted for the fourth quarter. It expects $40 billion to $45 billion of capital spending for more than one gigawatt of new capacity, with 75% to 85% funded through prepayments and asset-backed financing, while customer prepayments are expected to reach $17 billion to $20 billion. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Nebius plans $40bn to $45bn 2027 infrastructure spend as CEO Arkady Volozh warns site delays hit Microsoft capacity
stories.Summary:
Nebius announced on November 12, 2026, a planned capital spending outline of $40 billion to $45 billion for 2027, according to CASRAI. The AI Insider reported on November 16, 2026, that the neocloud company warned delays at third-party sites are weighing on its AI infrastructure buildout. CEO Arkady Volozh said building at this scale is hard and that Nebius is not immune to industry-wide delays. Capacity for Microsoft at a Vineland, New Jersey, site run by DataOne has slipped, with just over half now due by year-end and the rest in Q2 2027. Nebius reported third-quarter revenue of $981 million, up 571%, but cut its 2026 forecast to $3 billion, and shares fell 17%.

The 2027 plan projects between $40 billion and $45 billion in infrastructure spending to expand global GPU clusters and data centre operations. The plan follows a revision of the full-year 2026 capital expenditure target to approximately $27 billion. Nebius aims to surpass one gigawatt of operational power capacity across its facilities. The Microsoft contract is worth up to $19.4 billion and allows Microsoft to terminate affected service and impose penalties for missed dates. A primary bottleneck occurred at a 300-megawatt data centre facility in Vineland, New Jersey, operated by partner DataOne.

Chief product and infrastructure officer Andrey Korolenko attributed the delay to DataOne winding down temporary generation faster than expected as it moves to Bloom Energy fuel cells. Volozh said Nebius is not immune to industry-wide delays. Nebius said Microsoft has been part of the planning. Chief revenue officer Marc Boroditsky said deals with Microsoft and Meta included large prepayments. CFO Maria Del Dado Alonso Sanchez said prepayments and contract-backed financing should cover up to 85% of 2027 spending.

CASRAI said management indicated roughly 75% to 85% of the projected capital outlay will be covered by customer prepayments on qualifying long-term contracts and asset-backed credit facilities secured against investment-grade commercial commitments. Site commissioning faced regulatory scrutiny from the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection regarding temporary natural gas generation units, prompting an accelerated transition to permanent Bloom Energy fuel cells. The resulting timeline revisions pushed commercial activation for certain capacity blocks from late 2026 into the first half of 2027. Nebius expects 2027 revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion. The neocloud commercial model is predicated on multi-year, multi-million-dollar take-or-pay agreements backed by substantial upfront cash prepayments.

Nebius operates within the rapidly expanding category of specialised GPU neocloud providers, offering high-density compute clusters distinct from traditional general-purpose hyperscale cloud architectures. Recent transactions with major industry partners, including multi-billion-dollar capacity agreements with Microsoft and Meta, underscore how hyperscalers are leasing wholesale capacity blocks from specialized operators. To mitigate counterparty and operational risks inherent in third-party development, Nebius is shifting future capacity additions toward owned-and-operated sites. The company's expansion roadmap focuses on scaling proprietary sites, including a second facility in Mäntsälä and new development in Lappeenranta, Finland, alongside domestic US campus developments in Missouri and Alabama. As facilities expand to multi-hundred-megawatt scales, the environmental footprint and power grid interactions become critical operational factors.

Very few academic institutions possess the balance sheet flexibility or procurement authority to enter into multi-year capacity prepayment arrangements, leaving research groups at a structural disadvantage when seeking direct access to leading-edge GPU architectures. As major hyperscalers contract large tranches of neocloud capacity wholesale to satisfy commercial enterprise commitments, spot and on-demand GPU capacity for academic researchers becomes increasingly scarce and volatile in pricing. Research teams undertaking compute FLOPs estimation for grant proposals must frequently adjust computing budgets upward to account for shifting cloud pricing tiers. For universities, managing access to scalable research data infrastructure increasingly requires hybrid strategies that combine campus-level clusters, national consortium allocations such as the National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource (NAIRR), and structured institutional cloud agreements. Research computing administrators must ensure external cloud compute deployments comply with institutional research data management policies and data sovereignty requirements.

stories.Headline: Kyndryl finds 64% of leaders report positive AI returns as readiness for external risks falls to 24%
stories.Summary:
Kyndryl released findings from its third annual Readiness Report on November 10, 2026, in New York, showing a widening divide between AI returns and readiness to manage risks. The report found that 64% of leaders report positive returns on AI investments, up 10 points from 2025. Average readiness across external risks fell seven points to 24%, with the steepest declines in readiness for cyber threats and competitive disruption. The report captures the attitudes and actions of 3,700 senior business leaders across 21 countries. The data shows organizations racing to deliver returns on significant AI investments while feeling ill-equipped to navigate the implications for the AI era.

Significantly fewer leaders describe themselves as in the experimentation phase compared to a year ago, down 13 points from 2025 to 49%. Nearly half, 48%, substantially changed their AI strategies this year, with implications across tech, people and governance. About a quarter, 24%, saw an AI investment fail, and 21% canceled a major AI initiative. Just 27% have formally updated roles and responsibilities around AI, and 29% have fully implemented change management for AI adoption. Those who have done both are 28 points more likely to be completely ready for their AI implementation and 8 points more likely to report positive ROI on their AI investments.

Martin Schroeter, Chairman and CEO of Kyndryl, said that as AI creates significant opportunity, organizations are now focusing on how to make early returns sustainable. He said this year's Readiness Report shows a new kind of readiness gap, with AI ambitions moving faster than the systems needed to support them. He said the bar for readiness keeps moving as AI becomes more integrated in enterprises. He said Kyndryl's data shows that focusing on people, technology and governance can help organizations win with AI and keep the ability to adapt as opportunities evolve. Kyndryl is described as a leading provider of mission-critical enterprise technology services and trades on the NYSE under KD.

For the third year in a row, security concerns topped the list of external risks and contributed most to the overall decline in readiness. Just 26% of firms said they were completely ready for cyberattacks, a drop of 11 points from last year. Three in four leaders say AI helps their organizations identify threats faster, even as confidence in their ability to respond to cyberattacks has declined. The second-largest drop in readiness came from leaders' concerns about competitive disruptions outside of their industry, down 10 points from 2025 to 23%. Retailers are weighing how to benefit from AI shopping assistants without forfeiting direct customer relationships, software companies face questions about SaaS models as AI rebalances the build-versus-buy equation, and financial institutions are challenged by emerging lending models.

The research captures how leaders are considering digital sovereignty in a year marked by greater actions by governments, most visibly in the European Union. Leaders in the EU are slightly less likely to have taken sovereignty-related actions compared to those in the rest of the world. 68% say solutions offering full operational control, should they need it, are worth a premium of 10% or more, and 60% say greater control is worth slower deployment and adoption of advanced capabilities. For the third year in a row, leaders said upgrading their IT infrastructure was the number one action their organizations are taking to mitigate external risks, and 71% rate their infrastructure as mostly or fully modernized. Yet two-thirds of CIOs surveyed think their technology foundations need significant re-architecture before being fully ready for AI at scale.

The report is Kyndryl's third annual Readiness Report, and the 2026-27 Readiness Report is promoted on Kyndryl's site as exploring how organizations are navigating AI adoption, IT modernization and evolving business demands. Kyndryl's 2026 People Readiness Report is described as revealing a decline in workforce readiness as AI adoption surges, and what leading organizations are doing to prepare. The articles state that 66% of CIOs believe their infrastructure requires significant re-architecture before it can support AI at scale. The articles do not state what Kyndryl plans to do next with the findings, and they leave open which specific countries or industries drove the declines. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Nvidia stops reporting Singapore unit revenue in 2025 after it reaches $104bn, nearly half of global sales
stories.Summary:
Nvidia stopped reporting revenue for its Singapore unit in 2025, according to documents cited by the Financial Times, after that unit accounted for nearly 50% of the company's global revenue. The Singapore unit's revenue rose 72% year on year to $104bn in 2025, the documents show. The disclosure change came as the unit grew to represent almost half of Nvidia's worldwide sales. The Financial Times reported the details on Tuesday, November 17, 2026.

The documents indicate that the Singapore unit's revenue reached $104bn in 2025, a 72% increase from the prior year. That figure represented nearly 50% of Nvidia's global revenue for the year, according to the same documents. Nvidia stopped disclosing the unit's sales in 2025, the Financial Times reported, meaning the breakdown is no longer part of its regular reporting. The report does not say why the company made the change.

The Financial Times is the source of the report, which is based on documents it reviewed rather than on statements from Nvidia. The article does not include any comment from Nvidia or from company executives about the decision to stop reporting the Singapore unit's revenue. No explanation is given in the available material for why the disclosure ended in 2025. The report also does not say whether the company plans to resume reporting the figure.

The available article is a subscription page and does not provide further context on what the change requires or what happens next. It does not say how the missing Singapore figures affect Nvidia's overall reporting or what regulators or investors have said about it. The report gives no indication of any response from Nvidia or from Singapore authorities. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Elastic launches private preview of nightshift AI SRE agent for observability investigations
stories.Summary:
Elastic announced on November 17, 2026, a private preview of Elastic nightshift AI SRE, an AI agent built into Elastic Observability that carries out investigations the way an engineer would and makes the work visible, according to a press release from Elasticsearch Corporation, the Tokyo-based subsidiary led by president Ken Otani. The agent continuously detects and investigates problems across the whole stack with full context, surfacing unknown issues that rule-based alerts would miss, and it tests several hypotheses about root causes in parallel against telemetry and other relevant context. It then gives engineers evidence-backed answers while showing its reasoning at each step, and once it identifies a likely root cause it proposes remediation, either by selecting existing workflows and preconfigured actions or by providing commands for engineers to run. Engineers can inspect every step of an investigation, including the queries the agent ran and the underlying data. The release cites an April 2026 NeuBird AI survey finding that 78 percent of companies reported at least one incident in the past year where there was no alert and users themselves were the first to notice the problem.

Elastic says context behind investigations is usually incomplete because telemetry is cut to save costs, knowledge is scattered across code, runbooks and Slack, and lessons from past incidents are lost, while standalone AI SRE tools reason over data they do not hold. Because each investigation draws on full context from cost-efficient telemetry storage, customers can keep everything rather than sample data for AI, and a knowledge graph links that telemetry to source code from GitHub repositories so the agent can identify the commit likely behind an exception. Records of investigations accumulate over time, so each resolved incident shortens the time needed for the next one, and the agent continuously evaluates the environment and all telemetry, correlating alerts, SLOs and anomalies into findings engineers should actually review. Shannon Kalvar, a senior research director at IDC, said named-role agents such as AI SRE are a first step toward AI-driven operations, and that these agents need access to broader context, especially across wide and heterogeneous environments, along with the ability to learn from their own actions while validating those actions against facts.

Baha Azarmi, general manager of observability at Elastic, said most observability agents get smarter only by collecting more data, whereas Elastic nightshift AI SRE gets smarter by closely observing how engineers conduct investigations and by verifying the results of its own work after incidents are closed, which keeps production running without unwanted token costs. The private preview is available starting today on Elastic Observability Serverless, and Elastic customers can use it free during the early access period. Elastic plans to broaden support for third-party tools and data stores and to publish a technical preview within the year, and customers who want the private preview can register online. The Japanese release is an abridged translation of an English release Elastic published on October 8, 2026, and Elastic, listed on the NYSE under ESTC, says its platform is used by thousands of companies including more than 75 percent of Fortune 100 firms.

stories.Headline: Cato Networks launches AgentSense to block harmful AI agent actions in real time
stories.Summary:
Cato Networks announced on November 17, 2026, a patented capability called Cato AgentSense from Cato AI Labs that continuously assesses AI agents in real time to protect the integrity of their decisions, actions and outputs as they operate autonomously. The company said the guardrail stops harmful agent actions before they execute, keeping enterprises in control as agents gain greater autonomy. AgentSense is integrated within the Cato platform and will be included at no additional charge within Cato AI Usage licenses. Cato also introduced the AgentSense Challenge, which invites the security community to attack an AI agent workflow protected by AgentSense and plant instructions aimed at steering it away from the user's intent, with the first three eligible participants to succeed each receiving $10,000 USD.

The capability rests on two detection methods. Untrusted Influence Detection traces how instructions and data influence an agent's behavior at runtime, and when it detects that untrusted content is steering the agent toward an unsafe action, it blocks that action before execution, providing protection against indirect prompt injection even when attacks do not match previously observed patterns. Instead of relying on static classifiers or known attack patterns, it separates trusted instructions from untrusted content inside the AI session and traces how untrusted content influences both behavior and outputs, which Cato describes as a one-of-its-kind layer of protection from zero-day vulnerabilities. Drift Detection will identify when agent actions depart from the original task or intent, evaluating as a workflow progresses whether actions still serve the intended objective and flagging steps that may be individually permitted but fall outside the given task.

Shlomo Kramer, CEO and co-founder of Cato Networks, said enterprises entrust agents with decisions that shape revenue, customer relationships and business continuity, so control over agent behavior has become as essential as financial controls. He said giving agents greater autonomy requires security that can intervene before their actions cause harm, and that the vision for AgentSense is to give enterprises confidence to put agents in charge of critical business processes while retaining control over how they operate. Nithin Reddy, vice president of cybersecurity at Dayforce, said scaling AI safely means having the ability to detect and stop actions that could put customers, data or business at risk. Itay Ravia, head of Cato AI Labs, cited DuneSlide, EchoLeak and CurXecute as notable prompt injection vulnerabilities that continue to make headlines, and said AgentSense helps preserve trust by tracing how untrusted content influences an agent's decisions and sensitive actions. Grace Trinidad, senior research director of AI Security and Trust at IDC, said organizations need to know their objectives fully and evaluate agentic actions in the context of the full workflow and the task the agent was authorized to perform.

Cato said AI agents continue to scale faster than the guardrails put in place to secure them, citing Gartner figures that 71% of organizations expect to deploy agentic AI within the next 12 months while only 21% currently have agentic AI governance capabilities in place. It said forecasts report that by 2028, ungoverned AI agent abuse will drive 25 percent of enterprise breaches. The company described a fundamental architectural weakness in which agents cannot reliably distinguish between trusted instructions and untrusted data they pick up as they work, letting attackers hide malicious instructions in emails, webpages, documents, tickets or tool responses, and said the combination of sensitive data access and action-taking tools turns prompt injection into a business risk. Cato said it will use participants' findings and feedback from the Challenge to evaluate and strengthen the capability.

stories.Headline: Vertiv adds 800 VDC power systems for AI compute pods and data halls
stories.Summary:
Vertiv Holdings Co. (NYSE: VRT) added 800 VDC systems for the AI compute pod and the data hall on Nov. 17, 2026, extending a portfolio that began with the May 2026 introduction of the Vertiv PowerDirect 5000 Power Rack. The company announced the expansion in a release dated Nov. 17, 2026, from Columbus, Ohio. The expanded portfolio enables operators to meet rising power demands in next-generation AI data centers and scale infrastructure as compute requirements evolve. Vertiv offers three 800 VDC architecture options spanning medium-voltage to low-voltage AC-to-800 VDC conversion at the rack, LV AC-to-800 VDC conversion at the compute pod, and MV AC-to-800 VDC conversion at the data hall. The portfolio spans power conversion, energy storage, distribution and protection, delivering power train architectures from the medium-voltage grid to the compute tray.

The Vertiv PowerDirect 3000 90 kW, 19-inch 800 VDC Power Shelf is a 1U DC-DC converter inside the compute rack that converts 800 VDC to 54 VDC for compute trays at up to 98.5% peak efficiency and supports 180% pulse power for 0.5 milliseconds. This rack architecture frees 8 to 16 rack units for additional compute, with one power rack supporting one or two IT racks, and supports both 800 VDC and ±400 VDC through minimal hardware configuration changes. The Vertiv PowerDirect 9000, 1.5 MW 800 VDC Power Center converts 480 VAC to 800 VDC for an entire row or pod, distributing power via the Vertiv PowerBar Track DC busway and tap-off boxes to the PowerDirect 3000 shelves in each rack. The pod system scales in 60 kW increments through 27 hot-pluggable power supply units, and the Vertiv EnergyCore Li5 800 VDC battery cabinet delivers 200 kW of continuous backup at up to 98% conversion efficiency, with up to six cabinets operating in parallel through active current sharing. The Vertiv PowerNexus MV SST, 5 MW 800 VDC Solid-State Transformer, converts medium-voltage AC directly to 800 VDC in a single conversion stage, eliminates two to three intermediate conversion steps, delivers up to 98% AC-to-DC efficiency, and a single unit can support a 4.8 MW super pod reference architecture without chaining.

Scott Armul, Chief Product and Technology Officer at Vertiv, said the 800 VDC power train is not just a new power product or conversion methodology but a set of architectures and system designs. Armul said delivering it takes a comprehensive portfolio that brings together power conversion, energy storage, distribution, protection, controls and safety. He added that Vertiv has built a system-level 800 VDC portfolio giving customers flexibility to implement 800 VDC across different data center configurations. He said every layer, from the medium-voltage grid to the compute tray, is designed to work together, with safety built for DC operation. Kyle Keeper, Senior Vice President of Vertiv's Power Management Business Unit, said different operators have different requirements, whether building new AI facilities, upgrading existing sites, or supporting a mix of tenants and workloads.

Vertiv said AC and DC architectures are expected to coexist, making flexibility in power conversion, distribution and deployment essential, and that operators have different facilities, workloads, business models, risk tolerances and investment horizons. Vertiv said its role is to help operators determine which architecture matches their needs, and its portfolio lets operators introduce 800 VDC at different points in the power train without committing an entire data center to a single architecture. The rack architecture suits brownfield environments, retrofit scenarios and facilities running mixed AC and DC architectures, while the pod architecture suits colocation providers serving tenants with different workload types and GPU generations. The data hall architecture is designed for operators building purpose-built AI factories at campus scale, and its outdoor, liquid-cooled and containerized design reduces physical footprint and supports faster deployment and standardized replication across campuses. Vertiv 800 VDC architectures include touch-proof busbars, high voltage isolation, midpoint grounding, ground-fault detection and arc-flash prevention, supported by Vertiv Services offerings developed for DC environments.

Vertiv is headquartered in Westerville, Ohio, USA, and does business in more than 130 countries. Vertiv is showcasing its 800 VDC portfolio at SC26, the International Conference for High-Performance Computing, Networking, Storage, and Analysis, Nov. 17-22, 2026. Pilot programs, technical validation activities and collaborative development initiatives tailored to customers' deployment needs are currently underway. Vertiv experts are ready to discuss these solutions and engage on next steps. The release includes forward-looking statements and refers readers to Vertiv's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including its most recent Annual Report on Form 10-K and any subsequent Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q.

Vertiv said bidirectional power flow enables improved grid power quality and can provide active power support, and that battery communication ports coordinate with energy storage systems to manage the rapid load fluctuations of AI workloads. The data hall design provides fault ride-through and AI power smoothing when connected to external energy storage with a DC/DC converter coupled on the 800 VDC bus. The pod architecture consolidates power conversion into a single system ahead of the row, reducing component count and eliminating the need for individual power racks alongside each IT rack. The rack architecture moves power conversion and energy storage outside the IT rack and lets operators retain existing upstream AC infrastructure, helping simplify deployment without a facility redesign. Vertiv said 800 VDC cannot be reduced to a sidecar, a rectifier, or a single component, and that its portfolio covers power conversion, energy storage, distribution, protection, controls and monitoring to deliver a coordinated, end-to-end system.

The award is given by TMC's CUSTOMER magazine, and CAIRO was selected for its ability to use Voice AI to enhance customer engagement through intelligent call handling, automation, and orchestration capabilities. Crexendo describes CAIRO as the Crexendo AI Receptionist and Orchestrator, and the company says the product helps organizations improve satisfaction, streamline operations, and build stronger customer relationships. The company also says CAIRO delivers seamless, responsive, and highly personalized customer experiences for the businesses that use it.

Crexendo says CAIRO is an important component of its strategy to accelerate organic growth through AI-powered solutions, and that providing advanced AI capabilities through its NetSapiens cloud communications platform will create additional revenue opportunities for the company and its service provider licensees. The company says businesses increasingly seek intelligent automation to improve productivity, reduce operating costs, and enhance customer engagement, and that CAIRO and its expanding portfolio of AI solutions can drive increased adoption and additional recurring revenue. Crexendo states that its solutions support over eight million end users globally through a network of more than 250 cloud communication platform software subscribers and its direct retail offering. The press release also notes that TMC has been honoring technology companies with awards for more than 20 years, and that the company's forward-looking statements are subject to risks described in its Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, and its Form 10-Qs filed with the SEC.

Rich Tehrani, CEO of TMC, congratulated all of the 2026 Voice AI Technology Excellence Award winners and said the recipients represent some of the most innovative and impactful companies in voice technology. He said their commitment to excellence, customer success, and continuous innovation is helping shape the future of communications. Jeff Korn, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Crexendo, said the company is extremely pleased that CAIRO received the recognition, which he said further validates its commitment to making Crexendo and the NetSapiens platform leaders in AI-powered cloud communications. Korn said artificial intelligence represents one of the most significant opportunities to accelerate organic growth and create meaningful new revenue streams for Crexendo and its licensees, and he added that the ability to bring these innovations to an ecosystem supporting more than eight million end users is particularly exciting.

According to the release, earning an Excellence Award from TMC's CUSTOMER magazine elevates the Crexendo brand before TMC's audience of technology professionals, decision makers, and executives, along with their ecosystem of end users and other providers. Crexendo says the recognition underscores its influence on the future of customer engagement through intelligent cloud communications, and that it continues to advance its innovation leadership by delivering an AI-powered software platform. Korn said that as AI adoption accelerates, the expanding portfolio of AI solutions can generate additional recurring revenue, increase the value of the platform to existing customers, attract new licensees, and provide a meaningful catalyst for long-term growth. The release states that forward-looking statements speak only as of the date they are made and that the company undertakes no obligation to update them except as required by law.
