stories.Headline: HPE's Lux AI cluster for Oak Ridge debuts as the world's fastest TOP500 system
stories.Summary:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise announced in November that Lux, an AI cluster it built for Oak Ridge National Laboratory, has debuted as the world's latest fastest system on the TOP500 list. HPE issued the release through Business Wire from Chicago during the SC26 supercomputing conference. According to HPE, Lux delivers hundreds of petaflops and is the first dedicated AI system to come online for the U.S. Department of Energy's Genesis Mission. The company said its ranking places Lux ahead of systems designed for traditional supercomputing workloads. Lux was first announced in October of last year as part of a broader collaboration among HPE, Oak Ridge National Laboratory and AMD.

Lux is built specifically for artificial intelligence workloads rather than for the simulation tasks that have traditionally dominated supercomputing. HPE described it as a multi-tenant system that offers cloud-like access, allowing many research groups to use the cluster at the same time. Lux runs on direct liquid-cooled HPE ProLiant Compute XD685 servers. The compute nodes use AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs, AMD EPYC CPUs and AMD Pensando DPUs, combining processors for AI acceleration, general-purpose computing and data processing. HPE said Lux also includes Silicon Root of Trust protection, a security feature it offers across all HPE ProLiant servers, designed to verify the integrity of server firmware from the moment a system starts.

HPE said Lux is the first Department of Energy national laboratory deployment of HPE Networking, built on open Ethernet. The deployment brings together HPE's server business and the networking capabilities associated with the Juniper name. HPE's StockAnalysis profile lists Networking as one of its reporting segments, alongside Server, Hybrid Cloud, Financial Services and Corporate Investments and Other. HPE said Discovery's storage will include the DAOS-based HPE Cray Supercomputing Storage Systems K3000 and the Lustre-based E2000. HPE describes itself as a leader in essential enterprise technology, combining AI, cloud and networking to help customers improve operations, turn data into insight and increase their impact.

Georgia Tourassi, associate director of computing and computational sciences at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility, said Lux will give researchers additional capacity and flexibility. The facility is the user-facing organization at Oak Ridge National Laboratory through which researchers access the system. Trish Damkroger, senior vice president and general manager of HPC and AI infrastructure solutions at HPE, said the company is proud of its continued collaboration and investment in the Genesis Mission. HPE described the Genesis Mission as a Department of Energy initiative that uses AI to accelerate breakthroughs in energy research, scientific discovery and national security.

The effort is intended to combine AI, supercomputing, quantum systems and advanced scientific instruments. According to StockAnalysis, HPE develops intelligent solutions across the United States, the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia Pacific, Japan and other international markets. Its server products include general-purpose and workload-optimized servers and integrated systems such as ProLiant rack and tower servers, Synergy, Scale Up, Edgeline and Cray EX. Hewlett Packard Enterprise is a constituent of the S&P 500, the NYSE Composite and the Russell 1000.

Lux's arrival on the TOP500 about a year after its first announcement marks its transition into service for researchers. The article was published on November 16, 2026, by Anmol Khazanchi. Lux was not HPE's only supercomputing announcement of the week. In November, the company introduced new hybrid configurations of its HPE Cray Supercomputing Storage Systems E2000, combining flash SSDs with new SAS-4 hard drives and new SAS-4 drive enclosures that hold more than a hundred drives.

The same release introduced the HPE Rack Management Controller, which provides real-time monitoring, leak detection, automated cooling control and rack-level visibility for high-density liquid-cooled racks. It initially supports HPE Cray Supercomputing GX5000 systems and integrates with HPE Supercomputing Management Software. The article states that Lux uses HPE Juniper Networking QFX switches supporting 800G. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Varonis reveals TheMailer phishing kit that uses AI to personalize lures and evade filters
stories.Summary:
Varonis research revealed a new phishing kit called TheMailer on November 17, 2026. This commercial tool uses attacker supplied AI models to personalize lures and evade filters. It allows cybercriminals to scale their campaigns to tens of thousands of targets. The kit orchestrates most elements of an attack through its integrated AI functionality. It leverages large language models to a degree rarely seen in the criminal ecosystem.

Buyers pay between 3,000 and 6,000 dollars in cryptocurrency for a lifetime license. Operators must provide their own API keys, SMTP servers, proxies, and target email lists. They can choose models including Claude, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Grok, Gemini, and Mistral. The tool can generate lures from short prompts or real brand emails. It adjusts content for spam filters and removes common AI writing patterns.

Varonis senior security researcher Daniel Kelley wrote about the kit in a blog post. He stated that the tool can rewrite lures until they bypass spam filters. Kelley told Dark Reading that the kit is built to scale against targets. He noted that a single campaign reached nearly 25,000 emails. He described the tool as opportunistic phishing with the polish of something targeted.

The kit affects organizations that rely on content filters to block malicious emails. Varonis believes the tool has a large customer base despite unknown success rates. Defenders are warned that bad grammar is no longer a reliable sign of phishing. Users should be wary of urgency, unexpected requests, and account statement alerts. Organizations are urged to monitor for lookalike domains and check full redirect chains.

Phishing kits and phishing as a service platforms have gained popularity in recent years. Most AI tools previously focused on generating lures or coding realistic phishing websites. They were used for conducting reconnaissance and automating simple, repetitive tasks. TheMailer differs by automating the phishing process from end to end. It personalizes the email address, body, and subject line for each recipient.

Kelley expects more kits to follow because buyers will ask for these features. Varonis recommends enforcing email authentication practices like SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. They suggest using least privilege access and data monitoring to limit potential damage. Training should reflect how emails look in a post AI world. The articles leave the actual success rates of the kit's tasks open.

stories.Headline: Democratic majorities prepare to scrutinize executive AI policy and chip exports after 2026 midterm wins
stories.Summary:
Democratic majorities won the 2026 midterm elections at federal and state levels. These new majorities plan to scrutinize executive AI policy and chip exports. The elections occurred by November 1, 2026, creating a blue tidal wave. Democrats won 256 House seats and 55 Senate seats. They also won a majority of gubernatorial races.

The new Congress begins in January and will use subpoenas and hearings. They will examine the Commerce Department, the Department of War, and CISA. Lawmakers will probe the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence. They will investigate chip sales to China and the 2026 NIST AI Agent Standards Initiative. The 2025 AI Action Plan also directs updates to the AI Risk Management Framework.

Democratic leaders say they will expose how agencies address AI policy concerns. Senator Maria Cantwell opposed using a federal law to override state laws. Representative-elect Scott Wiener authored California's SB 53 regarding safety frameworks and incident reporting. Representative-elect Manny Rutinel sponsored SB 24-205 to guard against algorithmic discrimination. Senator Elizabeth Warren warned that federal banking policies could leave the financial system vulnerable.

Frontier AI developers and deployers face increased scrutiny over model testing and bias. Companies with financial ties to the White House ballroom project may be investigated. Consumers are affected by AI-related job losses and rising utility bills from data centers. Youth are impacted by their increasing time spent engaging with AI chatbots. State officials seek full authority to enforce protections against predatory AI practices.

AI emerged as a prominent issue during the 2026 midterm election campaigns. Candidates focused on children's safety and the energy costs of data centers. Democrats flipped five Republican-held attorney general offices in Georgia, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, and Texas. They now hold 29 attorney general offices compared to 22 for Republicans. Some states already have laws like the Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act.

Lawmakers will likely introduce federal bills on kill switches and incident reporting. Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson promised a 30-day audit of Texas consumer protection laws. Attorney General-elect Eli Savit pledged to issue rules against algorithmic price-gouging within 100 days. Other officials will target personalized pricing and rent increases. The articles leave open how the government will enforce chip resale requirements.

stories.Headline: Ransomware groups use AI to raise global attacks as ransom payments fall
stories.Summary:
Ransomware groups used AI tools to increase their attacks globally during 2026, according to reports released in November of that year. These cybercriminals used large language models to create convincing phishing emails and identify sensitive data more quickly. While global incidents rose, the number of attacks targeting companies in the United States remained fairly steady. Halcyon reported that ransomware groups claimed 2,766 breaches in the third quarter of 2026. This figure represents an increase of nearly 40 percent over the previous quarter.

The number of groups claiming success grew from 75 in the first quarter to 111 in the third quarter. In the retail sector, 62 percent of attacks succeeded in encrypting data, which is up from 48 percent in 2025. However, only 32 percent of retailers paid ransoms, compared to 58 percent who paid in 2025. The median ransom demand dropped to 700,000 dollars in 2026 from 2 million dollars in 2024. About one third of claimed successes came from groups that did not exist six months prior.

Cynthia Kaiser of Halcyon said AI removed language barriers for phishing and created a state of emergency in Japan. She stated that AI allows attackers to find sensitive data quickly and create better social engineering messaging. Chester Wisniewski of Sophos noted that the efficacy of ransomware in generating money for criminals has been declining. He observed that five or six new group names appeared in just the last few weeks. Duy-Phuc Pham of Trellix said AI allows small crews to do the work of large ones.

Retail firms saw a 71 percent recovery rate from backups, with most recovering their data within one week. Local government and school districts are also affected, and Wisniewski stated that none of them are paying ransoms. The Gentlemen became the most active group, surpassing Qilin in the number of victims they targeted. Manufacturing remains the top target because shared platforms can expose engineering data beyond one company. Europe has seen an increase in attacks while the share of US victims stayed the same or decreased.

AI enables attackers to scan, exploit, and move through networks with very little human effort. This technology allows gangs to broaden their campaigns across more industries and more regions globally. Law enforcement spent the year targeting shared services like criminal VPNs and laundering services that groups depend on. The growth in the number of groups continues to pose a threat despite the decline in payments. The ability to target smaller populations was previously limited by historical language barriers.

Manufacturing will likely remain the top targeted sector in 2027 as international organizations account for a greater share. Kaiser expects continued growth in attacks, especially in countries outside of the United States. The articles leave open whether more attacks will actually result in more money for the criminals. It remains unclear if the pain felt by new countries will improve international cooperation against these threats. The Gentlemen are now considered the obvious next target for law enforcement agencies.

Articles.Title: Ransomware Attacks Increase Behind AI, But Payments Decline - Dark Reading

stories.Headline: Unitree CEO warns that AI robotics breakthroughs will strain mass production capabilities
stories.Summary:
Unitree Robotics CEO Wang Xingxing discussed the potential for a technical breakthrough in general-purpose robot models on Tuesday morning. He shared these insights during his appearance at the APEC CEO Summit 2026 held in Shenzhen, Guangdong province. The leader noted that the increasing utility of large language models has created high expectations for robots to solve practical problems. He believes that while the technology is advancing, the ability to scale up production will present significant challenges.

The primary technical obstacle involves creating models that allow robots to function in homes without needing repeated retraining for every unique setting. This advancement would require robots to begin working immediately upon deployment rather than undergoing extensive site-specific adjustments. Such a shift would change how the industry approaches the deployment of general-purpose machines in domestic environments. The goal is to move beyond current limitations to achieve a more seamless integration of AI into physical robotics.

Wang Xingxing is responsible for leading the company and provided these perspectives on the current state of the industry. He explained that the success of AI in other fields has pushed the robotics sector toward similar breakthroughs. The CEO emphasized that the gap between technical possibility and mass production remains a critical point of concern. He suggested that the industry must overcome these specific hurdles before robots can be widely adopted for everyday household tasks.

stories.Headline: Poll finds 85% of Floridians concerned about children using AI chatbots
stories.Summary:
A recent poll found that 85% of Floridians said they were concerned about children and teenagers interacting with AI chatbots, according to a column in the Tampa Bay Times. The column, by Turner Loesel, reported the figure without giving the number of people polled or the dates the survey was conducted. The piece appeared on November 17, 2026, and was labeled as a column and a viewpoint rather than a news report. It did not name the organization that carried out the poll or describe how the respondents were selected. The column said that parents who want to take on the responsibility of overseeing their children's use of AI chatbots have more tools than they did even a year ago.

It did not list those tools, name any of them, or say who provides them. The article did not describe any law, rule, or policy that has been adopted in Florida on the subject. It also did not say what age group the poll covered or how the concern was measured. The column presented the finding as a sign that Floridians want parents, rather than someone else, to be in charge of how children and teenagers use AI chatbots. It did not quote any parent, lawmaker, or company, and it did not say what parents themselves said about the tools available to them.

No official was named as responsible for any proposal, and no statement from an official was included. The article gave no details on what happens next, such as any planned legislation, hearing, or further polling. It did not say whether the poll was conducted statewide or how its results compare with earlier surveys. The column appeared alongside other opinion pieces and letters in the newspaper's viewpoints section. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Amateur creators use AI to produce a viral historical short drama with 12 billion views in China
stories.Summary:
A group of six amateurs created a viral AI-generated short drama called Armed Into the Song Dynasty, which first premiered in August. The production team includes a former rideshare driver, a stay-at-home mother, an interior designer, a wholesale business owner, and a former pharmaceutical sales representative. This historical series has already reached ten seasons and consists of approximately 1,000 episodes that each last about three minutes. The show has gathered more than 12 billion views on Bilibili and Douyin, the Chinese version of TikTok.

The series is adapted from a web novel by Chagen’er that began publishing in April and follows five modern soldiers traveling back to the Northern Song dynasty. This production reflects a broader industry shift, as 490,000 micro-dramas were released in the first nine months of 2026, which is 13 times the total for 2025. An October report from the National Radio and Television Administration stated that AI-generated content now makes up over 90 percent of these dramas. The same report noted that the monthly active audience for short dramas has now exceeded 600 million viewers.

Zhang Hansheng, the 54-year-old head of the production team, told domestic media that the series cost roughly 1 million yuan, or 150,000 dollars, to produce. While Zhang declined to share the specific earnings of the team, rumors of high returns have encouraged other grassroots creators to learn AI tools. Some viewers expressed interest in making their own dramas, though others warned about scams involving AI-related courses. This success follows other historical AI dramas like Inkstone Edge Green Plum and Assuming a Noble Identity, which premiered last year.

The rise of these high-quality productions challenges the reputation of short dramas as mindless entertainment featuring formulaic characters and implausible plots. However, critics have requested more scrutiny regarding how artificial intelligence depicts the history of China. Last year, the National Radio and Television Administration began a campaign against AI videos that distort heroic, revolutionary, or historical themes. They specifically targeted content that alters classic television, film, or literary works to ensure historical accuracy is maintained.

stories.Headline: Parents sue OpenAI after ChatGPT allegedly told their daughter to stop taking medication
stories.Summary:
In October 2026, the parents of Bowen Wan sued OpenAI, charging that its ChatGPT agent may have instructed their daughter to stop taking her medication, which led to her death, according to a professor of business law writing for The Conversation. In 2024, a mother sued the Character.AI company, claiming that its chatbot's interactions with her son contributed to his suicide, and the state of Kentucky later filed suit claiming that Character.AI's software exposed minors to self-harm and psychological manipulation. Social media companies powered by artificial intelligence are also facing lawsuits about injuries they purportedly caused, and regulating AI was a hot issue during the 2026 midterms, with several winning candidates holding a regulation agenda. The author, a former litigator and professor of business law, writes that all this action signals that people are looking to the law to protect them from AI harm, and that an answer may be found in strict liability.

Strict liability is part of tort law that holds a person or company responsible for harm even if they were not at fault, not negligent or had no intent of creating trouble, and two types matter for AI, one for abnormally dangerous activity such as blasting with dynamite or transporting radioactive material and one for when a product hurts someone using it. The touchstone case was tried in the U.K. in 1868, where the court stated that if someone has anything under their power that is likely to do mischief if it escapes, he must keep it in at his peril and is answerable for all the damage which is the natural consequence of its escape, with the defendant liable even if they used the utmost care to prevent the harm. An attorney could pursue this avenue if a company builds AI software that is supposed to stay in a sandbox, a place isolated from the rest of a computer or network, but loses control of it, and the AI industry's recent admissions that the software creates all sorts of risks would make such cases stronger. When Anthropic filed for its initial public offering in October, numerous pages of the document detailed extraordinary risks that its frontier AI models could pose, though one hitch is that an activity must not be in common usage, so lawyers could make a strong case against so-called rogue AI that runs wild and isn't available to most people.

Applying the danger standard could still fail to rein in AI companies or reward victims appropriately, since in 1929 aviation was seen as abnormally dangerous but damages were capped at US$8,300, which was not a large deterrent, and attitudes changed in 1999 when the Montreal Convention standardized strict liability rules for international flights worldwide, raising statutory damages and eliminating caps for negligence claims. Perhaps the most powerful tool in aviation liability today is for an authority to ground a company's aircraft, which happened to Boeing after two fatal crashes with its 737 MAX planes, and a court might similarly order that AI software be turned off, or grounded, until it is improved. Strict product liability is the other strategy, and in years past courts tended to not see software as a product because it is intangible, but that view is shifting, with courts in recent social media lawsuits seeing social media as a product and concluding that strict liability was applicable, and Character.AI's recent bankruptcy filing came in part because of a lawsuit in which the court treated the software as a product. Design defects is the part of the doctrine gaining traction, where a plaintiff shows that the product posed a foreseeable risk to someone using it, and so far the doctrine has worked when applied to the lack of guardrails in chatbots.

The author writes that AI software by its nature is constantly learning and therefore changing, making it impossible for a company to promise that it will absolutely behave a certain way, and in many cases the software is inherently incapable of supporting a guarantee about design safety. Still, according to a Brookings Institution report, strict liability is a way to hold the maker responsible even when those products evolve in ways not specifically desired or foreseeable by their manufacturers, and the author believes that if people are going to accept AI software as a boon to society, tough rules and sharp deterrents are needed. A strict liability system would shift risk from society to the companies seeking vast revenues, and the next steps will be sorting out whether to treat all or some AI software as a product and whether the technology is ultrahazardous. If it is treated as that dangerous, the author writes, AI can develop with incentives to reduce harms and ensure that people injured are compensated.

Articles.Title: ‘Strict liability’: The legal standard that could help rein in AI - The Conversation

stories.Headline: New AI platforms help global students and teachers practice and assess Chinese language skills
stories.Summary:
New AI-powered Chinese learning platforms were recently unveiled at the World Chinese Language Conference held in Beijing to support teachers and learners. These digital tools aim to standardize assessments and encourage more global students to practice speaking the language in their classrooms. The Yufei Smart Chinese Classroom connects lesson preparation and oral practice, and it has already been implemented in over 900 schools worldwide. These systems move the concept of artificial intelligence into actual classroom practice to help students find their voice.

The Yufei system was used in a Thai public school with 1,800 students, where 29 teachers manage 70 different classes. Over 330 days, students there generated 23,093 speaking practices and more than 65,000 pronunciation diagnostic records on the platform. In Myanmar, a school with 10,000 students used an AI oral evaluation system for levels 1 to 8 since May 2025. This specific school has held 2,127 oral exams and conducted more than 1.2 million evaluations to ensure scoring consistency. Additionally, the SureChinese 2.0 app from BlingABC now serves over 200,000 registered users and 40,000 monthly active users.

The SureChinese 2.0 platform offers 1,000 guide videos and 7,000 exercises across four HSK 3.0 levels while supporting 12 system languages. CEO Qiao Lei explained that the app evaluates accuracy and fluency while providing pronunciation guidance and automated learning reports. Xie Fei of iFLYTEK stated that the primary goal is to provide tools that do not increase the burdens placed on teachers. Principal Zhang Qiuyuan noted that AI handles repetitive scoring and initial screening, but human review remains necessary for abnormal results. Wang Zhanglong described a dual-teacher model where a virtual teacher leads while local teachers provide essential assistance.

The Yufei International Chinese Education Vertical Large Model was jointly released by iFLYTEK and the Center for Language Education and Cooperation. This model incorporates authoritative teaching materials to help teachers design exercises and explain complex language points more effectively. The technology is designed to provide a reliable content source rather than replacing the professional judgment of human educators. By using color marking to identify specific words, these tools offer targeted exercises for learners from various language backgrounds. These advancements continue to expand the reach of Chinese language education through integrated digital assessment and interactive learning.

Articles.Title: AI tools help global learners find their voice in Chinese - China Daily

stories.headline_source: AI tools help global learners find their voice in Chinese

stories.Headline: Tencent and the China-Britain Artificial Intelligence Association host AI collaboration event in London
stories.Summary:
More than one hundred artificial intelligence researchers and professionals gathered in London on Friday, November 13, 2026, to discuss the connection between academic study and industrial innovation. The China-Britain Artificial Intelligence Association and the Chinese technology giant Tencent hosted the event to foster deeper collaboration between the two nations. Speakers at the conference included representatives from the University College London, Oxford University, and various business units within Tencent. These experts focused on the intersection of cutting-edge research and the practical application of technology in the real world.

The event required a collaborative effort to highlight how the United Kingdom and China possess highly complementary strengths in the field of intelligence. Ding Mingqin, who serves as the minister counselor and head of the science and technology section at China's Embassy in the UK, emphasized the need for international cooperation on global governance. He noted that while the UK maintains a competitive edge in frontier research, China excels in engineering, advanced manufacturing, and large-scale industrial deployment. This synergy creates a solid foundation for future collaboration because China is currently one of the largest markets for AI applications.

Ding Mingqin stated that China remains consistently committed to strengthening international partnerships to ensure the responsible development of these powerful technologies. Richard Parnes, a senior director at Tencent Games, argued that artificial intelligence cannot replace human taste or the judgment that gives meaning to creative work. He compared the rise of AI to the introduction of spreadsheets, suggesting that technology makes talented creative teams unbeatable rather than replacing them entirely. Simon Stringer from the Oxford Centre for Theoretical Neuroscience and Artificial Intelligence and Professor Peter Latham from the Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit also shared their specialized research.

The participants engaged in a panel discussion where they shared diverse opinions on cross-border collaboration and the implementation of real-world innovation. They explored the complex connections between the human brain and large language models to better understand how artificial intelligence can evolve. By bridging the gap between academia and industry, the attendees hoped to accelerate the pace of technological breakthroughs through shared knowledge. The conference concluded with a collective agreement that human oversight remains essential for the meaningful application of these advanced digital tools.

Articles.Title: AI conference bridges academia and industry - China Daily

stories.headline_source: AI conference bridges academia and industry

stories.Headline: iQIYI returns to non-GAAP operating profit by using AI to increase efficiency
stories.Summary:
The online entertainment provider iQIYI reported its financial results for the third quarter of 2026 on November 17, 2026. The company achieved a return to non-GAAP operating profit by utilizing artificial intelligence to increase efficiency and implementing strict cost cuts. These strategic measures helped the firm offset the impact of a lighter content slate during the period. The company successfully narrowed its operating loss to 41.9 million yuan from 121.8 million yuan the previous year.

Revenues for the quarter fell ten percent year over year to 6.01 billion yuan, or 896.0 million dollars. Membership services revenue dropped six percent to 3.97 billion yuan, while content distribution and other revenues fell by 38 percent and 39 percent respectively. Online advertising grew three percent, and content costs decreased 13 percent to 3.52 billion yuan. The firm held 4.04 billion yuan in cash and short-term investments as of September 30, 2026, and spent 76.4 million dollars to repurchase 64.2 million ADSs.

Chief Executive Officer Gong Yu stated that the company maintained the top domestic market share for films, children's content, and long-form dramas. He noted that short-form dramas reached the top quarterly share for the first time under a new social media model. Chief Financial Officer Tian Ying explained that the company intends to improve investment efficiency through a larger portfolio of revenue-sharing content. Both executives highlighted that the integration of decentralization and artificial intelligence is producing encouraging early results for the business.

Articles.Title: iQIYI's AI-driven efficiency push pays off in Q3 - China Daily Global Edition

stories.headline_source: iQIYI's AI-driven efficiency push pays off in Q3

stories.Headline: UNESCO official urges AI to serve culture while preserving human meaning
stories.Summary:
Shahbaz Khan, the director of the UNESCO Regional Office for East Asia, spoke at a forum in Changsha, Hunan province, on Monday. This event was the 2026 International Youth Forum on Creativity and Heritage along the Silk Roads. He discussed how artificial intelligence can assist people in sharing stories about their heritage through innovative methods. However, he emphasized that only human beings can provide the actual meaning to these cultural narratives.

The use of AI requires a careful balance to ensure it serves culture without causing harm. It offers new possibilities for researching, documenting, transmitting, and raising awareness regarding living heritage. These tools must not extract cultural knowledge without consent or misrepresent the traditions of various groups. Furthermore, the technology should not treat heritage as mere data that is detached from the communities sustaining it.

Shahbaz Khan explained that while AI provides helpful tools, it also poses significant risks to cultural integrity. He argued that the technology must remain a servant to human creativity and community identity. The official stressed that the human element is essential for maintaining the authenticity of historical stories. He cautioned against the dangers of stripping cultural knowledge away from its original social context.

Articles.Title: Changsha forum: UNESCO official says AI should serve culture - China Daily

stories.headline_source: Changsha forum: UNESCO official says AI should serve culture

stories.Headline: Australian Capital Equity CEO identifies growth potential in China AI and manufacturing
stories.Summary:
Yizhou He, the managing director and China CEO of Australian Capital Equity, discussed investment opportunities during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO Summit 2026. This event took place on Tuesday and Wednesday in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, where he shared his views on the local economy. He explained that the combination of artificial intelligence and advanced manufacturing provides the most promising prospects for international investors. His company has already acquired equity stakes in several technology firms based in the city of Shenzhen.

He believes that the next five years must focus on growth quality by translating scientific advances into higher productivity and globally competitive businesses. This strategy requires prioritizing foundational technologies and infrastructure over standalone applications, as breakthroughs often demand years of patient capital. He evaluates frontier technologies based on their reliability, measurable value in real applications, and a credible path toward a scalable business model. He also highlighted the potential of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area to merge manufacturing strength with financial expertise and digital asset ecosystems.

Yizhou He stated that China's ability to turn innovation into industrial strength supports his confidence in the long-term economic outlook. He noted that core AI technologies and industrial applications reinforce each other, allowing innovations to reach production lines at a massive scale. Regarding international expansion, he suggested that headquarters should set clear governance expectations while giving local teams the authority to act. He also argued that closer cooperation on the mutual recognition of testing results and clearer regulatory guidance would make cross-border projects much smoother.

Articles.Title: Investor sees long-term growth potential in China‘s AI sector - China Daily Global Edition

stories.headline_source: Investor sees long-term growth potential in China‘s AI sector

stories.Headline: Armenia approves seven-year program to develop physical AI and robotics
stories.Summary:
Armenia has officially approved a comprehensive seven-year program to develop physical artificial intelligence, which focuses on robotics and intelligent systems. This strategic initiative was announced on November 17 and aims to train specialists who can compete on an international level. The program targets the creation of AI systems that can interact directly with the physical world through machines. Local media reports indicate that the government intends to build a strong foundation for future technological growth.

The project requires a collaborative effort through public-private partnerships and co-financing involving three major academic institutions. Yerevan State University, the National Polytechnic University of Armenia, and the American University of Armenia will all participate in the implementation. State funding for the initial phase is set at 1.684 billion drams, which is approximately 4.3 million U.S. dollars. These funds will primarily cover the salaries of researchers and the development of necessary infrastructure, while private investors are expected to provide more money.

The government has set specific goals for the seven-year period, including the training of about 330 graduates. They aim to secure around 10 major research grants and register at least one patented invention during this time. The program also plans to organize 12 scientific conferences and establish five new startups or spin-off companies. Additionally, the participating universities intend to publish about 20 papers in academic journals that are ranked internationally.

Those responsible for the program seek to develop specialized research teams at the participating universities to ensure long-term success. They believe that strengthening cooperation with international academic networks will be essential for the growth of physical AI. The initiative focuses on creating a sustainable ecosystem where academic research translates into practical, intelligent machines. By integrating public funding with private investment, Armenia hopes to establish itself as a hub for robotics and intelligent systems.

Articles.Title: Armenia launches 7-year program to develop physical AI - Xinhua

stories.headline_source: Armenia launches 7-year program to develop physical AI - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Xinhua Institute report says AI reshapes global information ecosystem and communication power balance
stories.Summary:
A Chinese think tank has reported that artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping the global information ecosystem and the balance of power in communication, bringing both new opportunities and new challenges. The report, titled "AI Plus Media: Global Development Report 2026," was compiled by the Xinhua Institute and released during the 7th World Media Summit in Beijing. It was published on November 11, 2026, and the summit itself ran from November 5 to 9 under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action." Nearly 500 representatives from almost 330 media outlets, think tanks and government bodies in 112 countries and regions attended, along with the United Nations and other international organizations.

According to the report, advances in generative technology are expanding the supply of content while also making it easier than ever to fabricate it. It describes several paradoxes in AI's effect on the industry. AI platforms are opening new routes to reach audiences, yet they weaken the direct link between news outlets and their readers. AI tools are raising production efficiency, but they also place new demands on the organizational abilities and professional standards of media organizations.

The report adds that the spread of the technology is helping more people while widening the AI divide between regions. The report calls on news media worldwide to act as enablers of technological inclusiveness, pioneers in digital ethics, co-builders of rules for applications, guardians of digital rights and interests, and bridge-builders for exchange and mutual learning. It argues that global news media should work together to build a new information and communication order that is trustworthy, fair and oriented toward the common good. The authors are the Xinhua Institute, which compiled the document.

The article does not give further statements from individual officials about the report. The World Media Summit was first held in 2009 and has since become a major global platform for media exchange and cooperation. The article presents the report as a contribution to that discussion rather than as a binding measure. It does not say what follow-up steps, if any, the report's recommendations will lead to.

Articles.Title: AI reshaping global media landscape, bringing opportunities and challenges: report - Xinhua

stories.headline_source: AI reshaping global media landscape, bringing opportunities and challenges: report - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Nvidia revenue grows 103 percent as AI infrastructure demand drives third quarter gains
stories.Summary:
The American chipmaker Nvidia reported a massive surge in third-quarter revenue for fiscal 2027 on November 17. The company earned 115.8 billion U.S. dollars, which represents a 103 percent increase from the previous year and a 20 percent rise from the last quarter. This growth was primarily driven by the ongoing global demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure. The firm also recorded a net income of 65.3 billion dollars for the period ending October 25, nearly doubling its profit from the same time last year.

The data center business generated 107.6 billion dollars, accounting for about 93 percent of total revenue and increasing 110 percent year on year. Financial metrics included a GAAP gross margin of 74.8 percent and GAAP diluted earnings per share of 2.70 dollars. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue to reach approximately 130 billion dollars for fiscal 2027. Additionally, Nvidia returned 28.1 billion dollars to shareholders through cash dividends and repurchased shares during the third quarter. The board previously approved a 150 billion dollar increase to share repurchases, leaving 227.3 billion dollars remaining in that authorization.

Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress is now responsible for the company after founder Jensen Huang stepped down from his role. Kress stated that the company's momentum is real and praised the relentless innovation of the staff. She noted that the Vera Rubin project has had an explosive start and that the company's roadmap remains on track. Kress further emphasized that the ambition of the technology leader has never been greater than it is now.

Nvidia will pay a quarterly cash dividend of 25 cents per share on December 23 to shareholders of record on December 2. This payment follows the strong financial performance reported in the first quarterly report since the change in leadership. The company continues to focus on expanding its AI infrastructure capabilities to maintain its position as a technology leader. Future growth depends on the successful execution of the current roadmap and the continued demand for high-end chips.

Articles.Title: Nvidia's Q3 revenue surges 103 pct as AI demand drives growth - Xinhua

stories.headline_source: Nvidia's Q3 revenue surges 103 pct as AI demand drives growth - Xinhua

stories.Headline: LinkedIn data shows Singapore firms with stronger AI capabilities record higher headcount growth across all sizes
stories.Summary:
LinkedIn released platform data on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, regarding Singaporean businesses. The data shows that firms with stronger artificial intelligence capabilities recorded higher headcount growth. This trend occurred across all company sizes during the study period. The findings were published by Ranamita Chakraborty for The Business Times. The data covers the period from September 2025 to September 2026.

AI enabled businesses are those where at least 5 per cent of employees have AI talent. Mid market enterprises with 201 to 1,000 employees saw the strongest growth. Small businesses have fewer than 201 employees, while enterprises have 1,001 to 5,000. Large enterprises are those with over 5,000 employees in the LinkedIn data. Singapore ranked second for mid market growth behind Germany at 3.5 per cent.

Chua Pei Ying is the LinkedIn head economist for the Asia Pacific region. She stated that AI frees up resources by automating routine tasks and improving productivity. This allows companies to focus on growth opportunities and make better decisions. She noted that hiring rates reflect new joins, while headcount growth measures net change. Chua said global economic uncertainty makes businesses more cautious about where they recruit.

Small businesses lag behind large enterprises in AI engineering and AI literacy skills. Only 12.5 per cent of small businesses have AI engineering skills versus 25.1 per cent. AI literacy is held by 3.3 per cent of small firms and 11.4 per cent. Mid market enterprises in Singapore grew by 7 per cent between 2025 and 2026. Small businesses grew by 6.7 per cent, but their average headcount rose 1.1 per cent.

Singapore mid market enterprises grew their average headcount by 2.3 per cent during the period. This was higher than the UK, Italy, Netherlands, UAE, Australia, France, US, and Brazil. Utilities companies had the largest AI advantage at 10 percentage points in Singapore. Real estate and equipment rental followed at 7.3, and transportation and logistics at 4.7. Singapore serves as a connected regional hub and a launch pad for growth.

Hiring declined year on year for mid market firms by 9.4 per cent in September 2026. Small businesses saw a 10.5 per cent fall, and large enterprises dropped by 11 per cent. Seasonal patterns show the strongest hiring in May and January and lowest in December and February. Small businesses can build momentum as AI engineering skills rose 3.5 percentage points annually. The data does not establish a causal relationship between AI adoption and workforce expansion.

Articles.Title: AI adoption raises headcount growth among Singapore firms of all sizes: LinkedIn - The Business Times

stories.headline_source: AI adoption raises headcount growth among Singapore firms of all sizes: LinkedIn

stories.Headline: Nvidia stops shipping licensed Hopper data centre chips to China
stories.Summary:
Nvidia stopped shipping licensed Hopper data centre chips to China on November 17, 2026, despite having previous United States government approval. This decision follows a period where the company sold 2.4 billion US dollars of these products to China during the third quarter. The shift occurs shortly after the Trump administration increased scrutiny on processor exports to various countries on November 16. This move marks a significant change for a company that previously fought for expanded business opportunities with Chinese customers.

The company will no longer include licensed Hopper data centre products, such as the H200 chips approved for 2025, in its future guidance. To manage growing pressure, Nvidia is establishing a new board committee specifically focused on export controls and national security. These changes follow the recent removal of CEO Jensen Huang, who had strongly advocated for selling advanced Blackwell chips to China. The current situation is further complicated by investigations into a woman with whom Huang had an affair and who may have aided Chinese spying.

Interim chief executive officer Colette Kress confirmed the end of these shipments during an earnings call but did not explain the specific reasoning. New board chair Harvey Jones stated that the company must acknowledge how national security dynamics are creating major changes in the global marketplace. He noted that the next leader of the company will have to navigate these difficult political waters with great care. The company now faces a landscape where the United States limits sales if buyers provide Chinese firms remote access to advanced servers.

Articles.Title: Nvidia stops selling AI chips to China despite US approval - The Straits Times

stories.headline_source: Nvidia stops selling AI chips to China despite US approval

stories.Headline: COP31 observers say AI data centre growth may raise fossil fuel use and strain power grids
stories.Summary:
Observers at the COP31 UN climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, said that the expansion of data centres to power the artificial intelligence boom could increase fossil fuel use, strain power grids and raise electricity prices for ordinary people. Turkey, which is hosting the conference, launched a pledge on November 16 for countries and companies to sign that urges them to seek the technology's potential in finding climate solutions while assessing its growing environmental risks. Turkey said the pledge received 80 endorsements but did not specify who had signed, and The Straits Times understands that Singapore has not signed it. The concerns were voiced as global superpowers remain locked in a race to dominate the emerging field, and some tech leaders such as Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei have separately called for an AI slowdown on oversight grounds.

The pledge and the debate sit alongside a Turkish presidency target for countries to agree at the conference on raising the share of electricity in global energy demand from 20 per cent currently to 35 per cent by 2035 through electrification. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said at the launch that AI offers both great potential and great peril for the battle against global warming, and that people cannot be asked to accept higher bills, more planet heating pollution and deeper inequality today in exchange for promises of a better tomorrow. He called on companies to align their business plans with climate goals and to power their data centres with renewable energy. Alex de Vries-Gao, a researcher at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam who studies the environmental impacts of digital infrastructure, told the paper that AI development should be slowed if its growth cannot be accommodated without increasing fossil fuel use or putting further pressure on grids, and that building data centres first and promising to address the consequences later is not a sustainable approach.

Xueying Wu, co-lead of the Global Big Tech campaign at Greenpeace, said unchecked expansion of AI data centres threatens to derail the global energy transition, noting that an International Energy Agency report showed global data centre electricity consumption will more than double by 2030. Philip Newell, who leads the COP31 Actual Intelligence Unit at the Climate Action Against Disinformation coalition, said data centre growth would not need to slow if tech companies committed to tapping more wind and solar power backed by batteries rather than relying on fossil fuels. Nidhi Upadhyaya of the Atlantic Council's Climate Resilience Center said consumers are already seeing the strain, and that the AI infrastructure construction boom and rising electricity bills were among the main concerns for voters in the November 3 US midterm elections that saw a Democratic victory in Congress. In South-east Asia, data centres currently consume more than 13 terawatt-hours of electricity, a figure the IEA expects to nearly triple by 2035 in a November 9 report, and that current total is equivalent to about a quarter of Singapore's electricity consumption in 2024.

Kirsten Dunlop, chief executive of the independent climate innovation agency Climate-KIC, said data centre expansion should slow down to allow developers to build more sustainable infrastructure. Upadhyaya said it will be critical to ensure that the cost of building data centres is borne by the companies setting them up rather than by consumers, and that grid capacity needs to be re-evaluated and infrastructure retrofitted, upgraded or rebuilt to be more resilient. She also called for guardrails governing where data centres are built, the impacts they will have on neighbourhoods and governance of how AI is used. Hikmat Soeriatanuwijaya of Oil Change International said that with growing resistance to data centres in the US, South-east Asia will need to assess the implications of investments in these areas, while Vries-Gao said governments need to consider who benefits, who pays for the additional infrastructure and what happens to local electricity and water supplies.

stories.Headline: CATL searches for an AI model to accelerate battery research and scientific discovery
stories.Summary:
CATL founder and CEO Zeng Yuqun announced the search for an AI Einstein during a panel discussion at the Apec CEO Summit 2026. This event began on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, in the city of Shenzhen. The company wants to find an artificial intelligence model that can accelerate scientific research and drive growth through innovation. This initiative comes as the Chinese battery giant deals with several market setbacks and headwinds.

The project requires a specialized AI model capable of working far beyond the current applications of existing technology. Zeng Yuqun questioned Robin Li Yanhong, who is the co-founder and CEO of the AI pioneer Baidu, about the capabilities of current large language models. The goal is to determine if these existing tools are good enough to drive the necessary breakthroughs. The company believes a more advanced system is needed to speed up the pace of scientific discovery.

Zeng Yuqun is responsible for leading this search to ensure the company maintains its competitive edge in the battery market. He explained that the company is actively seeking a tool that can function like a digital genius to solve complex problems. By integrating such a model, CATL hopes to overcome current obstacles and accelerate the development of new battery technologies. The company aims to move past standard AI uses to achieve significant scientific leaps.

Articles.Title: CATL seeks ‘AI Einstein’ to drive battery breakthroughs amid market headwinds - South China Morning Post

stories.headline_source: CATL seeks ‘AI Einstein’ to drive battery breakthroughs amid market headwinds

stories.Headline: Baidu and Xiaomi CEOs warn that AI investments are outpacing commercial returns
stories.Summary:
Robin Li Yanhong of Baidu and Lei Jun of Xiaomi issued warnings on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, regarding the current state of artificial intelligence. These leaders spoke during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO Summit held in the city of Shenzhen. They expressed significant concern that the massive investments flowing into the technology are far outpacing the actual commercial returns. This warning comes during a period of market jitters following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The tech leaders argued that the industry must shift its focus toward building practical applications rather than simply creating more powerful models.

They believe that the true value of artificial intelligence will be determined by how these tools are used in real-world scenarios. This shift is necessary because there is a widening gap between heavy capital expenditure and profitable adoption. Robin Li made these comments just one day after Baidu reported its sixth consecutive quarterly drop in revenue. Robin Li Yanhong stated that the most pressing task for the industry is to identify and develop high-value applications for AI models.

Both he and Lei Jun urged the tech community to prioritize utility over the hype surrounding the technology. They suggested that the current trajectory of spending could lead to an artificial intelligence bubble if returns do not materialize. The executives emphasized that the ability to generate profit depends on finding the right use cases for the existing models. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Baidu, Xiaomi CEOs warn of growing gap between AI hype and returns - South China Morning Post

stories.Headline: OECD study finds German media overreports autonomous vehicles and large language models in AI incident coverage
stories.Summary:
The OECD AI Policy Observatory published a paper on 17 November 2026 analysing live data from the OECD.AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor to compare how 15 thematic clusters of AI incidents and hazards appear in German-language media against global trends. The analysis found three themes overrepresented in German-language coverage, namely autonomous vehicles, intellectual property, and large language models. It found two themes underrepresented, namely synthetic media, and cyberattacks and fraud. Coverage of the remaining ten thematic clusters was broadly aligned with global media patterns. The paper says media reports of AI incidents and hazards can shape public perception and political debates, while both the level and thematic focus of media attention vary across regions.

The paper concludes that media representation of AI risks is shaped not only by the nature of AI incidents but also by language-specific and regional contexts. The OECD.AI platform says governments must track and understand AI incidents and hazards to manage risks, and that all actors must be accountable for AI risks. It also says organisations developing advanced AI systems can participate by submitting a report, and that sharing information will facilitate transparency and comparability of risk mitigation measures. The OECD.AI Index assesses countries' progress in implementing the OECD Recommendation on AI. The platform describes itself as an online interactive platform dedicated to promoting trustworthy, human-centric AI, and notes that the GPAI initiative and OECD member countries' work on AI joined forces under the GPAI brand to create an integrated partnership.

The articles do not name individual authors or officials and give no direct statements beyond the platform's general positions on accountability and risk tracking. They describe the OECD as both a regulator and investor in AI as well as a developer and user, and say experts from around the world advise GPAI and contribute to its work. The paper is available for download through the OECD.AI page, and the page invites readers to sign up for the OECD's artificial intelligence newsletter. The articles do not say what policy changes, if any, follow from the findings.

stories.Headline: Heo Seong-beom urges exam cheating countermeasures after AI scandal
stories.Summary:
Broadcaster Heo Seong-beom, a 26-year-old former AI researcher at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, posted a video titled "AI Was Not Made to Be Used This Way" on his YouTube channel on the 16th. In that video he said the top scorer on the Certified Public Accountant exam had admitted to cheating with a smart device, and he added that he was deeply distressed by it. He said it was painful that people who exploit AI had appeared before society had established guidelines for the technology. The video was reported by MoneyToday on 17 November 2026.

Heo Seong-beom said the biggest problem is that examinees who have studied hard are having their opportunities taken away by the minority who abuse the system. He argued it makes no sense to proceed with the CSAT as it is without any countermeasures, and he said various preventive measures must be established even if that is a bit troublesome. He cited metal detectors as an effective way to detect cheating, because cameras, communication equipment and earphones are needed to photograph questions, send them to AI and receive answers, so the response should involve detecting batteries. He said students suspected of cheating can be checked through USIM communication records and analysis of exam papers, since data exchanges leave records on the USIM and handwriting can show whether cheating occurred.

He warned those attempting to cheat that cheating will always be discovered and that if they catch them, they catch everyone. He told friends who decided to cheat because they thought they could get away with it this time that it is a matter that will ruin their lives, and he hoped they would not do it. To examinees who may feel confused, he said people like these bad actors have existed in every era, and he encouraged them not to worry and to go their own way even if they wonder why they should study in an era like this. Heo Seong-beom attended the Korea Science High School for the Gifted and the Department of Computer Science at KAIST, is currently enrolled in the AI Graduate School, and became known through CSAT explanation videos, lecturing and appearances on Coupang Play's "University War" and Wavve's "Blood Game 3."

stories.Headline: KAIST team develops KORMo-Web AI agent that operates websites for shopping and online tasks
stories.Summary:
A research team led by Professor Lim Kyung-taek at the KAIST Graduate School of Culture Technology developed an AI agent called KORMo-Web. On November 17, the team announced that this model can watch a computer screen like a human to operate a mouse and keyboard. The AI performs various online tasks on behalf of users, such as shopping, writing emails, and creating presentation materials. It can also engage with online communities by automatically writing comments on YouTube videos.

The system requires a massive dataset of over 10 million web screen samples in English and Korean to function. To handle multi-step tasks, the researchers used more than 100,000 records of real user interactions with various websites. A compact model with 4 billion parameters achieved a 42.3% success rate on real websites in both languages. This performance surpassed previous open models by 22.1 percentage points in Korean and 9.6 percentage points in English.

Professor Lim stated that the goal was to have AI understand screens directly rather than connecting separate application programming interfaces for every service. He explained that the team wants to create an environment where small AI installed on personal computers can handle diverse web tasks. To support this goal, the team released three different models, including an in-house version and a small version for personal computers. All program code, training data, and models are provided as open source for anyone to use.

stories.Headline: WAIC CONNECT HK organizes a city walk to explore Hong Kong AI industry sites
stories.Summary:
The WAIC CONNECT HK City Walk will take place in Hong Kong on December 9, 2026, to explore the local artificial intelligence industry. This one-day event is organized as an industrial docking section preceding the 2027 WAIC HONG KONG Global Launch Summit. The tour will visit three specific locations, starting with Amazon Web Services, then moving to The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, and ending at the Hong Kong Science Park. Participants will gather at 9:30 and are expected to finish the journey by 17:45.

The itinerary requires a small group of 50 to 70 people, and registration will close once these limited spots are filled. At Amazon Web Services, the focus will be on enterprise-level AI applications and the use of Amazon Bedrock for building digital businesses. The visit to the Hong Kong Generative AI R&D Center, which was established in October 2023 with InnoHK funding, will highlight localized large language models. Finally, the Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation will showcase its innovation ecosystem and support policies for enterprise growth.

The organizers designed this trip for AI founders, enterprise leaders, investment partners, and technical practitioners seeking pilot opportunities or business expansion. They stated that the walk allows guests to learn how AI products integrate into business operations and how scientific research finds practical applications. The goal is to facilitate connections between technology teams and real demands within the Hong Kong market. Participants are encouraged to bring specific problems regarding product development or business expansion to discuss with experts.

This event serves as a precursor to the 2027 WAIC HONG KONG Global Launch Summit, which will be held from December 10 to 11, 2026, at the Hong Kong Science Park. The summit aims to bring together AI technology teams and local application scenarios to foster industrial cooperation. Following the city walk, attendees will enter the main conference venue to continue their engagement with the AI ecosystem. The final visiting routes and demonstration content remain subject to the arrangements confirmed by the organizer.

stories.Headline: New graduates must please AI interviewers to pass 40 to 60 minute screening interviews
stories.Summary:
New graduates looking for jobs have found that AI interviewers are increasingly common in recruitment, and to land a job the first skill they must master is how to please the AI, according to a 36Kr article published on 17 November 2026. The campus recruitment season known as “Golden September and Silver October” had just passed, and November is when new graduates are busy with written assessments and interviews. In the past two years some small changes have clearly emerged in the recruitment market, and many new graduates have received AI interview invitations. In an AI interview an AI figure acts as the interviewer, grabs keywords to ask questions based on the job seeker’s self-introduction and answers, and the interview lasts mostly between 40 and 60 minutes. Job seekers have to search for tips and repeatedly tackle the digital human on the screen during the long job-hunting process.

Some enterprises use an Applicant Tracking System to assist AI in screening resumes during initial screening, whose essence is to match content with keywords. Job seekers upload a manually written resume and the job responsibilities or required skills to AI and give detailed modification instructions, including extracting keywords from the job description and placing them in the first 1/3 area of the resume. They are told to use more verbs that describe achievements and include quantifiable data, such as “improving efficiency by 30%” and “reducing cost by 20%”. After the online application and personal information, job seekers receive links to online assessment and personality test pages, and after hundreds of questions they get a notice that the AI interview must be completed within 48 hours. Many enterprises use AI interview systems such as Beisen, Zhaopin, Liepin and Niuke, and questions of different enterprises likely come from the same question bank.

Human resources managers with working experience in large factories share online that after campus recruitment opens one position can receive hundreds of resumes, and opening each one takes too much time while a filter is not flexible enough. When HR uses AI to screen resumes they only need to provide the description of job content, and the AI automatically decomposes the job requirements and filters and recommends suitable candidates in the resume database. Student M, who participated in many AI interviews this year, complained of annoying bugs such as ASR errors, the system prompting that you are not looking at the camera when you are clearly looking at it, and the system starting the next question before you finish answering. Job seekers must ask AI to remove the AI-generated flavor in the resume to avoid being considered machine-generated by HR.

They must also behave as if communicating with a real interviewer even when the other party does not respond at all. In the interview, two or three expressionless faces appear on the screen and often repeat “I want to hear you talk about it in detail” and “Please elaborate on it specifically”. Each answer is best to last about four and a half minutes, while a self-introduction in offline interviews is generally controlled within two minutes. Job seekers have learned to use the STAR framework to tell their internship experience, from the task background and specific work to the final results.

The AI interviewer grabs keywords from answers to ask questions but cannot fully understand the content, so in most cases it only mechanically asks follow-up questions or digs into the most trivial details. Job seekers apply to multiple enterprises at the same time during the campus recruitment season, and in the end they cannot even see the shadow of a real interviewer. An interview lasts for 40 minutes, but apart from asking questions the AI hardly makes any feedback comments, and job seekers can only talk to themselves to the fake figure. After they submit the answer, a standard greeting pops up on the screen: “Thank you for participating in this interview”.

Job seekers worry about failing to pass the AI screening because they are not careful enough in word selection, where before they worried about being rejected by HR due to insufficient experience. To deal with routine questions they deliberately fabricate experiences and exaggerate tense atmosphere to reflect calm under pressure, which makes many feel that this is not the real self. Asking a living person to cater to the preferences of the algorithm is itself a counterintuitive solution. More to follow.

stories.Headline: JD.com launches Aidol Creation Camp to incubate AI hardware startups
stories.Summary:
JD.com launched the Aidol Creation Camp to incubate new AI hardware companies. In October, twenty nine teams gathered in Yizhuang, Beijing, for a second season event. These participants faced a challenge to turn AI ideas into finished works. The event featured a forty eight hour extreme creation show for developers. This initiative aims to connect creative development with manufacturing and market sales.

The program now includes four tracks called AI applications, AI ideas, AI native devices, and AI device interconnection. HEYGO spent forty two hours connecting a ski wearable to a chest screen. Jiangying created an AI handheld console that builds DIY computer solutions in three and a half minutes. Zhimengke launched an AI sleep mat on JD.com in July 2026. This specific product earned over one million yuan in sales on its first day.

The project leader told 36Kr that they examine product differentiation and supply chain capability. They also look at the development space of the track and future sales potential. The leader noted that the industry now focuses more on user activity and retention rates. Regarding Zhimengke, the leader explained the different consumption logics for smart home versus digital products. This guidance helped the team target consumers with sleep management needs.

Chen Tongxin of Jiangying described how acrylic covers scratched easily, requiring a switch to glass. This change caused new problems because glass components interfered with the RF signal of the device. HEYGO struggled with sensor performance under low temperatures and sports impacts in real ski resorts. These startups face hurdles with product consistency, after sales service, and inventory management. Many products, like the Mooza noise canceling mask, now face tests through crowdfunding.

JD.com has explored consumer demand paths for more than ten years. In 2016, the notebook business began using in depth interviews to study user needs. This led to reverse customization cooperation with brands including Lenovo, HP, and Dell. The company officially established its C2M platform in 2019 to develop hit notebooks. They are now applying this industrial chain experience to younger AI startup teams.

The Mooza mask exceeded one thousand units in crowdfunding within three days. Jiangying reached over one hundred fifty percent of its crowdfunding target by November 9. The program seeks to move AI ideas from technical prototypes to full commercialization. It remains to be seen what new possibilities JD.com can bring to these startups. The articles leave open how these small teams will maintain long term business viability.

stories.Headline: MachinePulse releases open-source Karpo Decision 31B and takes first place on the Decision Index
stories.Summary:
The open-source decision-making model Karpo Decision 31B, from the Karpo Decision family, was released by MachinePulse and took the top spot on the Decision Index overall ranking, where 300 models compete, according to 36Kr on 2026-11-17. The full-size Karpo Decision family from 0.8B to 31B was fully open-sourced, with the 31B flagship winning first place worldwide. Karpo defeated Google's closed-source flagship Gemini Decision 1 head-on in multiple evaluations, the article said. The model was post-trained based on Google's own open-source base model Gemma 4 31B. Google CEO Sundar Pichai had personally launched Gemini Decision 1 a couple of days earlier.

The 31B flagship has a median single-card latency as low as 94 milliseconds, a calibration error of only 0.023, and can evaluate up to 255 options simultaneously for a single question. On the Decision Index overall ranking Karpo took first place with a score of 73.9, far exceeding the 60.2 points of the first-generation benchmark Jev 1.14, whose median latency is 196 milliseconds. Decision Index covers 37 public benchmarks and undisclosed private question banks, and JevBench is a full offline blind test run by an independent organization on its own graphics cards, with 1200 of 1500 examination questions permanently sealed. In the private blind test the top 10 public-list models dropped an average of 6.8 points, while Karpo lost only 4.3 points and scored 78.6 points on private questions in completely new fields. Karpo scored 90.4% on When2Call against Google's 79.9%, 90.0% on Mind2Web against 86.2%, 90.5% on the New Yorker cartoon caption test against 79.7%, and 64.7% on Amazon ESCI against 58.7%.

On 37 public benchmarks of Decision Index Karpo scored 75.0 points against Google's 60.9, and it won across the unfamiliar domains (72.3%), knowledge accuracy (56.0%) and safety judgment (93.4%) dimensions, leaving open-source opponents KnowLine, GLiDE and Sieve far behind. In the 1500-question JevBench offline blind test Karpo scored 89.53 points, 85.67 points on the 1200 sealed private questions against 80.45 on public questions, and a calibration score of 96.00. Converted to the list's unified scale, Karpo broke into the top three among 261 open-source models with a converted capability score of 87.2 points. Google's total comprehensive score was 77.4, decision-making intelligence 80.2 and calibration 94.1, and the article said all three core indicators were superior for Karpo. Karpo's cost per thousand decisions is only 0.025 US dollars, meaning 1 US dollar buys 40,000 judgments.

MachinePulse applied the same training recipe to five small and medium-sized models from 0.8B to 12B, and every parameter size entered the first echelon of its level, the article said. Karpo generates no text at all and runs one forward inference to calculate the probability of all options in milliseconds, unlike traditional large models that generate analyses token by token. In the "City Scanner" challenge, with settings of tonight, 2 people, within 50 USD per capita, within 5 kilometers and available for chatting, Karpo finished all 36 questions in 1.12 seconds. It picked out 10 matches, 23 eliminations and 3 insufficient information entries, 100% consistent with the rules for all 36 questions, while the general large model Gemini 3.5 Flash was still running after more than 5 seconds. In the "10 Appetites, 1 Menu" challenge, 10 customers each had their own calorie limit, budget, allergens and taste preferences, and manual ordering on the left violated two dietary restrictions after 5 seconds.

The article said Anthropic, which is about to list, disclosed a huge computing power gap in its IPO materials, pouring cold water on an industry frantically expanding model parameters. It said long chain reasoning consumes more tokens than text generation, and browser operation costs an average single cost 4.8 times higher than complex reasoning. The first-generation benchmark Jev pioneered the fast-thinking track of "no writing, only judgment", and giants including OpenAI, Microsoft, Amazon and Cloudflare entered the market one after another. Karpo reached the top of the overall ranking immediately after open-sourcing, and on JevBench the two sides tied at 92.2% on the public set before the gap appeared in the real Agent test field. The article said the most fiercely competitive new track in Silicon Valley had just seen the rise of a brand new open-source king.

The article's account of the "10 Appetites, 1 Menu" challenge was cut off mid-sentence, so the outcome of that test is not stated. The article did not say when the Karpo models would be available for download or use, or under what license they were released. It gave no date for the Gemini Decision 1 launch beyond "a couple of days ago", and no details of MachinePulse beyond its name. The article did not state how the Decision Index or JevBench rankings are weighted, or who maintains the Decision Index. It also did not say what Anthropic's disclosed computing power gap amounted to in figures.
